13.3.3.a.s: audumbaryāṃ srucyupastīrya yāvatī dyāvāpṛthivī iti dadhi gṛhītvābhighārya vākca tvā manaśca śrīṇītāṃ prāṇaśca tvāpānaśca śrīṇītāṃ cakṣuśca tvā śrotraṃ ca śrīṇītāṃ dakṣaśca tvā balaṃ ca śrīṇītāmojaśca tvā sahaśca śrīṇītāmāyuśca tvā jarā ca śrīṇītāmātmā ca tvā tanūśca śrīṇītāṃ śṛto 'si śṛtaṃkṛtaḥ śṛtāya tvā śṛtebhyastvetyāgnīdhrīye 'dhiśrityāha hotarvadasva yatte vādyamiti
13.3.3.a.d: औदुम्बर्यां स्रुच्युपस्तीर्य यावती द्यावापृथिवी इति दधि गृहीत्वाभिघार्य वाक्च त्वा मनश्च श्रीणीतां प्राणश्च त्वापानश्च श्रीणीतां चक्षुश्च त्वा श्रोत्रं च श्रीणीतां दक्षश्च त्वा बलं च श्रीणीतामोजश्च त्वा सहश्च श्रीणीतामायुश्च त्वा जरा च श्रीणीतामात्मा च त्वा तनूश्च श्रीणीतां शृतो ऽसि शृतंकृतः शृताय त्वा शृतेभ्यस्त्वेत्याग्नीध्रीये ऽधिश्रित्याह होतर्वदस्व यत्ते वाद्यमिति
13.3.3.a.m: Having made an under-layer of ghee in an udumbara ladle, having taken the curd with [the mantra]: 'As great as are heaven and earth...', having basted it with ghee, having placed it on the āgnīdhrīya fire with: 'May speech and mind mix thee; may in-breath and out-breath mix thee; may sight and hearing mix thee; may skill and strength mix thee; may power and might mix thee; may life-span and old age mix thee; may self and body mix thee; thou art cooked, made cooked; for the cooked to thee, for the cooked to thee!', he says: 'Hotṛ, speak what is to be spoken by thee!'

13.3.4.a.s: yadāsya vijānāti yadi śrāto juhotana yadyaśrāto mamattanetyetasminkāle śrātaṃ haviriti pratyuktvā tamādāyāhavanīyaṃ gatvāśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyati
13.3.4.a.d: यदास्य विजानाति यदि श्रातो जुहोतन यद्यश्रातो ममत्तनेत्येतस्मिन्काले श्रातं हविरिति प्रत्युक्त्वा तमादायाहवनीयं गत्वाश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यति
13.3.4.a.m: When he understands from him [the verse ending]: 'If it is cooked, make the offering; if it is not cooked, revel!', having answered at that time: 'Cooked is the oblation!', having taken it, having gone to the āhavanīya fire, having called for attention, when the call for attention has been responded to, he gives the ritual call:

13.4.1.a.m: 'Recite the consecratory verse for the warm curd-offering!'

13.4.2.a.m: 'Him whom they call Indra, whom they call Varuṇa, whom they call Mitra, and whom they call Truth,

13.4.2.b.s: yo devānāṃ devatamastapojāstasmā indrāya sutamājuhomi svāheti vaṣaṭkṛte juhoti /
13.4.2.b.d: यो देवानां देवतमस्तपोजास्तस्मा इन्द्राय सुतमाजुहोमि स्वाहेति वषट्कृते जुहोति ।
13.4.2.b.m: Who is the most divine of the gods, born of tapas—to that Indra I offer the pressed [soma], svāhā!'—with this he offers when the vaṣaṭ-call has been uttered.

13.4.2.c.m: Having offered when the secondary vaṣaṭ-call 'Svāhā vaṭ to Indra' has been made, he takes the portion for partaking.

13.4.3.a.m: Those partake of it who [perform] the Pravargya.

13.4.4.a.m: Its mantra for partaking is the one recited in the forest.

13.4.5.a.m: Another [view is]: It should not be [performed] in a sacrifice without a Pravargya.

13.4.6.a.s: mitro janānpra sa mitreti bhakṣayitvā nābhideśānabhimṛśante
13.4.6.a.d: मित्रो जनान्प्र स मित्रेति भक्षयित्वा नाभिदेशानभिमृशन्ते
13.4.6.a.m: Having partaken with 'Mitra [directs] the people...' and 'May that Mitra...', they touch the navel region.

13.4.7.a.m: The procedure for the animal cake oblations has been explained.

13.4.8.b.m: He modifies the beginning of the ritual call as: 'For Indra of the midday pressing, of the sacrificial cakes...'

13.4.9.a.d: होत्र इडां हृत्वा हविर्धानं गच्छन्संप्रेष्यत्युन्नीयमानेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहीति
13.4.9.a.m: Having brought the iḍā to the hotṛ, while going to the havirdhāna shed, he gives the ritual call: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for those being drawn out!'

13.4.10.a.m: From the drawing out up to the setting down of the Nārāśaṃsa goblets [the procedure is the same].

13.4.12.a.m: He draws out the acchāvāka's goblet as the tenth.

13.4.13.a.m: Having called for attention, when the call for attention has been responded to, he gives the ritual call:

13.4.14.a.s: mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya niṣkevalyasya bhāgasya śukravato manthivato madhuścuta indrāya somāniti saṃpraiṣādiḥ
13.4.14.a.d: माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य निष्केवल्यस्य भागस्य शुक्रवतो मन्थिवतो मधुश्चुत इन्द्राय सोमानिति संप्रैषादिः
13.4.14.a.m: The beginning of the ritual call is: 'Of the midday pressing, of the exclusive share, containing śukra, containing manthin, dripping honey, for Indra, the somas...'

13.4.16.a.m: They proceed with the acchāvāka's goblet before the āgnīdhra's goblet.

13.4.17.a.m: These very hotra-priests are present at the third pressing.

13.5.1.a.m: When the Nārāśaṃsa goblets are set down, he gives the sacrificial gifts.

13.5.1.b.s: bahvaparimitaṃ saptaikaviṃśatiḥ ṣaṣṭiḥ śataṃ dvādaśaśataṃ sahasraṃ sarvavedasaṃ vā
13.5.1.b.d: बह्वपरिमितं सप्तैकविंशतिः षष्टिः शतं द्वादशशतं सहस्रं सर्ववेदसं वा
13.5.1.b.m: Much, unlimited: seven, twenty-one, sixty, one hundred, one hundred and twelve, one thousand, or the entire property.

13.5.2.a.m: Or having given a share to the eldest son, he gives the entire property.

13.5.3.a.m: At a sacrifice of a thousand [cows] and at one of entire property, he gives a mule.

13.5.4.a.s: aviṃ dadātyajāṃ gāmaśvaṃ puruṣaṃ hastinaṃ vāso 'no rathamodanaṃ manthaṃ māṣāṃstilānvrīhiyavāngardabhamityadhikānyaniyatāni
13.5.4.a.d: अविं ददात्यजां गामश्वं पुरुषं हस्तिनं वासो ऽनो रथमोदनं मन्थं माषांस्तिलान्व्रीहियवान्गर्दभमित्यधिकान्यनियतानि
13.5.4.a.m: He gives a sheep, a female goat, a cow, a horse, a human, an elephant, a garment, a cart, a chariot, boiled rice, a flour drink, black grams, sesame seeds, rice, barley, a donkey—these are optional additions.

13.5.6.a.s: dakṣiṇena vedimavasthitāsu dakṣiṇāsūttareṇa havirdhānaṃ gatvottareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parītya pūrvayā dvārā prāgvaṃśaṃ praviśyātra yajamānasyāmātyānāṃ saṃhvayanādyā srugdaṇḍopaniyamanātkṛtvā pracarṇyā dakṣiṇāni juhoti
13.5.6.a.d: दक्षिणेन वेदिमवस्थितासु दक्षिणासूत्तरेण हविर्धानं गत्वोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं धिष्णियं परीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा प्राग्वंशं प्रविश्यात्र यजमानस्यामात्यानां संह्वयनाद्या स्रुग्दण्डोपनियमनात्कृत्वा प्रचर्ण्या दक्षिणानि जुहोति
13.5.6.a.m: While the sacrificial gifts are stationed to the south of the altar ground, having gone north of the havirdhāna shed, having gone around north of the āgnīdhra hearth, having entered the hall with east-facing beams by the east door, having performed the rites here from summoning the sacrificer's dependents up to fastening the ladle handle, he offers the dakṣiṇā oblations with the pracaraṇī ladle.

13.5.7.a.s: hiraṇyaṃ prabadhya ghṛte 'vadhāyodu tyaṃ citramiti dvābhyāṃ gārhapatye juhoti
13.5.7.a.d: हिरण्यं प्रबध्य घृते ऽवधायोदु त्यं चित्रमिति द्वाभ्यां गार्हपत्ये जुहोति
13.5.7.a.m: Having tied a piece of gold and placed it in ghee, he offers into the gārhapatya fire with two verses: 'Up that [all-knowing god]...' and 'The bright [face of the gods]...'

13.5.8.a.s: divaṃ gaccha suvaḥ pateti hiraṇyaṃ hutvodgṛhṇāti
13.5.8.a.d: दिवं गच्छ सुवः पतेति हिरण्यं हुत्वोद्गृह्णाति
13.5.8.a.m: Having offered, he takes up the gold with: 'Go to heaven, fly to the light!'

13.5.9.a.s: ubhayaṃ dhārayamaṇo rūpeṇa vo rūpamabhyaimīti dakṣiṇā abhyaiti
13.5.9.a.d: उभयं धारयमणो रूपेण वो रूपमभ्यैमीति दक्षिणा अभ्यैति
13.5.9.a.m: Holding both, he approaches the sacrificial gifts with: 'With form I approach your form!'

13.5.10.a.m: Some teachers prescribe the distribution after leading them across.

13.5.11.a.s: tutho vo viśvavedā vibhajatviti tā yajamānaścaturdhā kṛṣṇājinena vyuttrāsya caturthamadhvaryubhyo vibhajati
13.5.11.a.d: तुथो वो विश्ववेदा विभजत्विति ता यजमानश्चतुर्धा कृष्णाजिनेन व्युत्त्रास्य चतुर्थमध्वर्युभ्यो विभजति
13.5.11.a.m: With 'May Tutha, all-knower, distribute you!', the sacrificer, having divided them into four parts by frightening them off with a black antelope skin, divides one-fourth among the adhvaryus.

13.5.12.a.s: yāvadadhvaryave dadāti tasyārdhaṃ pratiprasthātre tṛtīyaṃ neṣṭre caturthamunnetre
13.5.12.a.d: यावदध्वर्यवे ददाति तस्यार्धं प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे तृतीयं नेष्ट्रे चतुर्थमुन्नेत्रे
13.5.12.a.m: As much as he gives to the adhvaryu, half of that to the pratiprasthātṛ, a third to the neṣṭṛ, a fourth to the unnetṛ.

13.5.13.a.m: By this the giving to the others has been explained.

13.6.1.a.m: He gives gold, a full dish, a cushion, and an entirely threaded cloth first to the agnīdh.

13.6.3.a.m: He should give to the brahman in such a way that he does not covet any other sacrificial gift.

13.6.4.a.s: aṅgāni dattvā tentena yathāliṅgaṃ niṣkrīṇīte yaddāsyansyāt
13.6.4.a.d: अङ्गानि दत्त्वा तेन्तेन यथालिङ्गं निष्क्रीणीते यद्दास्यन्स्यात्
13.6.4.a.m: Having given the limbs, he redeems whatever he would give by that [gift], in accordance with the characteristic marks [in the mantras]:

13.6.5.a.s: hotarvācaṃ te dadāmi tāṃ te 'nena niṣkrīṇāmīti
13.6.5.a.d: होतर्वाचं ते ददामि तां ते ऽनेन निष्क्रीणामीति
13.6.5.a.m: 'O hotṛ, I give thee speech; with this I redeem it from thee!'

13.6.6.f.m: Body hairs to the participants in the procession;

13.6.7.a.m: [These are given] outside of the regular sacrificial gifts for the camasādhvaryus, the participants in the procession, and the sadasya.

13.6.8.a.m: With gold in his hand, he leads [the cows] in front of the gārhapatya fire and behind the sadas.

13.6.8.b.m: Between the āgnīdhra hearth and the sadas, he releases them facing north obliquely.

13.6.9.a.m: The leading across of the sacrificial gifts is accompanied by: 'This is thy gift, O Agni!'

13.6.10.a.m: Just so, whether [the priests] are touching in line or not touching, he makes an offering into the āgnīdhrīya fire with: 'O Agni, lead [us]!'

13.6.11.a.s: vaneṣu vyantarikṣaṃ tatāneti dvitīyāṃ yadyano ratho vāso 'dhīvāso vā dīyate yadi vā dāsyansyāt /
13.6.11.a.d: वनेषु व्यन्तरिक्षं ततानेति द्वितीयां यद्यनो रथो वासो ऽधीवासो वा दीयते यदि वा दास्यन्स्यात् ।
13.6.11.a.m: He offers the second [oblation] with 'He stretched out the intermediate space in the woods...' if a cart, a chariot, a cloth, or an outer garment is given, or if he is going to give one.

13.6.11.b.s: prajāpate na tvadetānīti tṛtīyāṃ yadi puruṣo hastī vā dīyate yadi vā dāsyansyāt
13.6.11.b.d: प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति तृतीयां यदि पुरुषो हस्ती वा दीयते यदि वा दास्यन्स्यात्
13.6.11.b.m: He offers the third with 'O Prajāpati, none other than thou [encompasseth all these]...' if a human or an elephant is given, or if he is going to give one.

13.6.12.a.m: With 'May I satisfy the brāhmaṇa today!', he gives gold first to an Ātreya;

13.6.13.a.m: In the absence of that [person], he should give it to one who has the ṛṣi-lineage and is closely related.

13.6.14.a.s: asmaddātrā devatrā gaccateti nītā anumantraya sada etya vi suvaḥ paśyetyanuvīkṣate yadyatinīya vibhajet
13.6.14.a.d: अस्मद्दात्रा देवत्रा गच्चतेति नीता अनुमन्त्रय सद एत्य वि सुवः पश्येत्यनुवीक्षते यद्यतिनीय विभजेत्
13.6.14.a.m: He addresses [the gifts] as they are led away with: 'Go to the gods with us as givers.' Having gone to the sadas, he looks after them with: 'Behold heaven,' if he divides them having led them beyond.

13.6.15.a.m: He should give to the priests seated inside the sadas;

13.6.15.b.m: in the havirdhāna [shed] to the adhvaryus.

13.6.17.a.s: yaṃ yajñam āgacchet taṃ prasarped iti prasarpakāṇāṃ vijñāyate
13.6.17.a.d: यं यज्ञम् आगच्छेत् तं प्रसर्पेद् इति प्रसर्पकाणां विज्ञायते
13.6.17.a.m: 'To whichever sacrifice one might come, to that one should creep'—thus it is known [in the Brāhmaṇa] regarding those who creep up.

13.7.1.a.m: He gives to those who have crept up, seated to the south of the sadas.

13.7.7.a.m: Even to a Brahmin, if he is unlearned, it should not be given.

13.7.7.b.m: He may even give to a non-Brahmin who knows the sacred knowledge.

13.7.7.c.s: yāṃ sa vidyāṃ veda tāṃ tayāvarunddhe
13.7.7.c.d: यां स विद्यां वेद तां तयावरुन्द्धे
13.7.7.c.m: Whatever knowledge he knows, that he secures through that [gift].

13.7.8.a.s: yāṃ śrotriyāya jñātaye vānṛtvije prasṛptāya yāṃ sa vidyāṃ veda tāṃ tayāvarunddhe
13.7.8.a.d: यां श्रोत्रियाय ज्ञातये वानृत्विजे प्रसृप्ताय यां स विद्यां वेद तां तयावरुन्द्धे
13.7.8.a.m: Whatever [knowledge] a learned Vedic scholar or a relative who is not an officiating priest has, having crept up—whatever knowledge he knows, that he secures through that [gift].

13.7.9.a.s: yāṃ jyeṣṭhāya yayā sa devatayā jyaiṣṭhyaṃ gacchati tāṃ tayāvarunddhe
13.7.9.a.d: यां ज्येष्ठाय यया स देवतया ज्यैष्ठ्यं गच्छति तां तयावरुन्द्धे
13.7.9.a.m: Whatever [gift] to an elder—through whichever deity he attains seniority, that [deity] he secures through that [gift].

13.7.10.a.m: Whatever [gift] to a learned man of ṛṣi-lineage—through that he attains the heavenly world.

13.7.11.a.s: yāmanyo dīyamānāṃ na kāmayeta yaṃ dviṣyāttasmai dadyātsahānyena dhanena
13.7.11.a.d: यामन्यो दीयमानां न कामयेत यं द्विष्यात्तस्मै दद्यात्सहान्येन धनेन
13.7.11.a.m: Whichever [gift] another would not desire when being given, he should give to him whom he hates, along with other wealth.

13.7.13.a.s: atpratinuttāṃ dakṣiṇāṃ goṣu cārayetprati vā gṛhṇīyātsalāvṛkyenaṃ bhūtvā pravlinīyāt
13.7.13.a.d: अत्प्रतिनुत्तां दक्षिणां गोषु चारयेत्प्रति वा गृह्णीयात्सलावृक्येनं भूत्वा प्रव्लिनीयात्
13.7.13.a.m: If one should cause a rejected sacrificial gift to move among the cows or accept it, having become a she-hyena, it would crush him.

13.7.14.a.d: यामदानीयाय दक्षिणां ददाति तामस्य पशवो ऽन्वपक्रामन्ति ।
13.7.14.a.m: Whatever sacrificial gift he gives to an unworthy recipient, his cattle depart after it.

13.7.14.b.s: yadi manyetādānīyāyādāmiti na ma idamupadambhiṣagityetadyajurjapedgāṃ vā dadyādbrāhmaṇāya
13.7.14.b.d: यदि मन्येतादानीयायादामिति न म इदमुपदम्भिषगित्येतद्यजुर्जपेद्गां वा दद्याद्ब्राह्मणाय
13.7.14.b.m: If he should think, 'I have given to an unworthy recipient,' he should murmur this yajus: 'This is not my defeat, but a cure,' or he should give a cow to a Brahmin.

13.7.15.a.m: When the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, he should give [it], and they should accept.

13.7.16.a.s: nītāsu dakṣiṇāsu cātvāle kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāṃ prāsyati hariṇasya raghuṣyato 'dhi śīrṣaṇi bheṣajam /
13.7.16.a.d: नीतासु दक्षिणासु चात्वाले कृष्णविषाणां प्रास्यति हरिणस्य रघुष्यतो ऽधि शीर्षणि भेषजम् ।
13.7.16.a.m: When the sacrificial gifts have been led away, he throws the blackbuck horn into the pit (cātvāla) with: 'On the head of the swift-running deer is a medicine;

13.7.16.b.m: he, with his horn, destroyed the inherited disease, driving it away in all directions.'

13.7.16.c.m: 'The blackbuck antelope has stepped after you with four feet;

13.7.16.d.s: viṣāṇe viṣyaitaṃ granthiṃ yadasya gulphitaṃ hṛdi mano yadasya gulphitamityetābhyām
13.7.16.d.d: विषाणे विष्यैतं ग्रन्थिं यदस्य गुल्फितं हृदि मनो यदस्य गुल्फितमित्येताभ्याम्
13.7.16.d.m: O horn, untie this knot which is coiled in his heart, the mind which is coiled in him'—with these two [verses].

13.7.17.a.m: Having offered five Vaiśvakarmaṇa oblations in the āgnīdhrīya fire with: 'The ṛṣis blamed the lord of sacrifice with sin,'

13.8.1.a.m: they two proceed with the two Marutvatīya [draughts].

13.8.2.a.s: indrāya marutvate 'nubrūhīndrāya marutvate preṣyeti saṃpraiṣausānuvaṣaṭkārāvananuvaṣaṭkārau vā /
13.8.2.a.d: इन्द्राय मरुत्वते ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्राय मरुत्वते प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौसानुवषट्कारावननुवषट्कारौ वा ।
13.8.2.a.m: The ritual calls are: 'Recite for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,' and 'Prompt for Indra accompanied by the Maruts,' either with secondary vaṣaṭ-calls or without secondary vaṣaṭ-calls;

13.8.2.b.m: or one of the two is with a secondary vaṣaṭ-call.

13.8.2.c.m: Having poured down the residues of the draught as in the case of the two-deity draughts, the adhvaryu draws the third Marutvatīya draught with the unconsumed cup.

13.8.2.d.m: The drawing and settling mantras are: 'Indra accompanied by the Maruts...'

13.8.2.e.m: The pratiprasthātṛ brings the portion for consumption.

13.8.2.f.m: Both adhvaryus consume it in turn.

13.8.3.a.m: Taking this cup, the recitation and response, and the draughts and nārāśaṃsa goblets, are as in the case of the Aindrāgna [draught].

13.8.4.a.m: He draws the Māhendra draught with the Śukra cup.

13.8.4.b.m: The drawing and settling mantras are: 'Great Indra, who by his might...'

13.8.5.a.m: He introduces the chant of the Māhendra draught.

13.8.6.a.m: When it has been chanted, the recitation and response, and the draughts and nārāśaṃsa goblets, are as in the case of the Vaiśvadeva [recitation].

13.8.7.a.m: After the Māhendra draught, the atigrāhya draughts are offered.

13.8.8.a.m: Along with the adhvaryu, the pratiprasthātṛ takes the draught for Agni;

13.8.9.a.m: The pratiprasthātṛ, having offered the draught for Agni with: 'O Agni, full of splendour...', addresses it with: 'You are the finder of splendour.'

13.8.9.b.m: The neṣṭṛ, having offered the draught for Indra with: 'O Indra, full of vigour...', addresses it with: 'You are the finder of vigour.'

13.8.9.c.m: The unnetṛ, having offered the draught for Sūrya with: 'O Sūrya, full of brilliance...', addresses it with: 'You are the finder of heaven.'

13.8.10.a.s: tānhutvā sadasi pratyaṅmukhā bhakṣayanti mayi medhāmityetaiḥ svamsvaṃ yathāliṅgam
13.8.10.a.d: तान्हुत्वा सदसि प्रत्यङ्मुखा भक्षयन्ति मयि मेधामित्येतैः स्वम्स्वं यथालिङ्गम्
13.8.10.a.m: Having offered them, they consume them facing west in the sadas, each his own according to its characteristic mark, with: '[Place] wisdom in me...'

13.8.11.a.m: Just so are the apportioned ukthya draughts.

13.8.12.b.s: indrāya tvendrāya tveti sarvatra grahaṇasādanau saṃnamati
13.8.12.b.d: इन्द्राय त्वेन्द्राय त्वेति सर्वत्र ग्रहणसादनौ संनमति
13.8.12.b.m: everywhere he adapts the drawing and settling formulas to: 'For Indra, you; for Indra, you.'

13.8.13.a.s: ukthaṃ vācītyāha mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ pratigīrya śastraṃśastraṃ vā /
13.8.13.a.d: उक्थं वाचीत्याह माध्यंदिनं सवनं प्रतिगीर्य शस्त्रंशस्त्रं वा ।
13.8.13.a.m: Having responded to the midday pressing, or after each recitation, he says: 'The praise has been spoken.'

13.8.13.b.s: viśve devā maruta iti saṃsthite savana āhutiṃ juhoti
13.8.13.b.d: विश्वे देवा मरुत इति संस्थिते सवन आहुतिं जुहोति
13.8.13.b.m: When the pressing is concluded, he offers an oblation with: 'All-gods, Maruts...'

13.8.14.a.m: The ritual call and the creeping are just the same.

13.9.1.a.m: The third pressing begins with the Āditya [draught].

13.9.2.a.m: Having closed both doors of the cart-shed, when there are many people on the altar ground;

13.9.3.a.s: yadi vāsya bhrātṛvyaḥ prasṛptaḥ syādantarvedi sati gṛhṇīyāt
13.9.3.a.d: यदि वास्य भ्रातृव्यः प्रसृप्तः स्यादन्तर्वेदि सति गृह्णीयात्
13.9.3.a.m: Or, if his rival has crept in, he should draw it while remaining inside the altar ground.

13.9.4.a.s: bhrātṛvyayajñe tu gṛhyamāṇa āditye bahirvedi tiṣṭhet
13.9.4.a.d: भ्रातृव्ययज्ञे तु गृह्यमाण आदित्ये बहिर्वेदि तिष्ठेत्
13.9.4.a.m: At the sacrifice of a rival, however, while the Āditya [draught] is being drawn, he should stand outside the altar ground.

13.9.5.a.s: ādityapātreṇa ya ādityasthālyāṃ dvidevatyagrahasaṃpātāstebhyaḥ somaṃ gṛhṇāti kadācana starīrasīti
13.9.5.a.d: आदित्यपात्रेण य आदित्यस्थाल्यां द्विदेवत्यग्रहसंपातास्तेभ्यः सोमं गृह्णाति कदाचन स्तरीरसीति
13.9.5.a.m: With the Āditya vessel he draws soma from the remnants of the draughts for two deities which are in the Āditya pot, with [the formula]: 'Thou art never barren... '

13.9.6.a.m: With 'Thou art never negligent...', [he draws] boiled and curdled sour milk.

13.9.7.a.s: yajño devānāmiti punaḥ somaṃ gṛhītvā vivasva ādityeti tasmingrāvāṇamupāṃśusavanamavadhāya tenainaṃ mekṣayitvā
13.9.7.a.d: यज्ञो देवानामिति पुनः सोमं गृहीत्वा विवस्व आदित्येति तस्मिन्ग्रावाणमुपांशुसवनमवधाय तेनैनं मेक्षयित्वा
13.9.7.a.m: Having drawn soma again with 'The sacrifice of the gods...', putting the upāṃśusavana pressing-stone into it with 'O radiant Āditya...', having stirred it with that [stone],

13.9.8.a.s: yā divyā vṛṣṭistayā tvā śrīṇāmīti śṛtātaṅkyena dadhnā payasā vā vṛṣṭikāmasya śrītvā grāvāṇamudgṛhṇāti
13.9.8.a.d: या दिव्या वृष्टिस्तया त्वा श्रीणामीति शृतातङ्क्येन दध्ना पयसा वा वृष्टिकामस्य श्रीत्वा ग्रावाणमुद्गृह्णाति
13.9.8.a.m: [and] having mixed it with boiled and curdled sour milk, or with milk in the case of one desiring rain, with 'With that celestial rain I mix thee...', he lifts up the pressing-stone.

13.9.9.a.m: If a drop quickly falls from the lifted [stone], Parjanya will be prone to rain;

13.9.11.a.m: If he should desire: 'May the beasts miscarry their embryos,' he should lift it up and look at the sun.

13.9.12.a.s: darbhairhastena vāpidhāyottiṣṭhati sūryo mā devo devebhyaḥ patviti
13.9.12.a.d: दर्भैर्हस्तेन वापिधायोत्तिष्ठति सूर्यो मा देवो देवेभ्यः पत्विति
13.9.12.a.m: Covering it with darbha grass or with his hand, he stands up with: 'May the divine Sūrya protect me from the gods!'

13.9.13.a.d: अहं परस्तादित्यादित्यं यजमानो ऽन्वारभत आ होमात्
13.9.13.a.m: With 'I from beyond...', the sacrificer touches the Āditya [vessel] from behind until the oblation.

13.9.14.a.m: With 'The sage extends the path of the sacrifice...', he carries it [forward].

13.9.15.a.m: With 'From the ocean...', he makes it tip forward with blades of darbha grass.

13.10.1.a.s: ādityebhyo 'nubrūhi priyebhyaḥ priyadhāmabhyaḥ priyavratebhyo mahasvasarasya patibhya urorantarikṣasyādhyakṣebhya ādityebhyaḥ preṣya priyebhyaḥ priyadhāmabhyaḥ priyavratebhyo mahasvasarasya patibhya urorantarikṣasyādhyakṣebhya iti saṃpraiṣau /
13.10.1.a.d: आदित्येभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहि प्रियेभ्यः प्रियधामभ्यः प्रियव्रतेभ्यो महस्वसरस्य पतिभ्य उरोरन्तरिक्षस्याध्यक्षेभ्य आदित्येभ्यः प्रेष्य प्रियेभ्यः प्रियधामभ्यः प्रियव्रतेभ्यो महस्वसरस्य पतिभ्य उरोरन्तरिक्षस्याध्यक्षेभ्य इति संप्रैषौ ।
13.10.1.a.m: The two ritual calls are: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for the Ādityas, the dear ones, who have dear abodes, dear ordinances, the lords of the great gathering, the overseers of the broad intermediate space!' and 'Prompt [the hotṛ] for the Ādityas, the dear ones, who have dear abodes, dear ordinances, the lords of the great gathering, the overseers of the broad intermediate space!'

13.10.1.b.m: Or: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for the Ādityas!', 'Prompt [the hotṛ] for the Ādityas!'

13.10.2.a.s: yāste viśvāḥ samidhaḥ santyagna iti darbhānāhavanīye prāsyānyatrekṣamāṇa ādityaṃ juhoti
13.10.2.a.d: यास्ते विश्वाः समिधः सन्त्यग्न इति दर्भानाहवनीये प्रास्यान्यत्रेक्षमाण आदित्यं जुहोति
13.10.2.a.m: Having cast the blades of darbha grass into the āhavanīya with 'Whatever all kinds of kindling sticks are thine, O Agni...', looking elsewhere, he offers the Āditya [draught].

13.10.3.a.m: For one desiring rain, he should make the offering with: 'Cause the earth to swell...'

13.10.5.a.d: सूदवदादित्यपात्रमायतने सादयित्वादाभ्यांशुमुपांशुपावनौ यश्चोपांशुपात्रे ऽंशुस्तानृजीषे ऽपिसृज्य प्रातः सवनवन्महाभिषवः
13.10.5.a.m: Having set the Āditya vessel in its place like the Sūda, casting the Adābhya stalk, the two Upāṃśu strainers, and the stalk that is in the Upāṃśu vessel into the pressed soma-dregs, the great pressing takes place just as at the morning pressing.

13.10.6.a.m: They press only the soma-dregs, however.

13.10.7.a.m: The press-offerings [take place], omitting the curds.

13.10.8.a.s: āgnīdhre patnyāśiraṃ mathitvāparayā dvārā havirdhānaṃ prapādayati /
13.10.8.a.d: आग्नीध्रे पत्न्याशिरं मथित्वापरया द्वारा हविर्धानं प्रपादयति ।
13.10.8.a.m: Having churned the milk-mixture in the āgnīdhra [fire-shed], he brings it into the cart-shed by the western door;

13.10.9.a.m: The sacrificer enters by the eastern [door].

13.10.10.a.s: pūtabhṛto bila udīcīnadaśaṃ pavitraṃ vitatya tasminyajamānaḥ purastātpratyaṅtiṣṭhansaha patnyāśiramavanayatyasme devāso vapuṣe cikitsateti catasṛbhiḥ
13.10.10.a.d: पूतभृतो बिल उदीचीनदशं पवित्रं वितत्य तस्मिन्यजमानः पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ्तिष्ठन्सह पत्न्याशिरमवनयत्यस्मे देवासो वपुषे चिकित्सतेति चतसृभिः
13.10.10.a.m: Having stretched out the strainer with its fringes pointing northward over the opening of the pūtabhṛt [vat], the sacrificer, standing in front facing west, together with his wife, pours down the milk-mixture into it with the four [verses]: 'O gods, consider for our wondrous body...'

13.10.11.a.m: At the time of the draughts, [he takes] only the Āgrayaṇa for the four streams.

13.10.12.a.m: Pouring out from the Āgrayaṇa, he forms the second stream;

13.10.12.b.m: the third from the Āditya pot;

13.10.12.c.m: the fourth from the remnants of the Āditya draught.

13.10.13.a.m: If it is an Ukthya, he draws the Ukthya [draught] at this point.

13.10.14.a.s: viramati dhāraikadhanānāṃ yathārtham ity etadādi mādhyaṃdinavat
13.10.14.a.d: विरमति धारैकधनानां यथार्थम् इत्य् एतदादि माध्यंदिनवत्
13.10.14.a.m: 'The stream ceases,' 'According to need of the Ekadhana [waters]'—from this onward it is as at the midday pressing.

13.11.1.a.s: jāgataḥ panthā ādityā devatāvṛkeṇāparipareṇa pathā svastyādityānaśīyeti sarpaṇe vikāraḥ /
13.11.1.a.d: जागतः पन्था आदित्या देवतावृकेणापरिपरेण पथा स्वस्त्यादित्यानशीयेति सर्पणे विकारः ।
13.11.1.a.m: The modification at the creeping is: 'The path belongs to the Jagatī; the Ādityas are the deities. By an wolf-free, unobstructed path may I safely attain the Ādityas!'

13.11.1.b.s: āyuṣe hiṅkuru tasyai prastuhi tasyai stuhi tasyai me 'varuddhyā iti purastādārbhavātpavamānādyajamāno japati /
13.11.1.b.d: आयुषे हिङ्कुरु तस्यै प्रस्तुहि तस्यै स्तुहि तस्यै मे ऽवरुद्ध्या इति पुरस्तादार्भवात्पवमानाद्यजमानो जपति ।
13.11.1.b.m: Before the Ārbhava Pavamāna [chant], the sacrificer murmurs: 'Make the hiṅ-sound for life; chant the prologue for it; sing the chant for it; for my obtaining it!'

13.11.1.c.m: He recites the Pañcahotṛ or the Saptahotṛ [formula];

13.11.1.d.s: āyuvai hiṅkuru tasyai prastuhi tasyai stuhi tasyai me 'varuddhyā iti ca /
13.11.1.d.d: आयुवै हिङ्कुरु तस्यै प्रस्तुहि तस्यै स्तुहि तस्यै मे ऽवरुद्ध्या इति च ।
13.11.1.d.m: and: 'Make the hiṅ-sound for life; chant the prologue for it; sing the chant for it; for my obtaining it!'

13.11.1.e.s: stūyamāne ca pañcahotāraṃ saptahotāraṃ vā japati /
13.11.1.e.d: स्तूयमाने च पञ्चहोतारं सप्तहोतारं वा जपति ।
13.11.1.e.m: While the chant is being sung, he murmurs the Pañcahotṛ or the Saptahotṛ [formula];

13.11.1.f.m: and at the middle strophic verse, [he murmurs] the third ascension [formula].

13.11.1.g.s: stute 'dhvaryuḥ saṃpreṣyatyagnīdagnīnvihara barhi stṛṇīti puroḍāśām̐ alaṃkuru pratiprasthātaḥ paśau saṃvadasveti
13.11.1.g.d: स्तुते ऽध्वर्युः संप्रेष्यत्यग्नीदग्नीन्विहर बर्हि स्तृणीति पुरोडाशाम्̐ अलंकुरु प्रतिप्रस्थातः पशौ संवदस्वेति
13.11.1.g.m: When the chant is finished, the adhvaryu issues the call: 'Agnīdh, distribute the fires, strew the sacrificial grass, adorn the sacrificial cakes; pratiprasthātṛ, speak together concerning the victim!'

13.11.2.a.m: Here, he should not sprinkle melted butter across the dhiṣṇya hearths that have been distributed and are flaring up with splinters;

13.11.2.b.m: the sprinkling of melted butter takes place later.

13.11.3.a.s: śṛtaṃ havī3ḥ śamitarityetadādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyata eḍāyāḥ
13.11.3.a.d: शृतं हवी3ः शमितरित्येतदादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यत एडायाः
13.11.3.a.m: Beginning with 'Is the oblation cooked, O slaughterer?', he proceeds with the rites of the animal sacrifice up to the iḍā.

13.11.4.a.m: He carries the portion cut off to the south of the cart-shed;

13.11.5.a.m: When the iḍā has been consumed, [the rites] from the press-offerings up to the placing of the Nārāśaṃsa [goblets take place].

13.11.6.b.m: He alters the beginning of the ritual call to: 'Of the sacrificial cakes for Indra of the third pressing...'

13.12.1.a.m: At the time of proceeding, the adhvaryu takes the goblet of the hotṛ;

13.12.2.a.m: Having called for śrauṣaṭ and having received the response, he issues the call:

13.12.2.b.s: tṛtīyasya savanasyarbhumato vibhumataḥ prabhumato vājavataḥ savitṛvato bṛhaspativato viśvadevyāvatastīvrām̐ āśīrvata indrāya somānit saṃpraiṣādiḥ
13.12.2.b.d: तृतीयस्य सवनस्यर्भुमतो विभुमतः प्रभुमतो वाजवतः सवितृवतो बृहस्पतिवतो विश्वदेव्यावतस्तीव्राम्̐ आशीर्वत इन्द्राय सोमानित् संप्रैषादिः
13.12.2.b.m: The beginning of the ritual call is: 'Of the third pressing, accompanied by the Ṛbhus, accompanied by Vibhu, accompanied by Prabhu, accompanied by Vāja, accompanied by Savitṛ, accompanied by Bṛhaspati, accompanied by all the gods, the pungent [somas] mixed with milk, for Indra the somas...'

13.12.4.a.m: At the vaṣaṭ-call he offers with: 'To the flying falcon, svāhā!';

13.12.4.b.s: vaṭ svayam abhigūrtāya namaḥ svāhety anuvaṣaṭkṛte
13.12.4.b.d: वट् स्वयम् अभिगूर्ताय नमः स्वाहेत्य् अनुवषट्कृते
13.12.4.b.m: at the second vaṣaṭ-call with: 'Vaṭ! To him who is greeted by himself, homage, svāhā!'

13.12.6.a.m: In this manner he proceeds with the subsequent ones.

13.12.7.b.m: With each preceding mantra, he offers at each vaṣaṭ-call;

13.12.7.c.m: and with each subsequent [formula] at each secondary vaᤳaᥭ-call.

13.12.8.a.m: Having offered them all, he mutters: ‘May the Hotrās be satisfied.’

13.12.9.a.s: sanneṣu nārāśaṃseṣu camasinaḥ svaṃsvaṃ camasamanū nyante trīṃstrīn puroḍāśaśakalānupavapanta etatte tatāsau ye ca tvāmanvityetaiḥ pratimantram
13.12.9.a.d: सन्नेषु नाराशंसेषु चमसिनः स्वंस्वं चमसमनू न्यन्ते त्रींस्त्रीन् पुरोडाशशकलानुपवपन्त एतत्ते ततासौ ये च त्वामन्वित्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रम्
13.12.9.a.m: When the nārāœaᥓsa [goblets] have been set down, the goblet-holders fill along their respective goblets, scattering three pieces of sacrificial cake into each, with these respective formulas: ‘This for you, father, N.N., and whoever follow you.’

13.12.10.a.m: They mutter the salutations: ‘Homage to you, fathers, for the sap.’

13.12.12.a.m: They step across [the altar ground] with the [verse] to Prajāpati: ‘O Prajāpati, none other than you...’

13.13.1.a.m: Having drawn the Sāvitra [draught] from the āgrayaᥓa [trough] with the antaryāma cup with [the verse]: ‘Today [give us] pleasant [gifts], O Savitᥓ...’, he does not set it down.

13.13.2.a.s: devāya savitre 'nubrūhi devāya savitre preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
13.13.2.a.d: देवाय सवित्रे ऽनुब्रूहि देवाय सवित्रे प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
13.13.2.a.m: The two ritual calls are: ‘Recite for the god Savitᥓ’ and ‘Urge [the Hotᥓ to sacrifice] for the god Savitᥓ.’

13.13.4.a.m: With this very [cup], along with its remainder, he draws the Vaiœvadeva [draught] from the pţabhᥓt.

13.13.5.a.m: ‘You are taken with a support; you are good protection’ are the drawing and the setting-down formulas.

13.13.8.a.s: pra dyāvā yajñaiḥ pṛthivī ṛtāvṛdhetyabhijñāyobhayatomodaṃ pratigṛṇāti madā moda iva . modā moda iveti
13.13.8.a.d: प्र द्यावा यज्ञैः पृथिवी ऋतावृधेत्यभिज्ञायोभयतोमोदं प्रतिगृणाति मदा मोद इव । मोदा मोद इवेति
13.13.8.a.m: Having recognized [the beginning verse]: ‘Forth, Heaven and Earth, with sacrifices, increasing ᥓta...’, he responds with ‘joy’ at both ends: ‘madā moda iva, modā moda iva’.

13.13.9.a.s: anyataratomodaṃ vā madā moda iva . othā moda iveti
13.13.9.a.d: अन्यतरतोमोदं वा मदा मोद इव । ओथा मोद इवेति
13.13.9.a.m: Or with ‘joy’ at one end: ‘madā moda iva, othā moda iva’.

13.13.10.a.s: vyavahitameke samāmananti madā moda iva . othā moda iva . modā moda iveti
13.13.10.a.d: व्यवहितमेके समामनन्ति मदा मोद इव । ओथा मोद इव । मोदा मोद इवेति
13.13.10.a.m: Some hand it down separated: ‘madā moda iva, othā moda iva, modā moda iva’.

13.13.12.a.s: niyudbhirvāyaviha tā vimuñcetyabhijñāya pratiprasthātā dvidevatyapātrāṇi vāyurvo vimuñcatviti vimucyāparayā dvārā nirhṛtya mārjālīye prakṣālya pūrvayātihṛtya yathāyatanaṃ sādayati
13.13.12.a.d: नियुद्भिर्वायविह ता विमुञ्चेत्यभिज्ञाय प्रतिप्रस्थाता द्विदेवत्यपात्राणि वायुर्वो विमुञ्चत्विति विमुच्यापरया द्वारा निर्हृत्य मार्जालीये प्रक्षाल्य पूर्वयातिहृत्य यथायतनं सादयति
13.13.12.a.m: Having recognized [the verse]: ‘With your teams, O Vāyu, unyoke them here’, the pratiprasthātᥓ unyokes the two-deity cups with ‘May Vāyu unyoke you’, takes them out by the western door, washes them at the mārjālģya, brings them back across by the eastern door, and sets them down in their proper places.

13.13.13.a.m: The draught-nārāœaᥓsa [portions] are like the Vaiœvadeva ones.

13.13.14.a.m: He begins the procedure of the caru for Soma.

13.13.15.a.m: The procedure for the caru has been explained.

13.13.16.a.m: Having cooked it, with the sacrificial cord over the right shoulder, he performs the rites with [the caru] for Soma.

13.13.17.a.m: He takes the first portion by hand,

13.13.18.a.s: dakṣiṇato 'vadāyābhighāryodaṅṅatikramya dakṣiṇāmukhastiṣṭhannāśrāvya pratyāśrāvite saṃpreṣyati saumyasya yajeti
13.13.18.a.d: दक्षिणतो ऽवदायाभिघार्योदङ्ङतिक्रम्य दक्षिणामुखस्तिष्ठन्नाश्राव्य प्रत्याश्राविते संप्रेष्यति सौम्यस्य यजेति
13.13.18.a.m: Having taken the portion from the southern side, basted it, stepped across to the north, and standing facing south, having called for the response and it having been answered, he issues the call: ‘Recite the consecratory verse for the [caru] of Soma.’

13.13.19.a.m: At the vaᤳaᥭ-call, he offers on the southern half [of the fire].

13.13.20.a.m: Silently he offers around the [caru] for Soma on both sides with clarified butter,

13.13.21.a.m: Having called for the response and it having been answered, he issues the call: ‘Recite the consecratory verse for the clarified butter.’

13.13.22.a.m: Having offered at the vaᤳaᥭ-call and stepped back, having filled the caru with clarified butter,

13.14.2.a.s: tam udgātāro 'vekṣante satro ta etadyadu ta iheti
13.14.2.a.d: तम् उद्गातारो ऽवेक्षन्ते सत्रो त एतद्यदु त इहेति
13.14.2.a.m: The Udgātᥓs look at it with: ‘Here truly is that of yours which is here...’

13.14.3.a.m: Whoever does not see his reflection should look into it after having had clarified butter poured over it.

13.14.4.a.s: yo gatamanāḥ syātso 'vekṣeta yanme manaḥ parāgatamiti
13.14.4.a.d: यो गतमनाः स्यात्सो ऽवेक्षेत यन्मे मनः परागतमिति
13.14.4.a.m: Whoever might feel distracted should look into it with: ‘What mind of mine has wandered away...’

13.14.5.a.m: Here again, he pours clarified butter across the spread dhiᤳᥓya fires blazing with splinters, using eight ladlings of clarified butter alone.

13.14.6.a.s: yadyenaṃ brūyādāgnīdhrīyaṃ me punarvyāghārayeti navagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvāgnīdhrīyamādito 'ntataśca vyāghārya dhārayati dhiṣṇiyānājyaśeṣaṃ ca
13.14.6.a.d: यद्येनं ब्रूयादाग्नीध्रीयं मे पुनर्व्याघारयेति नवगृहीतं गृहीत्वाग्नीध्रीयमादितो ऽन्ततश्च व्याघार्य धारयति धिष्णियानाज्यशेषं च
13.14.6.a.m: If he should say to him: ‘Pour clarified butter across my Āgnģdhrģya [fire] again’, having taken nine ladlings and poured clarified butter across the Āgnģdhrģya fire from the beginning and at the end, he maintains the dhiᤳᥓyas and the remainder of the clarified butter.

13.14.7.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'si bṛhaspatisutasya ta ityupāṃśupātreṇa pātnīvatamāgrayaṇādgṛhītvā na sādayati
13.14.7.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि बृहस्पतिसुतस्य त इत्युपांशुपात्रेण पात्नीवतमाग्रयणाद्गृहीत्वा न सादयति
13.14.7.a.m: Having drawn the Pātnģvata [draught] from the āgrayaᥓa [trough] with the upāᥓœu cup with: ‘You are taken with a support; for you, pressed by Bᥓhaspati...’, he does not set it down.

13.14.8.a.m: Having mixed it with the remainder of the cross-pouring, and having called for the response and it having been answered, he issues the call: ‘O Agnģdh, recite the consecratory verse for the Pātnģvata [draught].’

13.14.8.b.m: He offers at the vaᤳaᥭ-call: ‘agnā3i patnģvā3’.

13.14.10.a.m: Or he may make a secondary vaᤳaᥭ-call silently.

13.14.11.a.s: tataḥ saṃpreṣyatyagnīnneṣṭurupasthamāsīda neṣṭaḥ patnīmudānayonnetarhotuścamasamanūnnaya hotṛcamase dhruvāyāvakāśaṃ kurūdgātrā patnīṃ saṃkhyāpayāpa upapravartayeti
13.14.11.a.d: ततः संप्रेष्यत्यग्नीन्नेष्टुरुपस्थमासीद नेष्टः पत्नीमुदानयोन्नेतर्होतुश्चमसमनून्नय होतृचमसे ध्रुवायावकाशं कुरूद्गात्रा पत्नीं संख्यापयाप उपप्रवर्तयेति
13.14.11.a.m: Then he issues the call: ‘Agnģdh, sit on the lap of the Neᥣᥭᥓ; Neᥣᥭᥓ, bring up the wife; unnetᥓ, fill up following the goblet of the Hotᥓ, make room for the dhruvā [spoon] in the goblet of the Hotᥓ, make the wife look at the Udgātᥓ, make the waters roll forward.’

13.14.12.a.m: They act according to the ritual call.

13.14.13.a.s: antarā neṣṭāraṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ cāgnīdhro vyavasṛpya bhakṣayati
13.14.13.a.d: अन्तरा नेष्टारं धिष्णियं चाग्नीध्रो व्यवसृप्य भक्षयति
13.14.13.a.m: Having crept between the Neᥣᥭᥓ and the dhiᤳᥓya fire, the Āgnģdhra partakes [of the soma].

13.14.14.a.m: He modifies the partaking formula to: ‘...of what has been drunk by Agni’.

13.15.1.b.m: If he were to sit on the lap, he would become a eunuch.

13.15.2.a.s: hotṛcamasamukhyāṃścamasānunnayansarvaṃ rājānamunnīya daśābhiḥ kalaśau mṛṣṭvā nyubjati
13.15.2.a.d: होतृचमसमुख्यांश्चमसानुन्नयन्सर्वं राजानमुन्नीय दशाभिः कलशौ मृष्ट्वा न्युब्जति
13.15.2.a.m: Filling the goblets, beginning with the goblet of the Hotᥓ, having filled up all the king [Soma], he wipes the two vats with the fringed filter cloth and turns them upside down.

13.15.3.a.m: He introduces the chant of the Yajñāyajñģya.

13.15.5.a.m: With ears covered or with ears uncovered, they chant with the Yajñāyajñģya [stotra].

13.15.6.a.m: All those who have crept up should join in singing the Agniᥣᥭoma chant.

13.15.8.a.s: viśvasya te viśvāvata iti hiṅkāramanūdgātrā patnīṃ saṃkhyāpayati /
13.15.8.a.d: विश्वस्य ते विश्वावत इति हिङ्कारमनूद्गात्रा पत्नीं संख्यापयति ।
13.15.8.a.m: Following the hi᥅-sound, with: ‘Of all you, possessing all...’, he makes the wife look at the Udgātᥓ

13.15.8.b.m: until three stotriyā verses [are sung], and with: ‘He has gone to the gods...’

13.15.9.a.m: The wife makes the waters roll forward with her bare right thigh towards the east or towards the north, from between her thighs.

13.15.10.a.m: ‘She should make them roll from upon her thighs,’ say some.

13.15.11.a.m: She should pull [her garment] far up, until uncovering her lap.

13.15.11.b.m: ‘An unembarrassed chief is born to her,’ so it is known [from the Brāhmaᥓa].

13.15.12.a.m: Facing [the hotṛ], he responds to the Āgnimāruta [śastra].

13.15.13.a.s: āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva ityabhijñāyāpo viṣiñcanpratigṛṇāti
13.15.13.a.d: आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इत्यभिज्ञायापो विषिञ्चन्प्रतिगृणाति
13.15.13.a.m: Recognizing [the verse], 'For you, waters, are wholesome', he responds while sprinkling water.

13.15.14.a.s: svāduṣkilāyaṃ madhumām̐ utāyamityabhijñāyobhayatomodaṃ pratigṛṇāti madā moda iva . modā moda ivetyā vyāhāvāt
13.15.14.a.d: स्वादुष्किलायं मधुमाम्̐ उतायमित्यभिज्ञायोभयतोमोदं प्रतिगृणाति मदा मोद इव । मोदा मोद इवेत्या व्याहावात्
13.15.14.a.m: Recognizing [the verse], 'Sweet indeed is this, and honeyed is this', he responds with joy on both sides: 'Madā moda iva', 'Modā moda iva', until the call.

13.15.15.a.s: sādanādi dhruvasya na yajamāno mūtraṃ karotyāvanayanāt
13.15.15.a.d: सादनादि ध्रुवस्य न यजमानो मूत्रं करोत्यावनयनात्
13.15.15.a.m: From the placing of the dhruva [draught] onwards, the sacrificer does not pass urine until its pouring out.

13.16.1.a.s: bhūtamasi bhūte mā dhā iti pratiprasthātā dhruvamavekṣya dyāvāpṛthivībhyāṃ tvā parigṛhṇāmītyañjalinā parigṛhya viśve tvā devā vaiśvānarāḥ pracyāvayantviti hṛtvā dhruvaṃ dhruveṇeti purastātpratyaṅṅāsīno hotṛcamase dhruvamavanayati
13.16.1.a.d: भूतमसि भूते मा धा इति प्रतिप्रस्थाता ध्रुवमवेक्ष्य द्यावापृथिवीभ्यां त्वा परिगृह्णामीत्यञ्जलिना परिगृह्य विश्वे त्वा देवा वैश्वानराः प्रच्यावयन्त्विति हृत्वा ध्रुवं ध्रुवेणेति पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ्ङासीनो होतृचमसे ध्रुवमवनयति
13.16.1.a.m: With 'You are the past, place me in the past', the pratiprasthātṛ looks at the dhruva; having grasped it with folded hands with 'I grasp you by Heaven and Earth', and having lifted it with 'May all the gods related to Vaiśvānara set you in motion', sitting in the east facing west, he pours the dhruva into the hotṛ's goblet with 'The firm with the firm'.

13.16.2.a.m: It is to be poured out before the ukthya [recitation],

13.16.3.a.s: uta no 'hirbudhnyaḥ śṛṇotvaja ekapāditi vā vaiśvadevyāmṛci śasyamānāyām
13.16.3.a.d: उत नो ऽहिर्बुध्न्यः शृणोत्वज एकपादिति वा वैश्वदेव्यामृचि शस्यमानायाम्
13.16.3.a.m: or while the verse addressed to the Viśvedevas, 'And may Ahirbudhnya hear us, Aja Ekapād', is being recited;

13.16.4.a.m: or when the concluding verse is recited once,

13.16.5.a.m: either at the middle or at the final [verse].

13.16.6.a.m: Having responded to the third pressing, he says: 'The recitation has been spoken for Indra';

13.16.7.a.m: At the time of performance, the adhvaryu takes the hotṛ's goblet;

13.16.7.c.m: Having called for the śrauṣaṭ and it being responded to, he gives the ritual call: 'Reciter of the uktha, recite the consecratory verse for the somas.'

13.16.7.d.m: When the vaṣaṭ-call and second vaṣaṭ-call are made, they offer;

13.16.8.a.s: hotṛcamasamadhvaryuḥ pratibhakaṣayati subhūrasi śreṣṭho raśmīnāṃ priyo devānāṃ saṃsadanīyaḥ /
13.16.8.a.d: होतृचमसमध्वर्युः प्रतिभकषयति सुभूरसि श्रेष्ठो रश्मीनां प्रियो देवानां संसदनीयः ।
13.16.8.a.m: The adhvaryu partakes of the hotṛ's goblet together [with the hotṛ]: 'You are well-manifest, the best of rays, dear to the gods, worthy to be sat with;

13.16.8.b.s: taṃ tvā subhava devā abhisaṃviśantviṣo 'si tveṣo 'si nṛmṇo 'si yahvo 'si vrato 'si svo 'si vārṇo 'si tasya ta iṣasya tveṣasya nṛmṇasya yahvasya vratasya svasya vāraṇasya śūdrasya cāryasya ca bhukṣiṣīyeti
13.16.8.b.d: तं त्वा सुभव देवा अभिसंविशन्त्विषो ऽसि त्वेषो ऽसि नृम्णो ऽसि यह्वो ऽसि व्रतो ऽसि स्वो ऽसि वार्णो ऽसि तस्य त इषस्य त्वेषस्य नृम्णस्य यह्वस्य व्रतस्य स्वस्य वारणस्य शूद्रस्य चार्यस्य च भुक्षिषीयेति
13.16.8.b.m: May the well-manifest gods settle into that you; you are food, you are splendour, you are manly power, you are the youngest, you are vow, you are one's own, you are protective; may I partake of that food, splendour, manly power, youth, vow, one's own, protective [power] of yours, belonging to both Śūdra and Ārya.'

13.16.9.a.s: yathā tvaṃ sūryāsi viśvadarśat evamahaṃ viśvadarśato bhūyāsamityādityaṃ yajamāna upatiṣṭhate
13.16.9.a.d: यथा त्वं सूर्यासि विश्वदर्शत् एवमहं विश्वदर्शतो भूयासमित्यादित्यं यजमान उपतिष्ठते
13.16.9.a.m: The sacrificer attends upon the sun: 'As you, Sun, are visible to all, so may I become visible to all.'

13.16.10.a.m: [He attends upon] the āhavanīya with 'Place life and vital power in me; may that come to me.'

13.16.11.a.m: He mentions the name of whatever he desires.

13.16.12.a.m: With 'Agnīdh, bring the coals for the upyāja-offerings', he commences the rite pertaining to the animal sacrifice, beginning with this.

13.17.1.a.m: When the enclosing sticks are thrown [into the fire], the unnetṛ draws the hāriyojana draught.

13.17.2.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'si harirasīti droṇakalaśena sarvamāgrayaṇaṃ gṛhītvā na sādayati /
13.17.2.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽसि हरिरसीति द्रोणकलशेन सर्वमाग्रयणं गृहीत्वा न सादयति ।
13.17.2.a.m: With 'You are taken with a support; you are the bay horse', having drawn all the āgrayaṇa [draught] with the droṇakalaśa, he does not set it down.

13.17.2.b.s: bahvībhirdhānābhiḥ śrītvā śīrṣannadhinidhāyopaniṣkramyendrāya harivate 'nubrūhīndrāya harivate preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau /
13.17.2.b.d: बह्वीभिर्धानाभिः श्रीत्वा शीर्षन्नधिनिधायोपनिष्क्रम्येन्द्राय हरिवते ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्राय हरिवते प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ ।
13.17.2.b.m: Having mixed it with many roasted barley grains, placed it on his head, and gone forth, the two ritual calls are: 'Recite the invitatory verse for Indra with the bay horses' [and] 'Urge [the hotṛ] for Indra with the bay horses';

13.17.2.c.m: or: 'Recite the invitatory verse for the soma with roasted grains', 'Urge [the hotṛ] for the soma with roasted grains set forth.'

13.17.3.a.s: harī stha haryordhānā iti vikramya vaṣaṭkṛtānuvaṣaṭkṛte hutvā harati bhakṣam
13.17.3.a.d: हरी स्थ हर्योर्धाना इति विक्रम्य वषट्कृतानुवषट्कृते हुत्वा हरति भक्षम्
13.17.3.a.m: Stepping across with 'You two are the bay horses, the roasted grains of the two bay horses', having offered at the vaṣaṭ-call and second vaṣaṭ-call, he brings the portion for partaking.

13.17.4.a.s: apareṇottaravediṃ droṇakalaśaṃ pratiṣṭhāpyonnetaryupahavamiṣṭvā sarve hāriyojanaṃ bhakṣayantīṣṭayajuṣaste deva someti
13.17.4.a.d: अपरेणोत्तरवेदिं द्रोणकलशं प्रतिष्ठाप्योन्नेतर्युपहवमिष्ट्वा सर्वे हारियोजनं भक्षयन्तीष्टयजुषस्ते देव सोमेति
13.17.4.a.m: Having placed the droṇakalaśa to the west of the uttaravedi and sought invitation from the unnetṛ, all partake of the hāriyojana draught with 'Of you, divine Soma, whose yajuṣ has been offered...'

13.17.5.a.m: Without chewing the roasted grains, they make cavities [in their mouths];

13.17.5.b.m: having made cavities, they suck [the liquid] out as it were;

13.17.7.a.s: kṛṣyai kṣemāya rayyai poṣāyeti bhakṣayitvā japanti
13.17.7.a.d: कृष्यै क्षेमाय रय्यै पोषायेति भक्षयित्वा जपन्ति
13.17.7.a.m: Having partaken, they murmur: 'For agriculture, for welfare, for wealth, for nourishment.'

13.17.8.a.s: āpūryā sthāmā pūrayatetyuttaravedyāṃ śeṣā nyupya yanma ātmano mindābhūditi mindayāhavanīyamupatiṣṭhante
13.17.8.a.d: आपूर्या स्थामा पूरयतेत्युत्तरवेद्यां शेषा न्युप्य यन्म आत्मनो मिन्दाभूदिति मिन्दयाहवनीयमुपतिष्ठन्ते
13.17.8.a.m: Having poured down the residues on the uttaravedi with 'You are full; fill me', they attend upon the āhavanīya with the mindā-hymn: 'Whatever flaw of mine there has been in myself...'

13.17.9.a.s: devakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi manuṣyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasi pitṛkṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasyātmakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasyanyakṛtasyainaso 'vayajanamasyenasaenaso 'vayajanamasītyāhavanīye śakalānabhyādhāyaikadhanapariśeṣeṣu hariṇīrdūrvāḥ prāsya saṃplomnāya tīvrīkṛtya yathācamasaṃ vyānīyāpareṇa cātvālamāstāve vā pratyañcaścamasinaḥ svaṃsvaṃ camasarasamavaghreṇa bhakṣayantyapsu dhautasya soma deva iti
13.17.9.a.d: देवकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि मनुष्यकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमसि पितृकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमस्यात्मकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमस्यन्यकृतस्यैनसो ऽवयजनमस्येनसएनसो ऽवयजनमसीत्याहवनीये शकलानभ्याधायैकधनपरिशेषेषु हरिणीर्दूर्वाः प्रास्य संप्लोम्नाय तीव्रीकृत्य यथाचमसं व्यानीयापरेण चात्वालमास्तावे वा प्रत्यञ्चश्चमसिनः स्वंस्वं चमसरसमवघ्रेण भक्षयन्त्यप्सु धौतस्य सोम देव इति
13.17.9.a.m: Having put chips of wood onto the āhavanīya with 'You are the expiation of sin committed against the gods; you are the expiation of sin committed against humans; you are the expiation of sin committed against the ancestors; you are the expiation of sin committed by oneself; you are the expiation of sin committed by another; you are the expiation of each and every sin'; having thrown green dūrvā grass into the remnants of the ekadhana waters, stirred it well, made it pungent, and poured it out into each goblet, the goblet-holders, facing west either behind the cātvāla or at the āstāva, partake of their own goblet-sap by smelling, with 'Of you washed in the waters, divine Soma...'

13.18.1.a.m: 'I send you to the ocean; go to your own womb;

13.18.1.b.s: ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrāḥ santu mā parāseci naḥ svam //
13.18.1.b.d: अरिष्टा अस्माकं वीराः सन्तु मा परासेचि नः स्वम् ॥
13.18.1.b.m: May our heroes be unharmed; may our property not be poured away.'

13.18.1.c.s: acchāyaṃ vo marutaḥ śoka etvacchā viṣṇuṃ niṣiktapāmavobhiḥ /
13.18.1.c.d: अच्छायं वो मरुतः शोक एत्वच्छा विष्णुं निषिक्तपामवोभिः ।
13.18.1.c.m: 'Toward you, Maruts, may this sorrow go; toward Viṣṇu, protector of the poured [drink], with his aids;

13.18.1.d.s: uta prajāyai gṛṇate vayo dhuryūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā na ityantarvedi śeṣānninīya dadhikrāvṇo akāriṣamityāgnīdhre dadhidrapsānbhakṣayanti
13.18.1.d.d: उत प्रजायै गृणते वयो धुर्यूयं पात स्वस्तिभिः सदा न इत्यन्तर्वेदि शेषान्निनीय दधिक्राव्णो अकारिषमित्याग्नीध्रे दधिद्रप्सान्भक्षयन्ति
13.18.1.d.m: And may they grant vigour to the progeny of the singer; protect us ever with your blessings'—having poured out the remnants inside the altar ground with [these verses], they partake of the drops of curd in the āgnīdhra [fire-shed] with 'I have praised Dadhikrāvan...'

13.18.2.a.s: ubhā kavī yuvānā satyā tā dharmaṇaspatī /
13.18.2.a.d: उभा कवी युवाना सत्या ता धर्मणस्पती ।
13.18.2.a.m: 'Both sages, youthful, true, guardians of law;

13.18.2.b.s: satyasya dharmaṇaspate vi sakhyāni sṛjāmaha iti tānūnaptriṇaḥ sakhyāni visṛjante
13.18.2.b.d: सत्यस्य धर्मणस्पते वि सख्यानि सृजामह इति तानूनप्त्रिणः सख्यानि विसृजन्ते
13.18.2.b.m: O guardian of law, of truth, we dissolve our friendships'—with this, those who took part in the tānūnaptra dissolve their friendships.

13.18.3.a.m: The patnīsaṃyājas are as in the animal sacrifice.

13.18.4.a.s: stīrṇe vede juhvāṃ navagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā dhātā rātiratyantarvedyūrdhvastiṣṭhansaṃtataṃ samaśo nava samiṣṭayajūṃṣi juhoti
13.18.4.a.d: स्तीर्णे वेदे जुह्वां नवगृहीतं गृहीत्वा धाता रातिरत्यन्तर्वेद्यूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्संततं समशो नव समिष्टयजूंषि जुहोति
13.18.4.a.m: When the veda has been strewn, having taken nine ladlings into the juhū, standing upright inside the altar ground, he offers the nine samiṣṭayajus offerings continuously and evenly with 'Dhātā, the giver...'

13.18.5.a.m: For one whom he wishes should become worse off, he should offer one by one, standing obliquely;

13.18.6.a.s: idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ savanaṃ kavīnāmiti saṃsthite savana āhutiṃ juhoti
13.18.6.a.d: इदं तृतीयं सवनं कवीनामिति संस्थिते सवन आहुतिं जुहोति
13.18.6.a.m: When the pressing is concluded, he offers an oblation with 'This third pressing of the wise...'

13.18.7.a.s: atra mekhalāyāḥ kṛṣṇaviṣāṇāyāśca cātvāle prāsanaṃ vājasneyinaḥ samāmananti māhirbhūrmā pṛdākuriti
13.18.7.a.d: अत्र मेखलायाः कृष्णविषाणायाश्च चात्वाले प्रासनं वाजस्नेयिनः समामनन्ति माहिर्भूर्मा पृदाकुरिति
13.18.7.a.m: Here, the Vājasaneyins prescribe the throwing of the girdle and the black antelope horn into the cātvāla with 'Do not be a serpent, do not be an adder.'

13.18.8.a.s: agninā devena pṛtanā jayāmīti yajamāno jāgatānviṣṇukramānkrāmati
13.18.8.a.d: अग्निना देवेन पृतना जयामीति यजमानो जागतान्विष्णुक्रमान्क्रामति
13.18.8.a.m: With 'With god Agni I conquer the battles', the sacrificer strides the viṣṇukrama strides in the Jāgatī metre.

13.18.9.a.s: sarvebhirdevebhiḥ pṛtanā jayāmyānuṣṭubhena chandasaikaviṃśena stomena vairājena sāmnā vaṣaṭkareṇa vajreṇa sarvajānbhrātṛvyānadharānpādayāmyavainānbādhe pratyenānnude 'sminkṣaye 'sminbhūmiloke yo 'smāndveṣṭi yaṃ ca vayaṃ dviṣmo viṣṇoḥ krameṇātyenānkrāmāmīti caturthameke samāmananti
13.18.9.a.d: सर्वेभिर्देवेभिः पृतना जयाम्यानुष्टुभेन छन्दसैकविंशेन स्तोमेन वैराजेन साम्ना वषट्करेण वज्रेण सर्वजान्भ्रातृव्यानधरान्पादयाम्यवैनान्बाधे प्रत्येनान्नुदे ऽस्मिन्क्षये ऽस्मिन्भूमिलोके यो ऽस्मान्द्वेष्टि यं च वयं द्विष्मो विष्णोः क्रमेणात्येनान्क्रामामीति चतुर्थमेके समामनन्ति
13.18.9.a.m: Some prescribe a fourth [stride]: 'With all the gods I conquer the battles, with the Anuṣṭubh metre, with the twenty-one-fold stoma, with the Vairāja sāman, with the vaṣaṭ-call as thunderbolt; I cause all brotherly enemies to fall beneath; I press them down; I repel them; in this dwelling, in this earthly world, whoever hates us and whom we hate, by Viṣṇu's stride I stride over them.'

13.18.10.a.m: With 'We united with Indra', the sacrificer attends upon the āhavanīya.

13.19.1.a.m: He commences the procedure of the avabhṛtha (purificatory bath).

13.19.2.a.m: Having made the veda and strewn around the fires, he commences the rite beginning with the washing of the hands;

13.19.2.b.m: the arrangement of the vessels is according to requirement.

13.19.3.a.m: At the time of measuring out, he measures out an offering on a single potsherd for Varuṇa.

13.19.4.a.m: Having decorated the fourfold drawn clarified butter and the cake for Varuṇa, he places them on the shoulder of the uttaravedi.

13.19.5.a.s: atra yajamāna audumbarīmutkhidatyupasṛjandharuṇaṃ mātre mātarā dharuṇo dhayanniha puṣṭiṃ puṣṭipatirniyacchatu rāyaspoṣamiṣamūrjamasmāsu dīdharaditi
13.19.5.a.d: अत्र यजमान औदुम्बरीमुत्खिदत्युपसृजन्धरुणं मात्रे मातरा धरुणो धयन्निह पुष्टिं पुष्टिपतिर्नियच्छतु रायस्पोषमिषमूर्जमस्मासु दीधरदिति
13.19.5.a.m: Here the sacrificer pulls out the audumbarī post with 'Letting the suckling go to the mother, the suckling suckling the two mothers, here may the lord of nourishment bestow nourishment, may he sustain wealth and growth, food and vigour among us.'

13.19.6.a.s: tāmadhiṣavaṇacarmaphalake sarvāṇi ca somaliptānyantarā cātvālotkarāvuttare vā vedyaṃsa audumbaryāmāsandyāṃ sādayati /
13.19.6.a.d: तामधिषवणचर्मफलके सर्वाणि च सोमलिप्तान्यन्तरा चात्वालोत्करावुत्तरे वा वेद्यंस औदुम्बर्यामासन्द्यां सादयति ।
13.19.6.a.m: Between the cātvāla and the utkara, or on the northern shoulder of the altar ground, he places it, the two pressing boards covered with skin, and all utensils smeared with soma, upon the audumbarī chair,

13.19.7.a.s: ava te heḍo varuṇa namobhiriti yajamānaścātvāle kṛṣṇājinaṃ prāsyati
13.19.7.a.d: अव ते हेडो वरुण नमोभिरिति यजमानश्चात्वाले कृष्णाजिनं प्रास्यति
13.19.7.a.m: With 'Avert your anger, Varuṇa, through reverences', the sacrificer throws the black antelope skin into the cātvāla.

13.19.8.a.s: punarvainena dīkṣeta vasīta vainadbhrastāṃ vainatsrucāmavadhānārthāṃ kārayet /
13.19.8.a.d: पुनर्वैनेन दीक्षेत वसीत वैनद्भ्रस्तां वैनत्स्रुचामवधानार्थां कारयेत् ।
13.19.8.a.m: Or he may consecrate himself again with it, or wear it, or have it made into a bag for placing the ladles;

13.19.8.b.m: Or it may be used for pounding the oblation.

13.19.9.a.m: Some say: Having come up from the avabhṛtha, he should give it to a son or to a brahmacārin.

13.19.10.a.m: When about to go down to the avabhṛtha, he should offer [a libation] with: "Giving life, O Agni, enjoying the oblation..."

13.20.1.a.s: namo rudrāya vāstoṣpataya āyane vidravaṇa udyāne yatparāyaṇa āvartane vivartane yo gopāyati taṃ huva iti ca
13.20.1.a.d: नमो रुद्राय वास्तोष्पतय आयने विद्रवण उद्याने यत्परायण आवर्तने विवर्तने यो गोपायति तं हुव इति च
13.20.1.a.m: And with: "Homage to Rudra, lord of the dwelling, in our departure, in rushing away, in rising up, at whatever goal, in returning, in turning away; him who protects, do I invoke."

13.20.2.a.s: uruṃ hi rājā varuṇaścakāreti vedyā abhiprayānto vadanti /
13.20.2.a.d: उरुं हि राजा वरुणश्चकारेति वेद्या अभिप्रयान्तो वदन्ति ।
13.20.2.a.m: Advancing from the altar ground, they say: "Wide indeed the king Varuṇa made [a path for the sun]..."

13.20.4.a.m: All of them together with the wife join in the finale (nidhana) of the sāman three times.

13.20.6.a.m: The going to the avabhṛtha is prescribed in all directions: this applies from the beginning of the performance.

13.20.7.a.m: Having performed the ritual with the [sacrificial cake] related to Varuṇa accompanied by the scraping, he sacrifices two after-offerings (anuyājas) without sacrificial grass.

13.20.8.a.s: yatte grāvṇāpyāyasva saṃ ta iti saumībhirdrapsavatībhiḥ pañcabhiḥ saptabhistrayodaśabhirvā dadhnaudumbaraśākhayarjīṣaṃ prokṣati
13.20.8.a.d: यत्ते ग्राव्णाप्यायस्व सं त इति सौमीभिर्द्रप्सवतीभिः पञ्चभिः सप्तभिस्त्रयोदशभिर्वा दध्नौदुम्बरशाखयर्जीषं प्रोक्षति
13.20.8.a.m: With five, seven, or thirteen [verses] addressed to Soma containing [the word] "drapsa", [beginning with] "What of you by the pressing-stone...", "Swell up...", "Let together for you...", he sprinkles the soma-dregs with curds by means of an udumbara branch.

13.20.9.a.m: Or having thrown it in, he should make the offering over it.

13.20.10.a.s: ṛjīṣasya srucaṃ pūrayitvāpsūpamārayati samudre te hṛdayamapsvantariti
13.20.10.a.d: ऋजीषस्य स्रुचं पूरयित्वाप्सूपमारयति समुद्रे ते हृदयमप्स्वन्तरिति
13.20.10.a.m: Having filled the ladles with the soma-dregs, he lowers them into the water with: "In the ocean is your heart, within the waters..."

13.20.11.a.s: tato yo bhindurutsnavate tamupaspṛśedbhakṣayedvāpsu dhautasya soma deva ta iti
13.20.11.a.d: ततो यो भिन्दुरुत्स्नवते तमुपस्पृशेद्भक्षयेद्वाप्सु धौतस्य सोम देव त इति
13.20.11.a.m: Then, whatever drop rises up, he should touch or consume it with: "Of you, washed in the waters, O divine Soma..."

13.20.12.a.s: samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomīti sarvāṇi ca somaliptānyavabhṛthe pravidhyati
13.20.12.a.d: समुद्रं वः प्रहिणोमीति सर्वाणि च सोमलिप्तान्यवभृथे प्रविध्यति
13.20.12.a.m: And with "I send you forth to the ocean..." he throws into the avabhṛtha all things smeared with soma.

13.20.13.a.s: vicṛtto varuṇasya paśa iti yajamāno mekhalāṃ vicacṛte /
13.20.13.a.d: विचृत्तो वरुणस्य पश इति यजमानो मेखलां विचचृते ।
13.20.13.a.m: With "Untied is Varuṇa's noose," the sacrificer unties his girdle.

13.20.13.b.m: With "I untie this..." the wife [unties] the yoke-cord.

13.20.14.a.s: atra yoktramekhale vāsasī jālaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ cāvabhṛthe pravidhya
13.20.14.a.d: अत्र योक्त्रमेखले वाससी जालं कृष्णाजिनं चावभृथे प्रविध्य
13.20.14.a.m: Here, having thrown the yoke-cord, the girdle, the two garments, the net, and the black antelope skin into the avabhṛtha,

13.21.1.a.s: devīrāpa ityavabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpa oṣadhaya ityapaḥ pragāhya saśiraskāvanupamakṣantau snātaḥ patnī yajamānaśca
13.21.1.a.d: देवीराप इत्यवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आप ओषधय इत्यपः प्रगाह्य सशिरस्कावनुपमक्षन्तौ स्नातः पत्नी यजमानश्च
13.21.1.a.m: The sacrificer addresses the avabhṛtha with "O divine waters...", and having plunged into the water with "Friendly to us be the waters and the plants...", the wife and the sacrificer bathe with their heads [submerged], without dipping [the whole body at once].

13.21.3.a.s: yaddidīkṣe manasā yacca vācā yadvā prāṇaiścakṣuṣā yacca śrotreṇa /
13.21.3.a.d: यद्दिदीक्षे मनसा यच्च वाचा यद्वा प्राणैश्चक्षुषा यच्च श्रोत्रेण ।
13.21.3.a.m: "In that I underwent consecration with mind and in that with speech, or in that with the breaths, with sight, and in that with hearing,

13.21.3.b.s: yadretasā mithunenāpyātmanādbhyo lokā dadhire teja indriyam /
13.21.3.b.d: यद्रेतसा मिथुनेनाप्यात्मनाद्भ्यो लोका दधिरे तेज इन्द्रियम् ।
13.21.3.b.m: In that with seed, in a couple, and with myself: from the waters, the worlds have taken splendor and sensory faculty.

13.21.3.c.s: śukrā dīkṣāyai tapaso vimocanīrāpo vimoktrīrmayi teja indriyam //
13.21.3.c.d: शुक्रा दीक्षायै तपसो विमोचनीरापो विमोक्त्रीर्मयि तेज इन्द्रियम् ॥
13.21.3.c.m: Bright, releasing from consecration and from austerity, the waters that release: in me be splendor and sensory faculty!

13.21.3.d.s: yadṛcā sāmnā yajuṣā paśūnāṃ carmanhaviṣā didīkṣe /
13.21.3.d.d: यदृचा साम्ना यजुषा पशूनां चर्मन्हविषा दिदीक्षे ।
13.21.3.d.m: In that I underwent consecration with ṛc, with sāman, with yajus, with the hide of animals, with oblation,

13.21.3.e.m: In that with the meters, with plants, in the tree: from the waters, the world has taken splendor and sensory faculty.

13.21.3.f.s: śukrā dīkṣāyai tapaso vimocanīrāpo vimoktrīrmayi teja indriyam //
13.21.3.f.d: शुक्रा दीक्षायै तपसो विमोचनीरापो विमोक्त्रीर्मयि तेज इन्द्रियम् ॥
13.21.3.f.m: Bright, releasing from consecration and from austerity, the waters that release: in me be splendor and sensory faculty!

13.21.3.g.s: yana brahma yena kṣatraṃ yenendrāgnī prajāpatiḥ somo varuṇo yena rājā /
13.21.3.g.d: यन ब्रह्म येन क्षत्रं येनेन्द्राग्नी प्रजापतिः सोमो वरुणो येन राजा ।
13.21.3.g.m: By which the sacred power, by which the ruling power, by which Indra and Agni, Prajāpati, Soma, by which king Varuṇa,

13.21.3.h.s: viśve devā ṛṣayo yena prāṇā adbhyo lokā dadhire teja indriyam /
13.21.3.h.d: विश्वे देवा ऋषयो येन प्राणा अद्भ्यो लोका दधिरे तेज इन्द्रियम् ।
13.21.3.h.m: The All-gods, the ṛṣis, by which the breaths: from the waters, the worlds have taken splendor and sensory faculty.

13.21.3.i.s: śukrā dīkṣāyai tapaso vimocanīrāpo vimoktrīrmayi teja indriyamiti trirañjalinā viṣicyonnetarvasīyo na unnayābhi /
13.21.3.i.d: शुक्रा दीक्षायै तपसो विमोचनीरापो विमोक्त्रीर्मयि तेज इन्द्रियमिति त्रिरञ्जलिना विषिच्योन्नेतर्वसीयो न उन्नयाभि ।
13.21.3.i.m: Bright, releasing from consecration and from austerity, the waters that release: in me be splendor and sensory faculty!" — having three times poured [water] over himself with the folded hands, the sacrificer gives the ritual call: "O unnetṛ, lead us up to what is better!

13.21.3.j.m: Upwards to you, gaining most wealth, the songs, the stomas speed

13.21.3.k.s: satrājito dhanasā akṣitotayo vājayanto rathā iva /
13.21.3.k.d: सत्राजितो धनसा अक्षितोतयो वाजयन्तो रथा इव ।
13.21.3.k.m: Winning all at once, gaining goods, with unexhausted aids, striving for prizes like chariots,

13.21.3.l.s: kaṇvā iva bhṛgavaḥ sūryā iva viśvamiddhītamānaśuriti yajamānaḥ saṃpreṣyati
13.21.3.l.d: कण्वा इव भृगवः सूर्या इव विश्वमिद्धीतमानशुरिति यजमानः संप्रेष्यति
13.21.3.l.m: Like the Kaṇvas, the Bhṛgus, like suns: they have reached all that is placed in thought."

13.22.1.a.m: "Come up, bestowing offspring, life, and luster; may we then be wealthy in the houses of both;

13.22.1.b.m: May the meters follow along the gāyatrī; may riches and sacrifices accompany us!

13.22.1.c.m: Well-pleased, the sun has entered the waters" — saying this, the unnetṛ leads [them] up.

13.22.3.a.m: The sacrificer puts on the soma-turban.

13.22.3.b.m: The wife [puts on] the cloth used for wrapping soma, or the cloth used for enclosing soma.

13.22.4.a.m: Those two [garments] are given to the adhvaryu at the udavasānīyā sacrifice.

13.22.5.a.s: udvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya pāśa ityudakānataṃ pratyasitvā samitpāṇaya unnetāraṃ puraskṛtyāpratīkṣamāyantyapāma somamiti mahīyāṃ vadanto yāny apāmityāny apratīttāny asmi yamasya balinā carāmi /
13.22.5.a.d: उद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पाश इत्युदकानतं प्रत्यसित्वा समित्पाणय उन्नेतारं पुरस्कृत्याप्रतीक्षमायन्त्यपाम सोममिति महीयां वदन्तो यान्य् अपामित्यान्य् अप्रतीत्तान्य् अस्मि यमस्य बलिना चरामि ।
13.22.5.a.m: Having stood worshipping the sun with "Up into the darkness...", having cast back [the water] bent towards the water with "Varuṇa's noose is repelled," with firewood in their hands, placing the unnetṛ in front, they return without looking back, reciting the Great Verse: "We have drunk soma... What debts of mine are unpaid, what I pay out as Yama's tribute:

13.22.5.b.s: ihaiva santaḥ prati tadyātayāmo jīvā jīvebhyo niharāma enat //
13.22.5.b.d: इहैव सन्तः प्रति तद्यातयामो जीवा जीवेभ्यो निहराम एनत् ॥
13.22.5.b.m: Remaining right here, let us requite that; living, let us remove it for the living!

13.22.5.c.s: anṛṇā asminnanṛṇāḥ parasmiṃstṛtīye loke anṛṇāḥ syāma /
13.22.5.c.d: अनृणा अस्मिन्ननृणाः परस्मिंस्तृतीये लोके अनृणाः स्याम ।
13.22.5.c.m: Debtless in this world, debtless in the other, in the third world may we be debtless!

13.22.5.d.s: ye devayānā uta pitṛyāṇāḥ sarvānpatho anṛṇā ā kṣīyemeti ca
13.22.5.d.d: ये देवयाना उत पितृयाणाः सर्वान्पथो अनृणा आ क्षीयेमेति च
13.22.5.d.m: Whatever paths lead to the gods and lead to the ancestors, on all paths may we dwell debtless!"

13.22.6.a.m: Having placed pieces of firewood on the āhavanīya with "You are fuel; may we prosper!", they stand worshipping [the fire] with "I have gone along with the waters...".

13.23.1.a.m: The concluding sacrifice (udayanīyā) is like the introductory sacrifice (prāyaṇīyā).

13.23.2.a.m: He cooks [the oblation] in that very pot without having scraped it clean.

13.23.3.a.m: They perform the rites on the śālāmukhīya fire.

13.23.4.a.m: In those very places, he sacrifices to Agni first of the butter-portions.

13.23.4.b.m: [And he sacrifices to] Pathyā Svasti last.

13.23.5.a.m: The consecratory verses are those of the introductory sacrifice: thus it is stated.

13.23.6.a.m: He binds [as a sacrificial victim] a barren cow for Mitra-Varuṇa as the anūbandhyā cow.

13.23.7.a.m: Her procedure is like that of the independent animal sacrifice (nirūḍhapaśubandha).

13.23.8.a.s: mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ gorvapāyā medaso 'nubrūhi mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ gorvapāyā medasa preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
13.23.8.a.d: मित्रावरुणाभ्यां गोर्वपाया मेदसो ऽनुब्रूहि मित्रावरुणाभ्यां गोर्वपाया मेदस प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
13.23.8.a.m: The two ritual calls are: "Recite [the invitatory verse] for Mitra-Varuṇa for the omentum and fat of the cow!" and "Prompt [the hotṛ] for Mitra-Varuṇa for the omentum and fat of the cow!"

13.23.9.a.m: in the portions of the oblation, he thus adapts the ends with 'of the oblation'.

13.23.11.a.m: one for Mitra-Varuṇa, one for the Viśvedevas, and one for Bṛhaspati.

13.23.13.a.m: They perform [the rites] for the [victim] dedicated to the Viśvedevas silently in the middle.

13.23.14.a.s: tā na sarvatrālabheta vājapeye rājasūye sattre sahasre sarvavedase vā
13.23.14.a.d: ता न सर्वत्रालभेत वाजपेये राजसूये सत्त्रे सहस्रे सर्ववेदसे वा
13.23.14.a.m: One should not seize them everywhere, [but only] at the Vājapeya, the Rājasūya, a sattra, a thousand-[cow sacrifice], or a Sarvavedasa.

13.23.15.a.s: yaḥ kāmayeta sarvo me yajñaḥ syātsarasa iti sa etāstirso 'nūbandhyā ālabheta
13.23.15.a.d: यः कामयेत सर्वो मे यज्ञः स्यात्सरस इति स एतास्तिर्सो ऽनूबन्ध्या आलभेत
13.23.15.a.m: One who desires, 'May my sacrifice be complete, full of sap,' should seize these three anūbandhyā [victims].

13.23.16.a.s: anūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dakṣiṇe vedyante yajamānaḥ keśaśmaśru vāpayate
13.23.16.a.d: अनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायां दक्षिणे वेद्यन्ते यजमानः केशश्मश्रु वापयते
13.23.16.a.m: When the omentum of the anūbandhyā has been offered, the sacrificer has his hair and beard shaved at the southern edge of the altar ground.

13.23.17.a.m: [After] the animal cake of the anūbandhyā,

13.24.1.a.m: he measures out the Devikā oblations:

13.24.2.a.m: five [oblations, beginning with] a cake on twelve potsherds for Dhātṛ.

13.24.3.a.s: yāsu sthālīṣu somā bhavanti tāsūttarāṇi catvāri havīṃṣi śrapayati
13.24.3.a.d: यासु स्थालीषु सोमा भवन्ति तासूत्तराणि चत्वारि हवींषि श्रपयति
13.24.3.a.m: In the pots in which the somas are kept, in those he cooks the subsequent four oblations.

13.24.4.a.m: The Sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā, however, are common [to them all].

13.24.5.a.m: One desiring offspring should measure out the Devikā [oblations]—these are optional.

13.24.6.a.m: During the anūbandhyā [rite], he offers the sacrificial chip (svaru).

13.24.8.a.s: rājño rājaṃbhavyasya vānūbandhyāyāḥ paśupuroḍāśamaṣṭau devasuvāṃ havīṃṣyanunirvapatyagnaye gṛhapataya iti
13.24.8.a.d: राज्ञो राजंभव्यस्य वानूबन्ध्यायाः पशुपुरोडाशमष्टौ देवसुवां हवींष्यनुनिर्वपत्यग्नये गृहपतय इति
13.24.8.a.m: For a king or one about to become king, he measures out after the animal cake of the anūbandhyā the eight oblations to the divine impellers (devasū), [beginning with] 'To Agni, lord of the house...'

13.24.9.a.m: The Sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā, however, are common [to them all].

13.24.10.a.m: The Ṛgvedins (Bahvṛcas) teach a curd-portion (āmikṣā) for Mitrā-Varuṇā in place of the anūbandhyā.

13.24.10.b.d: तस्या अग्रेण हविर्धानमासीनो ऽनवानं होता यजति ।
13.24.10.b.m: Sitting in front of the cart shed (havirdhāna), the hotṛ sacrifices for it without taking breath.

13.24.10.c.m: It is concluded beginning with the offering of oblations and ending with the iḍā,

13.24.10.d.m: or beginning with the fore-offerings (prayājas), or beginning with the butter portions (ājyabhāgas).

13.24.10.e.m: Some teach that it concludes with the iḍā;

13.24.12.a.m: Following it, he measures out the Devikā oblations.

13.24.13.a.m: The Sviṣṭakṛt and iḍā, however, are common [to them all].

13.24.14.a.s: sadaso havirdhānasya havirdhānayoriti prathamagrathitāngranthīnvisrasyodīcī havirdhāne bahirvedi nirvartayati
13.24.14.a.d: सदसो हविर्धानस्य हविर्धानयोरिति प्रथमग्रथितान्ग्रन्थीन्विस्रस्योदीची हविर्धाने बहिर्वेदि निर्वर्तयति
13.24.14.a.m: Untying the knots first tied with the mantras 'Of the sadas,' 'Of the havirdhāna,' and 'Of the two havirdhānas,' he rolls the two havirdhāna carts northwards, outside the altar ground.

13.24.15.a.m: Taking a firebrand from the āhavanīya, the sacrificer sets fire to the altar ground with: 'Whatever debt [is not yet paid back]...'

13.24.16.a.s: yadi miśramiva caredañjalinā saktūnpradāvye juhuyādviśvalopa viśvadāvasya tveti
13.24.16.a.d: यदि मिश्रमिव चरेदञ्जलिना सक्तून्प्रदाव्ये जुहुयाद्विश्वलोप विश्वदावस्य त्वेति
13.24.16.a.m: If he should behave somewhat confusedly, he should offer groats with his joined hands into the burning fire with: 'O Viśvalopa, for the all-consuming fire thee...'

13.24.17.a.m: With the three [verses] beginning with 'From intention...', he consecrates the smoke.

13.24.18.a.m: The [rite] 'On the arranger of days...' has [already] been stated.

13.24.19.a.m: Having attended [the fires] with the formulas beginning with 'This [is our protection] in front with vapor...', according to the Brāhmaṇa,

13.25.1.a.m: and having placed the veda in his lap, sitting inside the altar ground, he mutters the Atīmokṣa formulas.

13.25.2.a.m: Here, some prescribe the strides of Viṣṇu.

13.25.3.a.s: prājahitaṃ samāropya śalāmukhīyaṃ dvitīyaṃ gataśriyaḥ prāṅudaṅvodavasāyedamū nu śreyo 'vasānamāganma śive no dyāvāpṛthivī ubhe ime /
13.25.3.a.d: प्राजहितं समारोप्य शलामुखीयं द्वितीयं गतश्रियः प्राङुदङ्वोदवसायेदमू नु श्रेयो ऽवसानमागन्म शिवे नो द्यावापृथिवी उभे इमे ।
13.25.3.a.m: Having placed [the fire] of old standing (prājahita) into [the churning sticks], and a person who has attained prosperity [having placed] the śālāmukhīya fire as the second, he should depart towards the east or the north with: 'Now we have come to this better dwelling-place; may both these, heaven and earth, be auspicious to us;

13.25.3.b.m: rich in cattle, rich in wealth, rich in horses, full of sap, rich in heroes, may we move about together with our heroes!' Having arrived at the sacrificial enclosure and churned out [fire], he sets in motion the procedure of the departing sacrifice (udavasānīyā).

13.25.4.a.s: agnīnanvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīnparistīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate /
13.25.4.a.d: अग्नीनन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन्परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते ।
13.25.4.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, made the veda, and strewn around the fires, he proceeds to the action beginning with the washing of the hands.

13.25.4.b.m: The preparation of the utensils is according to requirement.

13.25.5.a.m: At the time of measuring out, he measures out [the offering] for Agni on five potsherds,

13.25.5.c.m: If it is on five potsherds, the two concluding verses (saṃyājyā) are in gāyatrī metre.

13.25.5.d.m: If it is on eight potsherds, [they are] in paṅkti metre.

13.25.6.b.m: or gold of the value of an ox.

13.25.7.a.m: The sacrifice concludes in the established manner.

13.25.7.b.m: The followers of the Vājasaneyi recension prescribe a full offering (pūrṇāhuti) to Viṣṇu in place of the departing sacrifice.

13.25.8.a.m: Having filled the ladle with twelve portions [of clarified butter], he offers it while standing upright inside the altar ground with: 'Through this Viṣṇu strode...'

13.25.9.a.d: सा यावद्रात्रेष्टिः संतिष्ठते ऽथ सायमग्निहोत्रं जुहोति ।
13.25.9.a.m: At whatever time of night that sacrifice concludes, he then performs the evening agnihotra.

14.1.1.a.m: The Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśin, Atirātra, and Aptoryāma are modifications of the Agniṣṭoma in terms of accessory qualities.

14.1.2.a.m: One desiring cattle should sacrifice with the Ukthya.

14.1.2.c.m: One desiring offspring or cattle [should sacrifice] with the Atirātra.

14.1.2.d.m: By means of the Aptoryāma Atirātra, he attains all desires.

14.1.3.a.m: Their ritual procedure is like that of the Agniṣṭoma.

14.1.5.a.s: yathā sadaḥ kratukaraṇaṃ kratupaśavaḥ ṣoḍaśinaḥ somakrayaṇī pātramiti
14.1.5.a.d: यथा सदः क्रतुकरणं क्रतुपशवः षोडशिनः सोमक्रयणी पात्रमिति
14.1.5.a.m: such as the sadas, the ritual actions, the sacrificial animals, the somakrayaṇī cow for the Ṣoḍaśin, and the cup.

14.1.6.a.m: If it is an Ukthya, when drawing up the Agniṣṭoma goblets, he leaves surplus king [Soma] for three groups of goblets.

14.1.7.a.s: agnīnneṣṭurupasthamāsīda neṣṭaḥ patnīmudānayonnetarhotuścamasamanūnnaya hotṛcamase dhruvāyāvakāśaṃ kurūdgātrā patnīṃ saṃkhyāpayāpa upapravartayeti saṃpraiṣaḥ
14.1.7.a.d: अग्नीन्नेष्टुरुपस्थमासीद नेष्टः पत्नीमुदानयोन्नेतर्होतुश्चमसमनून्नय होतृचमसे ध्रुवायावकाशं कुरूद्गात्रा पत्नीं संख्यापयाप उपप्रवर्तयेति संप्रैषः
14.1.7.a.m: The ritual call is: 'Agnīdh, sit in the lap of the Neṣṭṛ; Neṣṭṛ, bring up the wife; Unnetṛ, draw up after the Hotṛ's goblet; make room for the Dhruvā in the Hotṛ's goblet; cause the wife to look at the Udgātṛ; roll down the waters.'

14.1.8.a.m: Having performed with the Agniṣṭoma goblets, he draws the Ukthya [draughts] as at the morning pressing.

14.1.9.b.m: He adapts the [formulas for] drawing and depositing [with]: 'Thee for Indra and Varuṇa' at the first;

14.1.9.c.m: 'Thee for Indra and Bṛhaspati' at the second;

14.1.9.d.m: 'Thee for Indra and Viṣṇu' at the third.

14.1.10.a.s: unnetaḥ sarvaṃ rājānamunnaya mātirīrico daśābhiḥ kalaśau mṛṣṭvā nyubjeti sarvasaṃsthāsūttame gaṇa etatsaṃpreṣyati
14.1.10.a.d: उन्नेतः सर्वं राजानमुन्नय मातिरीरिचो दशाभिः कलशौ मृष्ट्वा न्युब्जेति सर्वसंस्थासूत्तमे गण एतत्संप्रेष्यति
14.1.10.a.m: 'Unnetṛ, draw up all the king [Soma]; do not leave any surplus; having wiped the two vats with the fringed ends, turn them upside down'—in all sacrifice forms, he gives this ritual call at the last group [of goblets].

14.2.1.a.m: The rite of the Agniṣṭoma beginning with 'Agnīdh, bring the coals for the supplementary offerings' is common to all sacrifice forms.

14.2.2.a.s: yadyu vai ṣoḍaśyukthyacamasānāmuttamaṃ gaṇamunnayannekasmai camasagaṇāya rājānamatirecayati
14.2.2.a.d: यद्यु वै षोडश्युक्थ्यचमसानामुत्तमं गणमुन्नयन्नेकस्मै चमसगणाय राजानमतिरेचयति
14.2.2.a.m: If indeed it is a Ṣoḍaśin, when drawing up the last group of the Ukthya goblets, he leaves surplus king [Soma] for one group of goblets.

14.2.4.a.m: At the morning pressing, as the last of the continuous-stream draughts;

14.2.6.b.m: At the first two pressings, he should draw it before the last Ukthya round from the Ukthya [draught], when performance with all [the goblets] has taken place;

14.2.6.c.m: at the third pressing, from the Āgrayaṇa [draught].

14.2.7.a.m: Or only at the third pressing from the Āgrayaṇa [draught] for one desirous of cattle.

14.2.9.b.m: in the Atirātra, for one desirous of holy luster;

14.2.10.a.m: even in the Agniṣṭoma, he should draw it for a nobleman.

14.2.11.a.m: It is accompanied by a chant and a recitation.

14.2.12.a.m: The [formulas for] drawing and depositing are: 'Mount [the chariot], O slayer of Vṛtra...'

14.2.13.a.s: yasmānna jātaḥ paro anyo asti ya āviveśa bhuvanāni viśvā /
14.2.13.a.d: यस्मान्न जातः परो अन्यो अस्ति य आविवेश भुवनानि विश्वा ।
14.2.13.a.m: 'Than whom no other greater was born, who has entered into all the worlds;

14.2.13.b.s: prajāpatiḥ prajayā saṃvidānastrīṇi jyotīṃṣi sacate sa ṣoḍaśī //
14.2.13.b.d: प्रजापतिः प्रजया संविदानस्त्रीणि ज्योतींषि सचते स षोडशी ॥
14.2.13.b.m: Prajāpati, united with offspring, attends to the three lights: he is the Ṣoḍaśin.'

14.2.13.e.m: for thee in the great assembly I would recite of the two bay steeds.'

14.2.13.h.m: who is by name Indra, like ghee.'

14.2.13.j.m: may the songs enter into thee,

14.2.13.k.m: who art of bay form, famous in the troop.' Having deposited [it], he addresses it with these four [verses].

14.3.1.a.m: When the sun is half-set, he brings about the chant of the Ṣoḍaśin with gold.

14.3.3.a.m: They hold a white horse in front;

14.3.4.a.s: othā moda iva made madā moda ivomatheti vyatiṣakta ubhayatomodaḥ pratigara ānuṣṭugbhyaḥ
14.3.4.a.d: ओथा मोद इव मदे मदा मोद इवोमथेति व्यतिषक्त उभयतोमोदः प्रतिगर आनुष्टुग्भ्यः
14.3.4.a.m: The response to the anuṣṭubh verses is intertwined, having moda on both sides: 'othā moda iva made madā moda ivomatha'.

14.3.5.a.s: indrādhipate 'dhipatistvaṃ devānāmasyadhipatiṃ māmāyuṣmantaṃ varcasvantaṃ namuṣyeṣu kurviti hutvendraśca samrāḍvaruṇaśca rājā tau te bhakṣaṃ cakraturagra etam /
14.3.5.a.d: इन्द्राधिपते ऽधिपतिस्त्वं देवानामस्यधिपतिं मामायुष्मन्तं वर्चस्वन्तं नमुष्येषु कुर्विति हुत्वेन्द्रश्च सम्राड्वरुणश्च राजा तौ ते भक्षं चक्रतुरग्र एतम् ।
14.3.5.a.m: Having offered with: 'O Indra, overlord, thou art the overlord of the gods; make me an overlord, long-lived and glorious among mortals', he partakes of the Ṣoḍaśin with: 'Both sovereign Indra and king Varuṇa, they prepared this share for thee in the beginning;

14.3.5.b.s: tayoranu bhakṣaṃ bhakṣayāmi vāgjuṣāṇā somasya tṛpyatviti ṣoḍaśinaṃ bhakṣayati /
14.3.5.b.d: तयोरनु भक्षं भक्षयामि वाग्जुषाणा सोमस्य तृप्यत्विति षोडशिनं भक्षयति ।
14.3.5.b.m: after their share I partake; may Speech, taking pleasure, be satisfied with soma.'

14.3.5.c.m: [He partakes of] the goblets along with the group, as in the case of the Āditya [draught].

14.3.6.a.m: He adapts the partaking formula with: 'Having the anuṣṭubh metre.'

14.3.7.a.m: A reddish-brown horse is the sacrificial gift;

14.3.8.a.m: If it is an Atirātra, when drawing up the Ṣoḍaśin goblets, he leaves surplus king [Soma] for thirteen groups of goblets.

14.3.9.a.m: Having performed with the Ṣoḍaśin, he performs with the night rounds.

14.3.10.a.m: The first group has the Hotṛ's goblet as head;

14.3.10.b.m: the second has the Maitrāvaruṇa's goblet as head;

14.3.10.c.m: the third has the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin's goblet as head;

14.3.10.d.m: the fourth has the Acchāvāka's goblet as head.

14.3.11.a.m: He draws up along with each principal goblet with: 'Thee for Indra at twilight.'

14.3.13.a.s: anuṣṭup chandasa iti sarvatra bhakṣamantraṃ namati
14.3.13.a.d: अनुष्टुप् छन्दस इति सर्वत्र भक्षमन्त्रं नमति
14.3.13.a.m: Everywhere he adapts the partaking formula with: 'Having the anuṣṭubh metre.'

14.3.14.a.m: The adhvaryu performs with the first two groups;

14.3.14.b.m: the pratiprasthātṛ with the latter two.

14.3.16.a.m: The second and third are prescribed in the same way.

14.4.1.a.m: Then the pratiprasthātṛ pours out [the oblations for] the cake on two potsherds for the Aśvins.

14.4.2.a.m: He draws the twilight goblets, of which the hotṛ's goblet is the first.

14.4.3.a.m: The twilight [performance] consists of the trivṛt stoma and the rathaṃtara saman.

14.4.4.a.m: The recitation to the Aśvins comprises more than a thousand [verses].

14.4.5.a.m: It is concluded when the sun has risen.

14.4.6.a.m: When that [recitation] is concluded, the adhvaryu takes the goblet of the hotṛ;

14.4.7.a.s: aśvibhyāṃ tiroahniyānāṃ somānāmanubrūhyaśvibhyāṃ tiroahniyānāṃ somānāṃ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau
14.4.7.a.d: अश्विभ्यां तिरोअह्नियानां सोमानामनुब्रूह्यश्विभ्यां तिरोअह्नियानां सोमानां प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ
14.4.7.a.m: The two ritual calls are: 'Recite [the invitatory verse] for the Aśvins for the overnight somas', [and] 'Prompt [the hotṛ to recite the consecratory verse] for the Aśvins for the overnight somas.'

14.4.8.a.m: Or: 'Prompt [the hotṛ] for the set-out overnight somas.'

14.4.10.a.s: saha somaiḥ puroḍāśaṃ pratiprasthātā sarvahutaṃ juhoti
14.4.10.a.d: सह सोमैः पुरोडाशं प्रतिप्रस्थाता सर्वहुतं जुहोति
14.4.10.a.m: Together with the somas, the pratiprasthātṛ offers the sacrificial cake as an entirely-offered oblation.

14.4.11.a.m: He modifies the partaking mantra as: 'The meter is the paṅkti.'

14.4.12.a.m: If it is an Aptoryāma, while drawing the twilight round goblets, he leaves over king [Soma] for the four sets of goblets.

14.4.13.a.s: yathā prathame rātriparyāye tathā mukhyā bhavanti
14.4.13.a.d: यथा प्रथमे रात्रिपर्याये तथा मुख्या भवन्ति
14.4.13.a.m: Just as in the first night round, so the principal ones are [designated]:

14.4.14.a.m: he draws those sacred to Agni first;

14.4.15.a.m: Some say the procedure for them is like that of the twilight round goblets.

14.4.16.a.m: Everywhere he modifies the partaking mantra as: 'The meter is the aticchandas.'

14.5.1.a.m: The sacrificial animals of the sacrifice form and the eleven [animals] alternate [optionally].

14.5.2.a.m: When they are combined, the preparatory rites are performed as prescribed [for each].

14.5.3.a.m: The subordinate rites are performed as a single combined procedure;

14.5.4.a.m: rites with distinct visible purposes are repeated for each preparation.

14.5.6.a.m: Having offered the sacrificial post oblation, he fells thirteen sacrificial posts with a mantra, beginning with the middle post.

14.5.7.a.m: The bringing of chips and the offerings over the stump pertain to all of them.

14.5.8.a.m: He carves the entire extra post.

14.5.9.a.s: tathā pātnīvataṃ chinatti yathādho nābhisaṃmito bhaviṣyatīti
14.5.9.a.d: तथा पात्नीवतं छिनत्ति यथाधो नाभिसंमितो भविष्यतीति
14.5.9.a.m: He fells the one for the Patnīvant [animal] such that it will be lower than the level of the navel.

14.5.10.a.s: yatprāgvedisaṃmānāttatkṛtvā daśarathākṣāmekādaśoparāṃ rajjuṃ mītvā tasyāścaturviṃśena bhāgena vediṃ mimīte
