14.5.10.a.d: यत्प्राग्वेदिसंमानात्तत्कृत्वा दशरथाक्षामेकादशोपरां रज्जुं मीत्वा तस्याश्चतुर्विंशेन भागेन वेदिं मिमीते
14.5.10.a.m: Having performed what comes before the measuring of the altar ground, having measured a rope ten chariot-axles long [and] with an eleventh butt-portion, he measures the altar ground with a twenty-fourth part of it.

14.5.11.a.m: It takes the place of the stride.

14.5.12.a.s: agniṣṭhaṃ dvābhyāṃ raśanābhyāṃ parivīyaikādaśinī raśanāḥ parivīyāgniṣṭhe vāsayati
14.5.12.a.d: अग्निष्ठं द्वाभ्यां रशनाभ्यां परिवीयैकादशिनी रशनाः परिवीयाग्निष्ठे वासयति
14.5.12.a.m: Having wound two cords around the middle post, and having wound cords for the set of eleven, he leaves them resting on the middle post.

14.5.14.a.m: On the next day, having drawn the draught for the Aśvins, he erects the sacrificial posts;

14.5.16.a.m: Taking the spade is done once, [while] the tracing around is repeated.

14.5.17.a.m: The intervals between the sacrificial posts are the length of a chariot-axle.

14.5.18.a.m: Having traced [the pit] south of the middle post, he traces [the pit] north of the middle post.

14.5.19.a.m: In this alternating manner, he erects the sacrificial posts ending in the north.

14.5.21.a.m: [The row of posts] is elevated towards the south.

14.5.22.a.m: For one desirous of the world of the ancestors, he should erect [a row] elevated towards the north;

14.6.1.a.m: for one desirous of stability, all of equal [height];

14.6.2.a.m: for one desirous of cattle, the three middle ones equal,

14.6.4.b.m: and the two ends are successively depressed;

14.6.5.a.m: for one desirous of rain, sloping uniformly downward [to the center]:

14.6.5.c.m: and the two ends are successively elevated;

14.6.6.a.m: for one with a rival, alternating in height.

14.6.8.a.s: yadi kāmayeta kṣatraṃ viśa ojīyaḥ syādityagniṣṭhāddakṣiṇānvarṣīyaso minuyāt
14.6.8.a.d: यदि कामयेत क्षत्रं विश ओजीयः स्यादित्यग्निष्ठाद्दक्षिणान्वर्षीयसो मिनुयात्
14.6.8.a.m: If he should desire: 'May royal power be stronger than the common people', he should erect the ones south of the middle post taller;

14.6.9.a.m: [if he should desire:] 'May the common people [be stronger] than royal power', then the reverse of this.

14.6.10.a.m: For one desirous of the world of the ancestors, he should erect [the posts] level with the butt-portions;

14.6.10.b.m: for one desirous of the human world, level with the middles and level with the cords;

14.6.10.c.m: for one desirous of power of the senses, level with the top-rings.

14.6.11.a.m: In length, the butt-portions should be equal;

14.6.11.b.m: horizontally, the middles and the cords;

14.6.12.a.s: upaśayaṃ dvābhyāṃ raśanābhyāṃ parivīyāgreṇa dakṣiṇaṃ yūpaṃ prāñcaṃ nidadhāti /
14.6.12.a.d: उपशयं द्वाभ्यां रशनाभ्यां परिवीयाग्रेण दक्षिणं यूपं प्राञ्चं निदधाति ।
14.6.12.a.m: Having wound two cords around the extra post, he places it eastwards in front of the southern post,

14.6.12.c.m: meditating in his mind on the enemy: 'Here do I strike down so-and-so, son of so-and-so, with the thunderbolt of Indra.'

14.6.13.a.m: He dedicates the black-necked [animal] sacred to Agni at the post standing in front of the fire.

14.6.13.b.m: On the north [side], a ewe sacred to Sarasvatī.

14.6.13.c.m: On the south [side], a brown [animal] sacred to Soma.

14.6.14.a.m: In this way, alternating, he dedicates the animals finishing toward the south.

14.6.15.a.m: At the end, the [animal] sacred to Varuṇa, [moving] northward from the south.

14.6.16.a.s: yadi kāmayeta yo 'vagataḥ so 'parudhyatām ity uktam
14.6.16.a.d: यदि कामयेत यो ऽवगतः सो ऽपरुध्यताम् इत्य् उक्तम्
14.6.16.a.m: "If he should desire: 'May he who is driven away be excluded'"—[this] has been explained.

14.7.1.a.m: He should assign a wild animal or a rat to the extra post,

14.7.2.a.s: asau te paśuriti vā dveṣyaṃ manasā dhyāyan
14.7.2.a.d: असौ ते पशुरिति वा द्वेष्यं मनसा ध्यायन्
14.7.2.a.m: or, meditating in his mind upon the enemy: "That is your animal!"

14.7.3.a.m: If he has no enemy, he should say: "A rat is your animal!"

14.7.4.a.m: For each animal there are barhis grasses, omentum-roasting spits, pots, and heart-spits.

14.7.5.a.s: tantramagnerharaṇaṃ tathādhriguḥ saṃjñaptahomo raśanānāmudasanaṃ parivapyau vapāśrapaṇīnāmanupraharaṇamabhihomo mārjanaṃ ca
14.7.5.a.d: तन्त्रमग्नेर्हरणं तथाध्रिगुः संज्ञप्तहोमो रशनानामुदसनं परिवप्यौ वपाश्रपणीनामनुप्रहरणमभिहोमो मार्जनं च
14.7.5.a.m: Common [to all] are: the carrying of the fire; likewise the Adhrigu [formula]; the offering of the strangled [victim]; the casting away of the cords; the two enclosing sticks; the casting of the omentum-roasting spits; the subsequent offering; and the purification.

14.7.8.a.m: The three parts of all [animals] and the shared portion [are offered together].

14.7.9.a.m: Having poured together the remainders, he offers to the quarters.

14.7.10.a.m: At the last animal he sacrifices to Vanaspati,

14.7.11.a.m: With the sections of the intestines of all [the animals], he offers the secondary offerings in the secondary ritual.

14.7.11.b.m: And with the tail-ends they perform the Patnīsaṃyāja offerings.

14.7.12.a.d: अनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायामग्रेण शालामुखीयं पात्नीवतं मिनोत्यधोनाभिमनवस्तीर्णे ऽचषालम्
14.7.12.a.m: When the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, in front of the śālāmukhīya [fire] he sets up the post sacred to Patnīvat, below the navel [in height], without [grass] strewn under it, and without a top-ring.

14.7.13.a.s: tasmiṃstvāṣṭraṃ sāṇḍaṃ lomaśaṃ piṅgalaṃ paśumupākṛtya paryagnikṛtamutsṛjyājyena śeṣaṃ saṃsthāpayet
14.7.13.a.d: तस्मिंस्त्वाष्ट्रं साण्डं लोमशं पिङ्गलं पशुमुपाकृत्य पर्यग्निकृतमुत्सृज्याज्येन शेषं संस्थापयेत्
14.7.13.a.m: Having dedicated at it an uncastrated, hairy, reddish-brown animal sacred to Tvaṣṭṛ, and having released it after fire has been carried around it, he should conclude the remaining [rite] with clarified butter.

14.7.14.a.m: As many portions as there would be of an animal, so many times he should cut off portions of clarified butter.

14.7.15.a.m: The clarified butter takes on the ritual characteristics of the animal.

14.7.16.a.m: It is taught [in the brāhmaṇa]: "They perform the rite at the śālāmukhīya [fire]."

14.7.17.a.m: Or rather, he should merely release it after fire has been carried around it;

14.7.18.a.m: Beginning with the animal cake, he should conclude the remainder of the anūbandhyā cow.

14.7.19.a.s: yadi kāpeyī paśvekādaśinī syādāgneyamabhita aindrau paśū bhavataḥ /
14.7.19.a.d: यदि कापेयी पश्वेकादशिनी स्यादाग्नेयमभित ऐन्द्रौ पशू भवतः ।
14.7.19.a.m: If it is the set of eleven animals according to the Kāpeyas, the two animals sacred to Indra are on either side of the [animal] sacred to Agni;

14.7.19.b.m: to the north, the [animal] sacred to Sarasvatī, that to Soma, that to Pūṣan, and that to Bṛhaspati;

14.7.19.c.m: to the south, the [animal] sacred to Savitṛ, that to the Viśve Devas, that to the Maruts, and that to Varuṇa.

14.7.20.b.m: He should immolate them on the last day of an Atirātra,

14.7.21.a.m: in ahīna sacrifices, on account of the textual connection.

14.8.1.a.m: A descendant of Vasiṣṭha is the brahman in the Jyotiṣṭoma,

14.8.2.a.m: or anyone who knows the Stomabhāga formulas.

14.8.3.a.m: During the duties of the adhvaryu, and during the chant and recitation, he restrains his speech,

14.8.4.a.s: yadi pramatto vyāharedvaiṣṇavīmṛcaṃ vyāhṛtīśca japitvā vācaṃ yacchet
14.8.4.a.d: यदि प्रमत्तो व्याहरेद्वैष्णवीमृचं व्याहृतीश्च जपित्वा वाचं यच्छेत्
14.8.4.a.m: If heedlessly he should speak, having silently recited a verse to Viṣṇu and the sacred utterances, he should restrain his speech.

14.8.5.a.s: rājani mīyamāne mahāvedyāmuttaravedyāṃ ca kriyamāṇāyāmagnau mīyamāne kṛṣyamāṇa opyamāne citeścaterupadhīyamānāyāḥ saṃcitakarmasūkhākarmasu ca kriyamāṇeṣu dakṣiṇata āste
14.8.5.a.d: राजनि मीयमाने महावेद्यामुत्तरवेद्यां च क्रियमाणायामग्नौ मीयमाने कृष्यमाण ओप्यमाने चितेश्चतेरुपधीयमानायाः संचितकर्मसूखाकर्मसु च क्रियमाणेषु दक्षिणत आस्ते
14.8.5.a.m: While the king [Soma] is being measured, while the great altar ground and the high altar are being made, while the fire is being measured, ploughed, and sown, while the layer of the brick altar is being laid, and while the rites of the accumulated [fire-altar] and the rites of the ukhā pot are being performed, he sits to the south.

14.8.6.a.s: rājanyohyamāne 'gnau praṇīyamāna ukhāmaccha gacchatāmohyamānāyāṃ vasatīvarīḥ savanīyāścāccha gacchatāmāhriyamāṇāsu nairṛtīrupadhāsyatāṃ cityagnīnāṃ ca praṇīyamānānāṃ dakṣiṇata eti
14.8.6.a.d: राजन्योह्यमाने ऽग्नौ प्रणीयमान उखामच्छ गच्छतामोह्यमानायां वसतीवरीः सवनीयाश्चाच्छ गच्छतामाह्रियमाणासु नैरृतीरुपधास्यतां चित्यग्नीनां च प्रणीयमानानां दक्षिणत एति
14.8.6.a.m: While the king [Soma] is being conveyed, while the fire is being brought forward, for those going toward the ukhā pot while it is being carried, for those going toward the Vasatīvarī waters and the Savanīya offerings while they are being brought, for those about to lay the Nairṛtī bricks, and while the fires of the brick altar are being brought forward, he walks to the south.

14.8.7.a.m: While the sadas and the havirdhāna sheds are being measured out, stepping along between the pit and the rubbish heap, passing south behind the high altar, he sits down.

14.8.8.a.m: He remains seated until the time of the Vaisarjana offerings.

14.8.9.a.s: hoṣyamāṇeṣu pratyatikramyottareṇa havirdhānaṃ gatvottareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parītya pūrvayā dvārā prāgvaṃśaṃ praviśyāpareṇa śālāmukhīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati
14.8.9.a.d: होष्यमाणेषु प्रत्यतिक्रम्योत्तरेण हविर्धानं गत्वोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं धिष्णियं परीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा प्राग्वंशं प्रविश्यापरेण शालामुखीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति
14.8.9.a.m: When they are about to make the offerings, stepping back and going north of the havirdhāna shed, walking around north of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth, entering the east-pointed hall by the east door, passing south behind the śālāmukhīya [fire], he sits down.

14.9.1.a.m: With the formula: "Praise indeed...", he places the king [Soma] on his lap.

14.9.2.a.m: When the offering has been made, having gone out first, he follows after the fire.

14.9.3.a.s: āgnīdhrīyaṃ prāpya pratiprasthātre rājānaṃ pradāyottareṇāgnīdhrīyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati /
14.9.3.a.d: आग्नीध्रीयं प्राप्य प्रतिप्रस्थात्रे राजानं प्रदायोत्तरेणाग्नीध्रीयं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति ।
14.9.3.a.m: Reaching the Āgnīdhrīya shed, having handed over the king [Soma] to the pratiprasthātṛ, passing south north of the Āgnīdhrīya hearth, he sits down.

14.9.3.b.m: As before, he places the king [Soma] on his lap.

14.9.3.c.s: hute pūrvo niṣkramyāparayā dvārā havirdhānaṃ rājānaṃ prapādyādhvaryave pradāyottareṇa havirdhānaṃ gatvāpareṇottaravediṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati /
14.9.3.c.d: हुते पूर्वो निष्क्रम्यापरया द्वारा हविर्धानं राजानं प्रपाद्याध्वर्यवे प्रदायोत्तरेण हविर्धानं गत्वापरेणोत्तरवेदिं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति ।
14.9.3.c.m: When the offering has been made, having gone out first, having brought the king [Soma] into the havirdhāna shed by the west door, and having handed him over to the adhvaryu, going north of the havirdhāna shed, and passing south behind the high altar, he sits down.

14.9.3.d.m: He remains seated until the offering of the omentum of the animal for Agni-Soma.

14.9.3.f.m: While the Vasatīvarī waters are being carried around, he sits to the south.

14.9.3.g.m: In the deep of night, when they wake, he wakes.

14.9.3.h.m: When the morning recitation has been dedicated, he restrains his speech until the concluding verse.

14.9.3.i.s: savanīyāsu prapādyamānāsu pūrvayā dvārā havirdhānaṃ praviśyāgreṇa kharaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati
14.9.3.i.d: सवनीयासु प्रपाद्यमानासु पूर्वया द्वारा हविर्धानं प्रविश्याग्रेण खरं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति
14.9.3.i.m: While the Savanīya waters are being brought in, entering the havirdhāna shed by the east door, and passing south in front of the mound, he sits down.

14.9.4.a.s: rājani mīyamāne 'bhiṣūyamāṇe graheṣu ca gṛhyamāṇeṣu vācaṃ yacchatyāgrayaṇasya grahaṇāt
14.9.4.a.d: राजनि मीयमाने ऽभिषूयमाणे ग्रहेषु च गृह्यमाणेषु वाचं यच्छत्याग्रयणस्य ग्रहणात्
14.9.4.a.m: While the king [Soma] is being measured and being pressed, and while the draughts are being drawn, he restrains his speech until the drawing of the Āgrayaṇa draught.

14.9.5.a.m: When they offer the drops, he makes an offering.

14.9.6.a.m: During the Pavamāna chants, holding onto [the preceding priest], he creeps forward.

14.9.7.a.s: brahmanstoṣyāmaḥ praśāstarityucyamāne deva savitaretatte prāhety anudrutya
14.9.7.a.d: ब्रह्मन्स्तोष्यामः प्रशास्तरित्युच्यमाने देव सवितरेतत्ते प्राहेत्य् अनुद्रुत्य
14.9.7.a.m: When he is addressed: "O brahman, we shall chant; O director!", having repeated: "O divine Savitṛ, this to thee he has proclaimed...",

14.10.1.a.s: raśmirasi kṣayāya tvā kṣayaṃ jinvoṃ stuteti prasauti
14.10.1.a.d: रश्मिरसि क्षयाय त्वा क्षयं जिन्वों स्तुतेति प्रसौति
14.10.1.a.m: he gives permission: "A ray art thou; for dwelling thee; quicken the dwelling! Om, chant!"

14.10.2.a.m: This is the rule for all the stotras.

14.10.3.a.m: He assigns each subsequent one of the stomabhāga formulas.

14.10.5.a.m: When the Pavamāna chant has been sung, having gone by the way he came, having crossed south behind the uttaravedi, he sits down.

14.10.5.b.m: He sits until the offering of the omentum of the animal for the pressing.

14.10.6.a.s: hutāyāṃ mārjayitvā prātaḥsavanāyasaṃprasarvatsu grahāvakāśaiḥ śṛtaṃ kāraiścopasthāyottareṇa havirdhānaṃ gatvā dakṣiṇena mārjālīyaṃ dhiṣṇiyaṃ parītya pūrvayā dvārā sadaḥ praviśyāgreṇa praśāsturdhiṣṇiyaṃ dakṣiṇātikramyopaviśati
14.10.6.a.d: हुतायां मार्जयित्वा प्रातःसवनायसंप्रसर्वत्सु ग्रहावकाशैः शृतं कारैश्चोपस्थायोत्तरेण हविर्धानं गत्वा दक्षिणेन मार्जालीयं धिष्णियं परीत्य पूर्वया द्वारा सदः प्रविश्याग्रेण प्रशास्तुर्धिष्णियं दक्षिणातिक्रम्योपविशति
14.10.6.a.m: When it has been offered, having purified himself with water, while they proceed together for the morning pressing, having attended upon [the soma] with the grahāvokāśa and śṛtaṅkāra formulas, having gone north of the havirdhāna shed, having circumambulated south of the mārjālīya dhiṣṇya, having entered the sadas by the eastern door, having crossed south in front of the praśāstṛ's dhiṣṇya, he sits down.

14.10.7.a.s: yatrāsmai brahmacamasamāharati taṃ pratigṛhya bhakṣayati yathetare camasān
14.10.7.a.d: यत्रास्मै ब्रह्मचमसमाहरति तं प्रतिगृह्य भक्षयति यथेतरे चमसान्
14.10.7.a.m: When they bring him the Brahman's goblet, having received it, he partakes of it just as the others [partake of their] goblets.

14.10.8.a.m: When the stotra has been commenced, he restrains his speech until the yājyā of the śastra.

14.10.9.a.m: When the pressing has concluded, he steps out by the way he came.

14.10.10.a.s: evaṃ vihitaṃ uttareyoḥ savanayoḥ saṃcaro brahmatvaṃ ca
14.10.10.a.d: एवं विहितं उत्तरेयोः सवनयोः संचरो ब्रह्मत्वं च
14.10.10.a.m: In this manner the movement and the office of Brahman are prescribed for the two later pressings.

14.10.11.a.s: ādhvaryava evāto 'nyāni karmāṇi brahmaṇa āmnātāni bhavanti
14.10.11.a.d: आध्वर्यव एवातो ऽन्यानि कर्माणि ब्रह्मण आम्नातानि भवन्ति
14.10.11.a.m: The other duties of the Brahman are recorded in the adhvaryu's ritual alone.

14.10.12.a.m: When they go to the purifying bath, he walks to the south.

14.10.13.a.m: Thus the office of Brahman for all soma sacrifices is prescribed.

14.11.1.a.m: When about to receive the sacrificial gift, exhaling seventeen times, having turned aside, he should receive it [saying]:

14.11.2.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ pratigṛhṇāmi /
14.11.2.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यां प्रतिगृह्णामि ।
14.11.2.a.m: "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, I receive you.

14.11.2.b.s: rājā tvā varuṇo nayatu devi dakṣiṇe /
14.11.2.b.d: राजा त्वा वरुणो नयतु देवि दक्षिणे ।
14.11.2.b.m: May King Varuṇa lead you, divine sacrificial gift.

14.11.2.c.m: To Agni gold; thereby may I attain immortality.

14.11.2.d.m: May there be vigour for the giver, joy for me, the receiver.

14.11.2.g.m: Desire is the giver; desire is the receiver.

14.11.2.h.m: Enter the ocean of desire! Through desire I receive you.

14.11.2.j.s: eṣā te kāma dakṣiṇā uttānastvāṅgīrasaḥ pratigṛhṇātviti
14.11.2.j.d: एषा ते काम दक्षिणा उत्तानस्त्वाङ्गीरसः प्रतिगृह्णात्विति
14.11.2.j.m: This is your sacrificial gift, O Desire! May Uttāna Āṅgirasa receive you!"

14.11.3.i.m: to Nirṛti a mule and a donkey; from Himavat an elephant;

14.11.3.j.m: to the Gandharvas and Apsarases a garland and an ornament;

14.11.4.a.s: vaiśvānaryarcā rathaṃ pratigṛhṇīyādvaiśvānaraḥ pratnathā nākamāruhaddivaḥ pṛṣṭhaṃ bhandamānaḥ sumanmabhiḥ
14.11.4.a.d: वैश्वानर्यर्चा रथं प्रतिगृह्णीयाद्वैश्वानरः प्रत्नथा नाकमारुहद्दिवः पृष्ठं भन्दमानः सुमन्मभिः
14.11.4.a.m: He should receive a chariot with the verse addressed to Vaiśvānara: "Vaiśvānara has mounted the firmament as of old, the back of heaven, being praised with good thoughts;

14.12.1.a.s: sa pūrvavajjanayajjantave dhanaṃ samānamajmā pariyāti jāgṛviriti
14.12.1.a.d: स पूर्ववज्जनयज्जन्तवे धनं समानमज्मा परियाति जागृविरिति
14.12.1.a.m: generating wealth for the creature as before, the vigilant one goes around the common course."

14.12.2.a.m: Whatever is inanimate, all that he should receive with just: "May Uttāna Āṅgirasa receive you";

14.12.3.a.m: In every case the formula addressed to Savitṛ is at the beginning, and the supplementary formula at the end.

14.12.4.a.m: "The divine women cut you, the active ones stretched you, the protective women wove you"—this he attaches to a garment before the deity formula.

14.12.5.a.s: ta ime tāntrīṇāṃ dakṣiṇānāṃ pratigrahaṇāḥ syuḥ
14.12.5.a.d: त इमे तान्त्रीणां दक्षिणानां प्रतिग्रहणाः स्युः
14.12.5.a.m: These should be the acceptances of sacrificial gifts in sacrifices with sacred rites.

14.12.6.b.m: "The gods, indeed, performed sacrifice for Varuṇa.

14.12.6.c.m: To whichever deity he brought a sacrificial gift, that deity he crushed."

14.12.6.d.s: te 'bruvanvyāvṛtya pratigṛhṇāma tathā no dakṣiṇā na vleṣyatīti /
14.12.6.d.d: ते ऽब्रुवन्व्यावृत्य प्रतिगृह्णाम तथा नो दक्षिणा न व्लेष्यतीति ।
14.12.6.d.m: They said: "Let us accept [it] separately; thus the sacrificial gift will not crush us."

14.12.6.f.m: Then indeed the sacrificial gift did not crush them.

14.12.6.g.s: ya evaṃvidvānvyāvṛtya dakṣiṇāṃ pratigṛhṇāti nainaṃ dakṣiṇā vlīnātīti //
14.12.6.g.d: य एवंविद्वान्व्यावृत्य दक्षिणां प्रतिगृह्णाति नैनं दक्षिणा व्लीनातीति ॥
14.12.6.g.m: One who, knowing thus, accepts a sacrificial gift separately—the sacrificial gift does not crush him.

14.12.7.a.m: One should go toward an ox or a horse with sacrificial grass;

14.12.8.a.m: toward a man or an elephant with food;

14.12.9.a.m: toward a bed with perfumes and pleasing speech.

14.13.1.a.m: For a year, one of the four [classes of food] he should not eat.

14.13.1.b.m: It is recognized [in the sacred text]: "That is the vow of one reciting the Caturhotṛ formulas."

14.13.2.a.m: This indeed is the sacrifice of one who has not set up the sacred fires, namely the Caturhotṛ formulas.

14.13.3.a.s: yaḥ prajayā paśubhir na prajāyeta sa dvādaśāhāni taptamudakaṃ pibanbarāsīṃ vasāno 'dhaḥ śayīta
14.13.3.a.d: यः प्रजया पशुभिर् न प्रजायेत स द्वादशाहानि तप्तमुदकं पिबन्बरासीं वसानो ऽधः शयीत
14.13.3.a.m: He who does not propagate with offspring [or] cattle, drinking heated water for twelve days, wearing hempen cloth, should lie on the bare ground.

14.13.4.a.s: dvādaśyāḥ prātaḥ prāṅutkramya prāṇyāpānyendraṃ gaccha svāhetyapānya daśahotāraṃ vyākhyāya caturhotāraṃ juhuyāccaturgṛhītenājyena
14.13.4.a.d: द्वादश्याः प्रातः प्राङुत्क्रम्य प्राण्यापान्येन्द्रं गच्छ स्वाहेत्यपान्य दशहोतारं व्याख्याय चतुर्होतारं जुहुयाच्चतुर्गृहीतेनाज्येन
14.13.4.a.m: In the morning of the twelfth [day], having stepped forward to the east, having inhaled and exhaled, having exhaled with: "Go to Indra, svāhā!", having recited the Daśahotṛ formula, he should offer the Caturhotṛ formula with fourfold-drawn ghee;

14.13.5.a.m: or half with the prior draught,

14.13.6.a.s: yaḥ kāmayeta prajāyeyeti sa dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā daśahotāraṃ manasānudrutya darbhastambe sagrahaṃ juhuyāt /
14.13.6.a.d: यः कामयेत प्रजायेयेति स द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा दशहोतारं मनसानुद्रुत्य दर्भस्तम्बे सग्रहं जुहुयात् ।
14.13.6.a.m: He who desires, "May I propagate," having filled the ladle with twelvefold-drawn [ghee], having mentally recited the Daśahotṛ formula, should offer into a clump of darbha grass along with the draught;

14.13.6.b.m: or half with the prior draught, half with the subsequent [draught].

14.13.7.a.s: yaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vidyāṃ vidvāṃsaṃ yaśo narchetso 'raṇyaṃ paretya darbhastambamudgrathya brāhmaṇaṃ dakṣiṇato niṣādya caturhotṝnvyācakṣīta
14.13.7.a.d: यं ब्राह्मणं विद्यां विद्वांसं यशो नर्छेत्सो ऽरण्यं परेत्य दर्भस्तम्बमुद्ग्रथ्य ब्राह्मणं दक्षिणतो निषाद्य चतुर्होतॄन्व्याचक्षीत
14.13.7.a.m: A brāhmaṇa who knows the sacred knowledge whom fame does not reach, having gone out into the wilderness, having tied a clump of darbha grass into a knot, having seated a brāhmaṇa to the south, should recite the Caturhotṛ formulas:

14.13.8.a.m: "All of them together with the Saṃbhāra-yajus formulas," says Āśmarathya;

14.13.9.a.s: yo dakṣiṇata āste tasmai varaṃ dadāti
14.13.9.a.d: यो दक्षिणत आस्ते तस्मै वरं ददाति
14.13.9.a.m: To him who sits to the south, he gives a chosen boon.

14.13.10.a.m: Now these are the Wives of the Gods.

14.13.10.b.m: With them one should perform the sacrifice for one desiring offspring or desiring cattle.

14.13.11.a.s: antarā tvaṣṭāraṃ devānāṃ ca patnīścatvāricatvāri padāni pratisaṃkhyāya yajeta
14.13.11.a.d: अन्तरा त्वष्टारं देवानां च पत्नीश्चत्वारिचत्वारि पदानि प्रतिसंख्याय यजेत
14.13.11.a.m: Having counted off groups of four words between Tvaṣṭṛ and the Wives of the Gods, he should sacrifice.

14.13.12.a.s: yadi saṃvatsaraṃ na jāyeta tatparo na sūrkṣet
14.13.12.a.d: यदि संवत्सरं न जायेत तत्परो न सूर्क्षेत्
14.13.12.a.m: If [offspring or cattle] are not born within a year, after that he should pay no heed.

14.13.13.a.m: Practicing sorcery, one should sacrifice with the Daśahotṛ formula.

14.13.14.a.m: One should offer into a naturally formed cleft or a fissure.

14.14.1.a.m: What is harsh in speech, with that he utters the vaṣaṭ-call;

14.14.1.b.m: he cuts him off with the harsh [part] of speech;

14.14.1.c.m: it is recognized [in the sacred text]: "Immediately he comes to ruin."

14.14.2.a.s: yaḥ kāmayeta vīro ma ājāyeteti sa caturhotāraṃ juhuyāccatrugṛhītenājyena /
14.14.2.a.d: यः कामयेत वीरो म आजायेतेति स चतुर्होतारं जुहुयाच्चत्रुगृहीतेनाज्येन ।
14.14.2.a.m: He who desires, "May a hero be born to me," should offer the Caturhotṛ formula with fourfold-drawn ghee;

14.14.2.b.m: or half with the prior draught, half with the subsequent [draught].

14.14.3.a.m: however, no subsequent [son] is born after him.

14.14.5.a.s: etenaiva caturhotrā rājānaṃ saṃgrāme saṃyatte yājayet
14.14.5.a.d: एतेनैव चतुर्होत्रा राजानं संग्रामे संयत्ते याजयेत्
14.14.5.a.m: With this very Caturhotṛ formula he should sacrifice for a king engaged in battle.

14.14.6.a.m: Whatever they obtain there, one hundred and twelve [units] from that are the sacrificial gifts.

14.14.7.a.m: With the Pañcahotṛ formula he should sacrifice for one desiring cattle;

14.14.8.b.m: or half with the prior draught, half with the subsequent [draught].

14.14.8.c.s: catasro dakṣiṇā dadātyaśvaṃ hiraṇyaṃ gāṃ vāsa iti
14.14.8.c.d: चतस्रो दक्षिणा ददात्यश्वं हिरण्यं गां वास इति
14.14.8.c.m: He gives four sacrificial gifts: a horse, gold, an ox, and a garment.

14.14.9.a.m: With this very [rite], excluding the sacrificial gifts, he should sacrifice for one who is sick or one desiring heaven.

14.14.10.a.m: For one desiring heaven, he should offer mentally.

14.14.11.a.m: With the Saptahotṛ formula he should sacrifice for one excluded from sacrifice, with fourfold-drawn ghee;

14.14.11.b.m: or half with the prior draught, half with the subsequent [draught].

14.14.12.a.s: yaḥ kāmayeta bahorbhūyānsyāmiti sa daśahotāraṃ prayuñjīta /
14.14.12.a.d: यः कामयेत बहोर्भूयान्स्यामिति स दशहोतारं प्रयुञ्जीत ।
14.14.12.a.m: He who desires, "May I become more numerous than many," should employ the Daśahotṛ formula;

14.14.12.b.s: yaḥ kāmayeta vīro ma ājāyeteti sa caturhotāram /
14.14.12.b.d: यः कामयेत वीरो म आजायेतेति स चतुर्होतारम् ।
14.14.12.b.m: he who desires, "May a hero be born to me," the Caturhotṛ formula;

14.14.12.c.m: he who desires, "May I possess cattle," the Pañcahotṛ formula;

14.14.12.d.s: yaḥ kāmayetartavo me kalperanniti sa ṣaḍḍhotāram /
14.14.12.d.d: यः कामयेतर्तवो मे कल्पेरन्निति स षड्ढोतारम् ।
14.14.12.d.m: he who desires, "May the seasons be favorable to me," the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula;

14.14.12.e.s: yaḥ kāmayeta somapaḥ somayājī syāmā me somapaḥ somayājī jāyeteti sa saptahotāram
14.14.12.e.d: यः कामयेत सोमपः सोमयाजी स्यामा मे सोमपः सोमयाजी जायेतेति स सप्तहोतारम्
14.14.12.e.m: he who desires, "May I be a soma-drinker, a soma-sacrificer; may a soma-drinker, a soma-sacrificer be born to me," the Saptahotṛ formula.

14.14.13.a.m: Now this [formula] beginning with the season is the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula: "Speech is the hotṛ..."

14.14.13.b.m: Of this, [the text] says: "One should offer at the beginning of each season."

14.15.1.a.s: yadyenamārtvijyādvṛtaṃ santaṃ nirharerannāgnīdhre juhuyāddaśahotāraṃ caturgṛhītenājyena purastātpratyaṅtiṣṭhanpratilomaṃ vigrāham /
14.15.1.a.d: यद्येनमार्त्विज्याद्वृतं सन्तं निर्हरेरन्नाग्नीध्रे जुहुयाद्दशहोतारं चतुर्गृहीतेनाज्येन पुरस्तात्प्रत्यङ्तिष्ठन्प्रतिलोमं विग्राहम् ।
14.15.1.a.m: If they should expel him after he has been chosen for priestly duty, he should offer the Daśahotṛ formula in the Āgnīdhra [fire] with fourfold-drawn ghee, standing in the east facing west, in reverse order, taking each separately;

14.15.1.b.m: he thereby causes his vital breaths to dry up.

14.15.1.c.s: yadyenaṃ punarupaśikṣeyurāgnīdhra eva juhuyāddaśahotāraṃ caturgṛhītenājyena paścātprāṅāsīno 'nulomamavigrāham /
14.15.1.c.d: यद्येनं पुनरुपशिक्षेयुराग्नीध्र एव जुहुयाद्दशहोतारं चतुर्गृहीतेनाज्येन पश्चात्प्राङासीनो ऽनुलोममविग्राहम् ।
14.15.1.c.m: If they should consult him again, he should offer the Daśahotṛ formula in that very Āgnīdhra [fire] with fourfold-drawn ghee, seated in the west facing east, in normal order, continuously;

14.15.1.d.m: it is recognized [in the sacred text]: "He arranges the vital breaths for him."

14.15.2.a.s: sa yaḥ kāmayeta priyaḥ syāmiti yaṃ vā kāmayeta priyaḥ syāditi tasmā etaṃ sthāgaramalaṃkāraṃ kalpayitvā daśahotāraṃ purastādvyākhyāya caturhotāraṃ dakṣiṇataḥ pañcahotāraṃ paścātṣaḍḍhotāramuttarataḥ saptahotāramupariṣṭātsaṃbhāraiśca patnibhiśca mukhe 'laṃkṛtyāsyārdhaṃ vrajet /
14.15.2.a.d: स यः कामयेत प्रियः स्यामिति यं वा कामयेत प्रियः स्यादिति तस्मा एतं स्थागरमलंकारं कल्पयित्वा दशहोतारं पुरस्ताद्व्याख्याय चतुर्होतारं दक्षिणतः पञ्चहोतारं पश्चात्षड्ढोतारमुत्तरतः सप्तहोतारमुपरिष्टात्संभारैश्च पत्निभिश्च मुखे ऽलंकृत्यास्यार्धं व्रजेत् ।
14.15.2.a.m: He who desires, "May I be dear," or for whomever he desires, "May he be dear," having prepared this sthāgara unguent for him, having recited the Daśahotṛ formula in front, the Caturhotṛ formula to the south, the Pañcahotṛ formula in the west, the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ formula to the north, the Saptahotṛ formula above, and having anointed his face with the Saṃbhāra [formulas] and the Wives [of the Gods formulas], he should go into his presence;

14.15.2.b.m: it is recognized [in the sacred text]: "He becomes dear indeed."

14.15.3.a.s: ta ime caturhotāro yatra homārthāḥ sagrahāḥ sasvāhākārāstatra prayujyeran /
14.15.3.a.d: त इमे चतुर्होतारो यत्र होमार्थाः सग्रहाः सस्वाहाकारास्तत्र प्रयुज्येरन् ।
14.15.3.a.m: These Caturhotṛ formulas, wherever they serve for offerings, should be employed along with the draughts and along with the exclamation svāhā.

14.15.3.b.m: Where [the Caturhotṛ formulas] are not for oblation, they are without draughts and without svāhā-calls;

14.15.5.a.m: Of them, one should understand that those associated with the sacrificial enclosure belong to one who has established the sacred fires;

14.16.1.a.m: Men have produced Agni from the two fire-drills with their thoughts and moving hands, [the one who is] praised,

14.16.1.b.m: far-seeing, the lord of the house, restless.

14.16.1.g.s: yanme manasaśchidraṃ yadvāco yacca me hṛdaḥ /
14.16.1.g.d: यन्मे मनसश्छिद्रं यद्वाचो यच्च मे हृदः ।
14.16.1.g.m: Whatever defect there is in my mind, whatever in my speech, and whatever in my heart,

14.16.1.h.s: ayaṃ devo bṛhaspatiḥ saṃ tatsiñcatu rādhasā //
14.16.1.h.d: अयं देवो बृहस्पतिः सं तत्सिञ्चतु राधसा ॥
14.16.1.h.m: may this god Bṛhaspati mend it with abundance.

14.16.1.i.s: viśvakarmā haviridaṃ juṣāṇaḥ saṃtānairyajñaṃ samimaṃ tanotu /
14.16.1.i.d: विश्वकर्मा हविरिदं जुषाणः संतानैर्यज्ञं समिमं तनोतु ।
14.16.1.i.m: May Viśvakarman, enjoying this oblation, join this sacrifice through continuous lines;

14.16.1.j.s: yā vyuṣṭā uṣaso yaśca nimrucastā saṃdadhāmi haviṣā ghṛtena //
14.16.1.j.d: या व्युष्टा उषसो यश्च निम्रुचस्ता संदधामि हविषा घृतेन ॥
14.16.1.j.m: the dawns that have shone forth and the sunsets, these I unite with oblation and ghee.

14.16.1.n.s: bhadraṃ karṇebhiḥ śṛṇuyāma devā bhadraṃ paśyemākṣabhiryajatrāḥ /
14.16.1.n.d: भद्रं कर्णेभिः शृणुयाम देवा भद्रं पश्येमाक्षभिर्यजत्राः ।
14.16.1.n.m: May we hear auspicious things with our ears, O gods; may we see auspicious things with our eyes, O holy ones;

14.16.1.o.m: praising with firm limbs and bodies, may we attain the life ordained by the gods.

14.16.1.p.s: svasti na indro vṛddhaśravāḥ svasti naḥ pūṣā viśvavedāḥ /
14.16.1.p.d: स्वस्ति न इन्द्रो वृद्धश्रवाः स्वस्ति नः पूषा विश्ववेदाः ।
14.16.1.p.m: May Indra of far-spread renown bestow well-being on us; may Pūṣan of all knowledge bestow well-being on us;

14.16.1.q.s: svasti nastārkṣyo ariṣṭanemiḥ svasti no bṛhaspatirdadhātu //
14.16.1.q.d: स्वस्ति नस्तार्क्ष्यो अरिष्टनेमिः स्वस्ति नो बृहस्पतिर्दधातु ॥
14.16.1.q.m: may Tārkṣya of unimpaired fellies bestow well-being on us; may Bṛhaspati bestow well-being on us.

14.16.1.r.s: pṛṣadaśvā marutaḥ pṛśnimātaraḥ śubhaṃyāvāno vidatheṣu jagmayaḥ /
14.16.1.r.d: पृषदश्वा मरुतः पृश्निमातरः शुभंयावानो विदथेषु जग्मयः ।
14.16.1.r.m: The Maruts with dappled steeds, having Pṛśni as mother, moving splendidly, frequenters at assemblies,

14.16.1.s.s: agnijihvā manavaḥ sūracakṣaso viśve no devā avasā gamanniha //
14.16.1.s.d: अग्निजिह्वा मनवः सूरचक्षसो विश्वे नो देवा अवसा गमन्निह ॥
14.16.1.s.m: Agni-tongued, wise, sun-eyed—may all the gods come hither to us with aid.

14.16.1.t.s: śataminnu śardo anti devā yatrā naścakrā jarasaṃ tanūnāṃ /
14.16.1.t.d: शतमिन्नु शर्दो अन्ति देवा यत्रा नश्चक्रा जरसं तनूनां ।
14.16.1.t.m: A hundred autumns are set before us, O gods, during which you have appointed the old age of our bodies,

14.16.1.u.s: putrāso yatra pitaro bhavanti mā no madhyā rīriṣatāyurgantoḥ //
14.16.1.u.d: पुत्रासो यत्र पितरो भवन्ति मा नो मध्या रीरिषतायुर्गन्तोः ॥
14.16.1.u.m: where sons become fathers: do not harm our life in the middle of our journey.

14.16.1.v.m: Kindled, O Agni, shine forth—this [verse is recited].

14.17.1.a.m: Praising with reverences, I approach heaven for the wise, knowable one who hears;

14.17.1.b.s: yato bhayamabhayaṃ tatkṛdhī no 'gne devānāmava heḍa iyakṣva //
14.17.1.b.d: यतो भयमभयं तत्कृधी नो ऽग्ने देवानामव हेड इयक्ष्व ॥
14.17.1.b.m: whence fear comes, make freedom from fear for us; O Agni, appease the anger of the gods.

14.17.1.c.s: agniṃ vo devamagnibhiḥ sajoṣā yajiṣṭhaṃ dūtamadhvare kṛṇudhvam /
14.17.1.c.d: अग्निं वो देवमग्निभिः सजोषा यजिष्ठं दूतमध्वरे कृणुध्वम् ।
14.17.1.c.m: Agni, your god, in harmony with the fires, make the most excellent sacrificer as messenger in the sacrifice,

14.17.1.d.s: yo martyeṣu nidhruvirṛtāvā tapurmūrdhā ghṛtānnaḥ pāvakaḥ //
14.17.1.d.d: यो मर्त्येषु निध्रुविरृतावा तपुर्मूर्धा घृतान्नः पावकः ॥
14.17.1.d.m: who is steadfast among mortals, observant of order, burning-headed, nourished by ghee, purifying.

14.17.1.e.m: With ghee-face, with ghee-back is Agni, kindled with offerings of ghee; ghee is his food;

14.17.1.f.s: ghṛtapruṣastvā sarito vahanti ghṛtaṃ pibanyajatāddeva devān //
14.17.1.f.d: घृतप्रुषस्त्वा सरितो वहन्ति घृतं पिबन्यजताद्देव देवान् ॥
14.17.1.f.m: the streams dripping ghee carry you; drinking ghee, sacrifice to the gods, O god!

14.17.1.p.m: May Agni, praised, protect us with the praise-worthy earthly gods;

14.17.1.q.m: may Vāyu, praised, protect us with the praise-worthy mid-space gods;

14.17.1.r.m: may Sūrya, praised, protect us with the praise-worthy heavenly gods;

14.17.1.s.m: may Viṣṇu, praised, protect us with the praise-worthy directional gods;

14.17.1.t.s: agniryajurbhiḥ pūṣā svagākāraista imaṃ yajñamavantu te māmavantvanu va ārabhe 'nu mārabhadhvaṃ svāhetyetaistribhiranuvākairavijñātaprāyaścitte some trayastriṃśatamāhutīrjuhoti
14.17.1.t.d: अग्निर्यजुर्भिः पूषा स्वगाकारैस्त इमं यज्ञमवन्तु ते मामवन्त्वनु व आरभे ऽनु मारभध्वं स्वाहेत्येतैस्त्रिभिरनुवाकैरविज्ञातप्रायश्चित्ते सोमे त्रयस्त्रिंशतमाहुतीर्जुहोति
14.17.1.t.m: Agni with the Yajus-formulas, Pūṣan with the Svagā-calls, may they protect this sacrifice, may they protect me; I take hold of you, do you take hold of me, svāhā—with these three anuvākas, in the case of an expiation for an unknown error during the Soma sacrifice, he offers thirty-three oblations,

14.17.2.a.m: and thirty-three [oblations of] the sacrificial forms in the Āgnīdhra [fire].

14.17.3.a.s: pṛthivi bhūvari sinīvālyurandhra ācitte manaste bhuvo vivasta iti vasatīvarīṣu savanīyāsu vā viṣiktāsu saptāhutīrhutvā
14.17.3.a.d: पृथिवि भूवरि सिनीवाल्युरन्ध्र आचित्ते मनस्ते भुवो विवस्त इति वसतीवरीषु सवनीयासु वा विषिक्तासु सप्ताहुतीर्हुत्वा
14.17.3.a.m: With: 'O Earth, Bhūvari, Sinīvālī, broad-hipped one, into the gathered thought your mind... may it shine forth for you on the earth'—having offered seven oblations when the Vasatīvarī waters or the Savanīyā waters have spilled,

14.18.1.a.m: having consecrated [the fresh water] with: 'That wave of yours which is fit for oblation, full of vigor, most exhilarating—with it may I thrive for you;

14.18.1.b.m: you are the clarified butter of Soma, the oblation of the oblation, the light of lights;

14.18.1.c.s: viśveṣāṃ vo devānāṃ devatābhirgṛhṇāmītyabhimantrya saṃ vaḥ siñcantu marutaḥ samindraḥ saṃ bṛhaspatiḥ /
14.18.1.c.d: विश्वेषां वो देवानां देवताभिर्गृह्णामीत्यभिमन्त्र्य सं वः सिञ्चन्तु मरुतः समिन्द्रः सं बृहस्पतिः ।
14.18.1.c.m: with the deities of all the gods I draw you,' [he pours it together with the verse]: 'May the Maruts pour you together, may Indra, may Bṛhaspati;

14.18.1.d.s: saṃ vo 'yamagniḥ siñcatvāyuṣā ca dhanena ca /
14.18.1.d.d: सं वो ऽयमग्निः सिञ्चत्वायुषा च धनेन च ।
14.18.1.d.m: may this Agni pour you together with life and wealth;

14.18.1.i.s: āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuva ityetābhiḥ saptabhih saṃsiñcedabhi vā mantrayeta
14.18.1.i.d: आपो हि ष्ठा मयोभुव इत्येताभिः सप्तभिह् संसिञ्चेदभि वा मन्त्रयेत
14.18.1.i.m: O Waters, you are wholesome indeed'—with these seven [verses] he should pour [the waters] together or consecrate them.

14.18.2.a.m: If at the morning pressing before the oblation he should see surplus soma, he should fill it additionally into the goblets or offer it as a subsidiary oblation.

14.18.3.a.m: If he sees it after the oblation, he should make it accompanied by a chant and recitation.

14.18.4.a.m: Having drawn [the soma into] the goblets, beginning with the Hotṛ's goblet, he brings on the chant of the Bṛhat [sāman].

14.18.5.a.m: They should chant on the verses containing dhayat [beginning with] "The cow sucks of the Maruts" [gaurdhayati marutām...];

14.18.6.a.s: asti somo ayaṃ suta iti vaitāsu bṛhatā gaurivītena vā stuvīran
14.18.6.a.d: अस्ति सोमो अयं सुत इति वैतासु बृहता गौरिवीतेन वा स्तुवीरन्
14.18.6.a.m: or they should chant on these [verses beginning with] "This soma is pressed" [asti somo ayaṃ sutaḥ] with the Bṛhat or Gaurīvita melody.

14.18.7.a.m: The hotṛ recites the śastra addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu.

14.18.8.a.m: He modifies the consumption formula to: "... of the one drunk by Indra and Viṣṇu".

14.18.9.a.m: If at the midday [pressing, soma remains over], it is the very same [procedure].

14.18.10.b.s: baṇmahām̐ asi sūryeti saurīṣu bṛhatā gaurivītena vā stuvīran
14.18.10.b.d: बण्महाम्̐ असि सूर्येति सौरीषु बृहता गौरिवीतेन वा स्तुवीरन्
14.18.10.b.m: They should chant with the Bṛhat or Gaurīvita on verses addressed to Sūrya, beginning 'Truly great art thou, O Sūrya' (baṇ mahām̐ asi sūrya).

14.18.11.a.m: The hotṛ recites after in just that manner.

14.18.12.a.m: If it remains over at the third pressing, he should make it an Ukthya.

14.18.13.b.m: If during a Ṣoḍaśin, an Atirātra.

14.18.13.c.m: If during an Atirātra, a Dvirātra.

14.18.13.d.m: If during a Dvirātra, only an Ekastotra.

14.18.14.a.s: tatra vaiṣṇavīṣu śipiviṣṭavatīṣu bṛhatā gaurivītena vā stuvīran
14.18.14.a.d: तत्र वैष्णवीषु शिपिविष्टवतीषु बृहता गौरिवीतेन वा स्तुवीरन्
14.18.14.a.m: There, they should chant with the Bṛhat or Gaurīvita on verses addressed to Viṣṇu containing [the word] 'śipiviṣṭa'.

14.18.15.a.m: The hotṛ recites after in just that manner.

14.19.1.a.s: yadi somau saṃsutau syātāmāditaścaturbhiḥ saṃbhārayajurbhirhutvā mahārātre prātaranuvākamupākṛtyānvārabdhe yajamāne juhoti saṃveśāyopaveśāya gāyatriyāstriṣṭubho jagatyā anuṣṭubhaḥ paṅktyā abhibhūtyai svāheti
14.19.1.a.d: यदि सोमौ संसुतौ स्यातामादितश्चतुर्भिः संभारयजुर्भिर्हुत्वा महारात्रे प्रातरनुवाकमुपाकृत्यान्वारब्धे यजमाने जुहोति संवेशायोपवेशाय गायत्रियास्त्रिष्टुभो जगत्या अनुष्टुभः पङ्क्त्या अभिभूत्यै स्वाहेति
14.19.1.a.m: If two somas should be simultaneously pressed, having offered with the first four saṃbhāra formulas, and having commenced the morning recitation late in the night, he offers while the sacrificer holds on to him, with: 'For lying down, for sitting down; for the Gāyatrī, for the Triṣṭubh, for the Jagatī, for the Anuṣṭubh, for the Paṅkti; for overcoming, svāhā!'

14.19.2.a.m: In this way at the beginning of each pressing, with the subsequent four saṃbhāra formulas and with the subsequent metre up to the Paṅkti [he offers].

14.19.3.a.m: 'The sacrifice has five pressings: the three pressings, the avabhṛtha, and the anūbandhyā [cow].'

14.19.3.b.s: pañca samiddhe 'gnau hūyante prāṇāpānau mṛtyormā pātaṃ prāṇāpānau mā mā hāsiṣṭamiti
14.19.3.b.d: पञ्च समिद्धे ऽग्नौ हूयन्ते प्राणापानौ मृत्योर्मा पातं प्राणापानौ मा मा हासिष्टमिति
14.19.3.b.m: Five [oblations] are offered on the kindled fire with: 'May prāṇa and apāna protect me from death; may prāṇa and apāna not abandon me.'

14.19.4.a.m: Before the animal sviṣṭakṛt, the adhvaryu mutters the consecutive consecratory verses containing 'eti', containing 'pra iti', and containing 'vāja'.

14.19.5.a.m: The introductory verses are accompanied by [verses] addressed to the Maruts or accompanied by [the word] 'vṛṣan'.

14.19.7.a.m: Both the Bṛhat and the Rathaṃtara are [used].

14.19.8.a.m: If the soma sacrifice [of the rival] beyond should be an Agniṣṭoma, he should perform an Ukthya.

14.19.8.f.m: If a Trirātra, only an Ekastotra.

14.19.9.a.m: 'An Abhijit should be performed for victory.'

14.19.9.b.m: 'A Viśvajit should be performed for all-conquering.'

14.19.9.c.s: sarvapṛṣṭhaḥ sarvastomo 'tirātro bhavati sarvasyāptyai sarvasyāvaruddhyā iti vijñāyate
14.19.9.c.d: सर्वपृष्ठः सर्वस्तोमो ऽतिरात्रो भवति सर्वस्याप्त्यै सर्वस्यावरुद्ध्या इति विज्ञायते
14.19.9.c.m: 'The Atirātra is with all pṛṣṭhas and all stomas for the attainment of everything, for the winning of everything,' so it is taught.

14.19.10.a.s: sajanīyaṃ śasyaṃ vihavyaṃ śasyamagastyasya kayāśubhīyaṃ nisevalyam /
14.19.10.a.d: सजनीयं शस्यं विहव्यं शस्यमगस्त्यस्य कयाशुभीयं निसेवल्यम् ।
14.19.10.a.m: The Sajanīya is to be recited, the Vihavya is to be recited, Agastya's Kayāśubhīya Niṣkevalya [is to be recited].

14.19.11.a.m: He should insert the Sajanīya into the Vaiśvadeva [recitation] of the morning pressing.

14.19.11.b.m: The Vihavya into the Marutvatīya of the midday [pressing].

14.19.11.c.d: अगस्त्यस्य कयाशुभीयं निष्केवल्यं तार्तीयसवनिके वैश्वदेवे ऽनुप्रोहेत्
14.19.11.c.m: He should insert Agastya's Kayāśubhīya Niṣkevalya into the Vaiśvadeva [recitation] of the third pressing.

14.20.1.a.m: In that regard, these are the injunctions for the chants:

14.20.1.c.m: 'The Nihava of Vasiṣṭha should be performed.'

14.20.1.d.m: 'Make the Abhīvarta the chant of the brahman.'

14.20.1.e.m: 'Make the sacrificial rite an Abhijit or a Viśvajit.'

14.20.1.f.m: 'Make the Krośa and Anukrośa,' so [the injunctions state].

14.20.2.a.m: Before the morning pressing he gives the order:

14.20.3.c.m: 'or he should make the sacrificial rite superior by means of the sacrificial gifts.'

14.20.4.a.s: yāvadrathāhnyamantarā girirgiribhidvā nadī vyaveyātparvatāntaraye vā nānārājyayorvā saṃsavo nāvidviṣāṇayoḥ saṃsavo vidyata iti kaṅkatibrāhmaṇaṃ bhavati
14.20.4.a.d: यावद्रथाह्न्यमन्तरा गिरिर्गिरिभिद्वा नदी व्यवेयात्पर्वतान्तरये वा नानाराज्ययोर्वा संसवो नाविद्विषाणयोः संसवो विद्यत इति कङ्कतिब्राह्मणं भवति
14.20.4.a.m: 'As long as there should intervene between them a mountain or a mountain-cleaving river, [a distance covered by] a day's journey of a chariot, or if they are separated by a mountain, or in two different kingdoms, there is no simultaneous pressing; there is no simultaneous pressing for two who do not hate each other,' so states the Kaṅkati Brāhmaṇa.

14.20.5.a.m: If an illness should befall the consecrated [sacrificer], he should lie down in the sacrificer's place.

14.20.6.a.m: Taking hold of him, he should lead him to the āgnīdhra [hearth].

14.20.7.a.s: parīmaṃ pari te brahmaṇe dadāmi brahma paridadātu devatābhyaḥ /
14.20.7.a.d: परीमं परि ते ब्रह्मणे ददामि ब्रह्म परिददातु देवताभ्यः ।
14.20.7.a.m: 'I deliver him over; I deliver thee over to Brahman; may Brahman deliver [thee] over to the deities.'

14.20.7.b.m: 'May the vaṣaṭ-call, together with the All-gods, heal thee.'

14.20.7.c.s: vasava etadvaḥ prātaḥsvanaṃ rudrā etadvo mādhyaṃdinaṃ savanaṃ viśve devā etadvastṛtīyasavanam /
14.20.7.c.d: वसव एतद्वः प्रातःस्वनं रुद्रा एतद्वो माध्यंदिनं सवनं विश्वे देवा एतद्वस्तृतीयसवनम् ।
14.20.7.c.m: 'O Vasus, this is your morning pressing; O Rudras, this is your midday pressing; O All-gods, this is your third pressing.'

14.20.7.d.s: tadrakṣadhvaṃ tadbhiṣajyata tadgopāyata tadvo mā vigāditi sarvatrānuṣajati
14.20.7.d.d: तद्रक्षध्वं तद्भिषज्यत तद्गोपायत तद्वो मा विगादिति सर्वत्रानुषजति
14.20.7.d.m: 'Protect it, heal it, guard it, may it not pass away from you,' so he attaches everywhere.

14.20.8.a.s: āgnīdhrīyamupasamādhāya saṃparistīrya brāhmaṇaṃ dakṣiṇato darbheṣu niṣādyottarata udapātramupanidhāya tasminnekaviṃśatiṃ yavāndarbhapuñjīlāṃścāvadhāya jīvā nāma stha tā imaṃ jīvayata jīvikā nāma stha tā imaṃ jīvayata saṃjīvikā nāma stha tā imaṃ saṃjīvayateti pratibrūyāt
14.20.8.a.d: आग्नीध्रीयमुपसमाधाय संपरिस्तीर्य ब्राह्मणं दक्षिणतो दर्भेषु निषाद्योत्तरत उदपात्रमुपनिधाय तस्मिन्नेकविंशतिं यवान्दर्भपुञ्जीलांश्चावधाय जीवा नाम स्थ ता इमं जीवयत जीविका नाम स्थ ता इमं जीवयत संजीविका नाम स्थ ता इमं संजीवयतेति प्रतिब्रूयात्
14.20.8.a.m: Having added fuel to the āgnīdhra fire, strewn grass all around, seated a brāhmaṇa on darbha grass to the south, and placed a vessel of water to the north, having put into it twenty-one barley grains and shoots of darbha grass, he should respond: 'Living ones by name are ye; do ye revive this one! Bestowers of life by name are ye; do ye revive this one! Full revivers by name are ye; do ye fully revive this one!'

14.21.1.a.m: With the hymn to the plants beginning 'The plants that were born' (yā jātā oṣadhayaḥ), he sprinkles him with this water.

14.21.2.a.s: āpaḥ prajāpateḥ prāṇā yajñasya bheṣajamiti cainamācamayanti
14.21.2.a.d: आपः प्रजापतेः प्राणा यज्ञस्य भेषजमिति चैनमाचमयन्ति
14.21.2.a.m: And they make him sip water with: 'The waters are the life-breaths of Prajāpati, the healing medicine of the sacrifice.'

14.21.4.a.s: upāṃśvantaryāmau te prāṇāpānau pātāmupāṃśusavanaste vyānaṃ pātu vācaṃ ta aindravāyavaḥ pātu dakṣa kratū te maitrāvaruṇaḥ pātu cakṣuṣī te śukrāmanthinau pātāṃ śrotraṃ ta āśvinaḥ pātvātmānaṃ ta āgrayaṇaḥ pātvaṅgāni ta ukthyaḥ pātvāyuṣṭe dhruvaḥ pātvasāvasāviti sarvatrānuṣajati
14.21.4.a.d: उपांश्वन्तर्यामौ ते प्राणापानौ पातामुपांशुसवनस्ते व्यानं पातु वाचं त ऐन्द्रवायवः पातु दक्ष क्रतू ते मैत्रावरुणः पातु चक्षुषी ते शुक्रामन्थिनौ पातां श्रोत्रं त आश्विनः पात्वात्मानं त आग्रयणः पात्वङ्गानि त उक्थ्यः पात्वायुष्टे ध्रुवः पात्वसावसाविति सर्वत्रानुषजति
14.21.4.a.m: 'May the upāṃśu and antaryāma [draughts] protect thy prāṇa and apāna; may the upāṃśusavana protect thy vyāna; may the aindravāyava protect thy speech; may the maitrāvaruṇa protect thy mental power and will; may the śukra and manthin protect thy eyes; may the āśvina protect thy ear; may the āgrayaṇa protect thy self; may the ukthya protect thy limbs; may the dhruva protect thy life, [NN]!'—so he attaches [the name] everywhere.

14.21.5.a.m: Then he touches himself in return, with: 'May the upāṃśu and antaryāma [draughts] protect my prāṇa and apāna.'

14.21.7.a.s: puṣṭipataye puṣṭiścakṣuṣe cakṣuḥ prāṇāya prāṇamātmana ātmānaṃ vāce vācamasmai punardhehi svāhetyāhutiṃ hutvā pūrvavadabhimarśaḥ
14.21.7.a.d: पुष्टिपतये पुष्टिश्चक्षुषे चक्षुः प्राणाय प्राणमात्मन आत्मानं वाचे वाचमस्मै पुनर्धेहि स्वाहेत्याहुतिं हुत्वा पूर्ववदभिमर्शः
14.21.7.a.m: Having offered an oblation with: 'To the lord of nourishment nourishment, to the eye the eye, to the breath the breath, to the self the self, to speech speech: restore [these] to him again, svāhā!', the touching is performed as before.

14.21.8.a.m: If he should die before the avabhṛtha, they should perform a fire-avabhṛtha.

14.21.9.a.s: avabhṛthaṃ vā gamayitvā prokṣyainamabhyudāhṛtya svairagnibhiryathālokaṃ daheyuḥ
14.21.9.a.d: अवभृथं वा गमयित्वा प्रोक्ष्यैनमभ्युदाहृत्य स्वैरग्निभिर्यथालोकं दहेयुः
14.21.9.a.m: Or having brought him to the avabhṛtha, sprinkled him, and brought him back, they should burn him with his own fires, each in its proper place.

14.21.11.a.s: ahargaṇeṣvāhara dahetyuktvā dakṣiṇāgneragnimāhṛtya nirmanthyena vā dagdhvā dakṣiṇena mārjālīye mṛtasya dahanam
14.21.11.a.d: अहर्गणेष्वाहर दहेत्युक्त्वा दक्षिणाग्नेरग्निमाहृत्य निर्मन्थ्येन वा दग्ध्वा दक्षिणेन मार्जालीये मृतस्य दहनम्
14.21.11.a.m: In rites lasting many days, having said, "Bring [fire], burn!", and having fetched fire from the anvāhāryapacana fire, or having burned him with churned-out fire, the cremation of the deceased takes place to the south of the mārjālīya.

14.21.12.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ tadahaḥ parisamāpya patnīsaṃyājānte kumbhe 'sthīni saṃbhṛtya mārjālīye nidadhāti
14.21.12.a.d: तूष्णीं तदहः परिसमाप्य पत्नीसंयाजान्ते कुम्भे ऽस्थीनि संभृत्य मार्जालीये निदधाति
14.21.12.a.m: Silently completing that day, at the conclusion of the patnīsaṃyājas, having gathered the bones into an urn, he places it on the mārjālīya.

14.21.13.a.m: The udgātṛs should chant with the three Sarparājñī verses, without the pratihāra.

14.22.1.a.s: ṛtvijo hotṛprathamāḥ prācīnāvītino yāmīranubruvantaḥ sarparājñīnāṃ kīrtayanto dakṣiṇānkeśpakṣānudgrathya savyānprasrasya dakṣiṇānūrūnāghnānāḥ sigbhirabhidhūnvantastriḥ prasavyaṃ pariyantyapa naḥ śośucadaghamiti
14.22.1.a.d: ऋत्विजो होतृप्रथमाः प्राचीनावीतिनो यामीरनुब्रुवन्तः सर्पराज्ञीनां कीर्तयन्तो दक्षिणान्केश्पक्षानुद्ग्रथ्य सव्यान्प्रस्रस्य दक्षिणानूरूनाघ्नानाः सिग्भिरभिधून्वन्तस्त्रिः प्रसव्यं परियन्त्यप नः शोशुचदघमिति
14.22.1.a.m: The priests, headed by the hotṛ, wearing their sacred threads over the right shoulder, reciting the Yama verses and proclaiming those of the Sarparājñī, having tied up the right tufts of hair and let down the left, striking their right thighs and fanning themselves with the borders of their garments, walk three times around counter-clockwise, [reciting]: "May evil burn away from us."

14.22.2.a.s: savyānudgrathya dakṣiṇānprasrasya savyānūrūnāghnānā anabhidhūnvantastriḥ pratipariyantyapa naḥ śośucadaghamiti
14.22.2.a.d: सव्यानुद्ग्रथ्य दक्षिणान्प्रस्रस्य सव्यानूरूनाघ्नाना अनभिधून्वन्तस्त्रिः प्रतिपरियन्त्यप नः शोशुचदघमिति
14.22.2.a.m: Having tied up the left, let down the right, striking their left thighs and not fanning themselves, they walk three times around clockwise, [reciting]: "May evil burn away from us."

14.22.3.a.s: te yadodañcaḥ saṃpadyante 'thaibhyo 'dhvaryurdakṣiṇato 'śmānaṃ paridhiṃ dadhātīmaṃ jīvebhyaḥ paridhiṃ dadhāmi mā no nu gādaparo ardhametam /
14.22.3.a.d: ते यदोदञ्चः संपद्यन्ते ऽथैभ्यो ऽध्वर्युर्दक्षिणतो ऽश्मानं परिधिं दधातीमं जीवेभ्यः परिधिं दधामि मा नो नु गादपरो अर्धमेतम् ।
14.22.3.a.m: When they come together towards the north, the adhvaryu places a stone as an enclosing stick south of them, [saying]: "This enclosing stick I place for the living, that no other of them may go to this side now.

14.22.3.b.s: śataṃ jīvantu śaradaḥ purūcīstiro mṛtyuṃ dadhmahe parvateneti
14.22.3.b.d: शतं जीवन्तु शरदः पुरूचीस्तिरो मृत्युं दध्महे पर्वतेनेति
14.22.3.b.m: May they live a hundred full autumns; we put death away by means of the mountain."

14.22.4.a.m: The soma sacrifice is an agniṣṭoma, beginning with the Aindravāyava draught or beginning with the Maitrāvaruṇa draught.

14.22.6.a.m: At each stotra he places the bone-urn down.

14.22.7.a.m: They pour out their portions on the mārjālīya.

14.22.8.a.s: agna āyūṃṣi pavasa iti pratipadaṃ kurvīran
14.22.8.a.d: अग्न आयूंषि पवस इति प्रतिपदं कुर्वीरन्
14.22.8.a.m: They should make "Agni, you purify our life-spans" the opening verse.

14.22.9.a.m: Their soma sacrifice should have the Rathaṃtara as its sāman.

14.22.10.a.d: आयुरेवात्मन्दधते ऽथो पाप्मानमेव विजहतो यन्तीति विज्ञायते
14.22.10.a.m: "They bestow life in themselves, and they proceed casting away evil"—so it is known [from the brāhmaṇa].

14.22.11.a.s: yadyu vai nāthavānsyāddagdhvainaṃ kṛṣṇājine 'sthīnyupanahya idhāya yo 'sya svo nediṣṭhī syāttatsthāne taṃ dīkṣayitvā tena saha yajamānā āsīran
14.22.11.a.d: यद्यु वै नाथवान्स्याद्दग्ध्वैनं कृष्णाजिने ऽस्थीन्युपनह्य इधाय यो ऽस्य स्वो नेदिष्ठी स्यात्तत्स्थाने तं दीक्षयित्वा तेन सह यजमाना आसीरन्
14.22.11.a.m: If, however, he had a protector, having burned him, bound the bones in a black antelope skin, and placed it on a seat, having consecrated in his place whoever is his nearest relative, they should remain as sacrificers together with him.

14.22.12.a.m: After a year, they should cause the bones to sacrifice.

14.22.13.b.m: "From the concluding offering onward," says Ālekhana.

14.22.14.a.m: The rules beginning with "The soma sacrifice is an agniṣṭoma" [apply].

14.22.15.a.m: As before, the sacrificial gifts are one hundred and twelve.

14.23.1.a.s: yadi sattrāyāgūrya na yajeta viśvajitātirātreṇa sarvapṛṣṭhena sarvastomena sarvavedasadakṣiṇena yajeta
14.23.1.a.d: यदि सत्त्रायागूर्य न यजेत विश्वजितातिरात्रेण सर्वपृष्ठेन सर्वस्तोमेन सर्ववेदसदक्षिणेन यजेत
14.23.1.a.m: If, having undertaken a sattra, he should not sacrifice, he should sacrifice with a Viśvajit Atirātra having all the pṛṣṭhas, having all the stomas, and with all his property as the sacrificial gift.

14.23.2.a.m: Some teach the Traidhātavīyā sacrifice with a thousand [cows] as the sacrificial gift.

14.23.3.a.s: sattre dīkṣitvā yadi sāmyuttiṣṭhāset somam apabhajya viśvajitātirātreṇa pūrvavad yajeta
14.23.3.a.d: सत्त्रे दीक्षित्वा यदि साम्युत्तिष्ठासेत् सोमम् अपभज्य विश्वजितातिरात्रेण पूर्ववद् यजेत
14.23.3.a.m: If, having been consecrated in a sattra, he should wish to leave midway, having assigned his share of soma, he should sacrifice with a Viśvajit Atirātra as before.

14.23.4.a.s: yadi dīkṣāsūttiṣṭhāsed avalikhyokhāyāstairanyāṃ mṛdaṃ saṃsṛjyokhāṃ kārayet
14.23.4.a.d: यदि दीक्षासूत्तिष्ठासेद् अवलिख्योखायास्तैरन्यां मृदं संसृज्योखां कारयेत्
14.23.4.a.m: If he should wish to leave during the consecration days, having scraped from the ukhā pot, having mixed that [clay] with other clay, he should have an ukhā pot made.

14.23.5.a.m: Having scraped [the clay] of the animal heads, he should attach it silently.

14.23.6.a.s: yadyupasatsu yā citā citiḥ syānna tāmāvartayet
14.23.6.a.d: यद्युपसत्सु या चिता चितिः स्यान्न तामावर्तयेत्
14.23.6.a.m: If [he leaves] during the upasads, whatever layer has been piled, he should not repeat it.

14.23.9.a.m: If he leaves when the fire altar has been piled, there is no piling of the fire altar.

14.23.10.a.m: When the fire has been brought forward, he should bring another forward silently.

14.23.11.a.m: He should take from the structures: from the great altar ground, the high altar, the dhiṣṇyas, the sounding-holes, the khara, the sadas, and the havirdhāna sheds.

14.23.11.b.m: He should also procure them in the other [cases].

14.23.12.a.m: If the dawn should break upon him before the chanting of all the night rounds, they should chant six [verses] addressed to Indra and Viṣṇu for the hotṛ,

14.23.12.b.m: and three each for the others.

14.23.13.a.s: yadi dvābhyāṃ hotre maitrāvaruṇāya ca pūrvasmin paryāye stuyuḥ /
14.23.13.a.d: यदि द्वाभ्यां होत्रे मैत्रावरुणाय च पूर्वस्मिन् पर्याये स्तुयुः ।
14.23.13.a.m: If [the dawn breaks] after two [rounds have been chanted], they should chant for the hotṛ and the Maitrāvaruṇa in the previous round,

14.23.13.b.m: and for the Brāhmaṇācchaṃsin and the Acchāvāka in the subsequent [round].

14.23.14.a.m: If [it breaks] after one [round], they should chant fifteen [verses] for the hotṛ,

14.23.14.b.m: and five each for the others.

14.23.15.a.m: He should prescribe "Agni, the shining dawns" as the opening verse of the Āśvina recitation.

14.24.1.a.s: yasyāśvine śasyamāne sūryo nāvirbhavati sauryaṃ bahurūpamālabheta
14.24.1.a.d: यस्याश्विने शस्यमाने सूर्यो नाविर्भवति सौर्यं बहुरूपमालभेत
14.24.1.a.m: He for whom the sun does not appear while the Āśvina recitation is being recited should seize a many-colored [victim] sacred to Sūrya.

14.24.2.a.m: He may also recite all the ten-book [verses of the Ṛgveda].

14.24.3.a.s: yeṣāṃ dīkṣitānām āhavanīya udvāyed āgnīdhrād uddharet /
14.24.3.a.d: येषां दीक्षितानाम् आहवनीय उद्वायेद् आग्नीध्राद् उद्धरेत् ।
14.24.3.a.m: If the āhavanīya fire of consecrated persons should go out, he should bring [fire] out from the āgnīdhra;

14.24.3.b.m: if the āgnīdhra [goes out], from the gārhapatya;

14.24.3.c.m: if the gārhapatya [goes out], he should churn it out anew from this very place.

14.24.4.a.m: From whatever piece of wood it went out, he should make churning-sticks of it.

14.24.6.a.m: He should give four choice gifts to the principal priests.

14.24.7.a.s: yasya soma upadasyetsuvarṇaṃ hiraṇyaṃ dvedhā vicchidyārdhamantardhāyarjīṣeṇa sahābhiṣuṇuyāt /
14.24.7.a.d: यस्य सोम उपदस्येत्सुवर्णं हिरण्यं द्वेधा विच्छिद्यार्धमन्तर्धायर्जीषेण सहाभिषुणुयात् ।
14.24.7.a.m: If one's soma should run short, having cut a piece of gold in two and placed one half within, he should press it together with the soma dregs,

14.24.7.b.m: and having drawn out the other half, they should proceed with the draughts.

14.24.8.a.m: He should give four choice gifts to the principal priests.

14.24.9.a.m: If they should steal someone's soma before it is bought, he should simply buy [more].

14.24.10.a.s: yadi krītaṃ yo nediṣṭhī syāttata āhṛtyābhiṣuṇuyāt
14.24.10.a.d: यदि क्रीतं यो नेदिष्ठी स्यात्तत आहृत्याभिषुणुयात्
14.24.10.a.m: If it was already bought, having fetched [more] from wherever is nearest, he should press it.

14.24.11.a.m: He should give to the soma-fetcher or to the soma-seller according to his faith.

14.24.12.a.m: In the absence of soma, he should press pūtīka plants.

14.24.12.b.s: pūtīkābhāva ādārānphālgunāni ca yāni śvetatūlāni syuḥ /
14.24.12.b.d: पूतीकाभाव आदारान्फाल्गुनानि च यानि श्वेततूलानि स्युः ।
14.24.12.b.m: In the absence of pūtīka [plants], [he should press] ādāra [plants] and phālguna [grasses] that have white tufts.

14.24.12.c.s: tadabhāve yāḥ kāścauṣadhīḥ kṣīriṇīraruṇadūrvāḥ kuśānvā haritāniti vājasaneyakam
14.24.12.c.d: तदभावे याः काश्चौषधीः क्षीरिणीररुणदूर्वाः कुशान्वा हरितानिति वाजसनेयकम्
14.24.12.c.m: "In their absence, whatever milky herbs [are available], reddish dūrvā grass, or green kuśa grass," thus says the Vājasaneyaka.

14.24.14.a.m: At the morning pressing, he should mix all the soma draughts with fresh, unboiled milk.

14.24.14.b.m: At the midday pressing, with boiled [milk].

14.24.14.c.m: At the third pressing, with curd, or with [curd] mixed with water.

14.24.15.b.m: At the morning pressing, both fresh milk and pūtīkas;

14.24.15.c.m: at the midday pressing, both boiled milk and pūtīkas;

14.24.15.d.m: and at the third pressing, both curd and pūtīkas.

14.24.16.a.m: The soma [sacrifice] should be an Agniṣṭoma having the Rathaṃtara as chant.

14.24.17.a.s: ya evartvijo vṛtāḥ syusta enaṃ yājayeyuḥ
14.24.17.a.d: य एवर्त्विजो वृताः स्युस्त एनं याजयेयुः
14.24.17.a.m: The very priests who were chosen should perform the sacrifice for him.

14.24.18.a.m: He should give only a single cow as sacrificial gift to them.

14.24.20.a.m: Having come up from the final bath, he should consecrate himself again for that same rite before the twelfth [day].

14.24.21.a.m: There he should give whatever he was going to give at the previous [sacrifice].

14.25.1.a.m: If the sadas and the havirdhāna sheds should burn down, the adhvaryu should mentally supervise the draughts,

14.25.2.a.s: anabhidagdhe some parśvato devayajanamadhyavasāya kṛtāntādeva prakrāmeyuḥ
14.25.2.a.d: अनभिदग्धे सोमे पर्श्वतो देवयजनमध्यवसाय कृतान्तादेव प्रक्रामेयुः
14.25.2.a.m: If the soma has not burned, having settled on a sacrificial place to the side, they should proceed right from the point completed.

14.25.3.a.m: If it has burned, however, that expiation applies which [is prescribed] when [the soma] is carried off.

14.25.4.a.m: In place of the cow, he should give five cows,

14.25.5.a.m: If at the morning pressing he cannot find a pressing stone, having brought a stick of palāśa wood, he should press with that alone.

14.25.5.b.m: "This indeed is its expiation," so it is known.

14.25.6.a.m: If at the midday [pressing], if at the third pressing, the very same [applies].

14.25.7.a.s: yadi prātaḥsavane grāvā śīryeta purastādbahiṣpavamānāddyutānasya mārutasya brahmasāmnā stuvīran
14.25.7.a.d: यदि प्रातःसवने ग्रावा शीर्येत पुरस्ताद्बहिष्पवमानाद्द्युतानस्य मारुतस्य ब्रह्मसाम्ना स्तुवीरन्
14.25.7.a.m: If at the morning pressing a pressing stone breaks, before the Bahiṣpavamāna chant they should chant with the Brahmasāman of Dyutāna Māruta.

14.25.9.a.s: yadi mādhyaṃdine yadi tṛtīyasavana etadeva purastātpavamānebhyaḥ stuvate
14.25.9.a.d: यदि माध्यंदिने यदि तृतीयसवन एतदेव पुरस्तात्पवमानेभ्यः स्तुवते
14.25.9.a.m: If at the midday [pressing], if at the third pressing, they chant the very same before the pavamāna chants.

14.25.10.a.s: yadi prataḥsavane kalaśo dīryeta vaiṣṇavīsu śipiviṣṭavatīṣvityuktam
14.25.10.a.d: यदि प्रतःसवने कलशो दीर्येत वैष्णवीसु शिपिविष्टवतीष्वित्युक्तम्
14.25.10.a.m: If at the morning pressing a vat breaks, it has been said: "On [verses] addressed to Viṣṇu containing the word śipiviṣṭa."

14.25.11.b.s: yadi prātaḥsavane kalaśo dīryeta vaṣaṭkāranidhanaṃ brahmasāma kuryāditi /
14.25.11.b.d: यदि प्रातःसवने कलशो दीर्येत वषट्कारनिधनं ब्रह्मसाम कुर्यादिति ।
14.25.11.b.m: "If at the morning pressing a vat breaks, he should make the Brahmasāman have the vaṣaṭ-call as its final part."

14.25.11.c.s: asave svāhā vasave svāhā vibhuve svāhā vivasvate svāhā śūṣāya svāhā sūryāya svāhā candrāya svāhā gaṇaśriye svāhāmalimluce svāhā jyotiṣe svāhābhibhuve svāhādhipataye svāhā divāṃ pataye svāheti trayodaśājyāhutīrhutvā
14.25.11.c.d: असवे स्वाहा वसवे स्वाहा विभुवे स्वाहा विवस्वते स्वाहा शूषाय स्वाहा सूर्याय स्वाहा चन्द्राय स्वाहा गणश्रिये स्वाहामलिम्लुचे स्वाहा ज्योतिषे स्वाहाभिभुवे स्वाहाधिपतये स्वाहा दिवां पतये स्वाहेति त्रयोदशाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा
14.25.11.c.m: Having offered thirteen clarified butter oblations with: "To breath svāhā! To wealth svāhā! To the all-pervading svāhā! To the shining one svāhā! To impetuosity svāhā! To the sun svāhā! To the moon svāhā! To the glory of the host svāhā! To the intercalary month svāhā! To light svāhā! To the conqueror svāhā! To the overlord svāhā! To the lord of days svāhā!"—

14.26.1.a.s: indrasya graho 'syagṛhīto grāhyo devānāṃ pūrasi taṃ tvā prapadye saha grahaiḥ saha pragrahaiḥ saha prajayā saha paśubhiḥ sahartvigbhyaḥ saha somyaiḥ saha sadasyaiḥ saha dākṣiṇeyaiḥ saha yajñena saha yajñapatinā //
14.26.1.a.d: इन्द्रस्य ग्रहो ऽस्यगृहीतो ग्राह्यो देवानां पूरसि तं त्वा प्रपद्ये सह ग्रहैः सह प्रग्रहैः सह प्रजया सह पशुभिः सहर्त्विग्भ्यः सह सोम्यैः सह सदस्यैः सह दाक्षिणेयैः सह यज्ञेन सह यज्ञपतिना ॥
14.26.1.a.m: "You are Indra's draught, unseized, to be seized; you are the citadel of the gods. To you, as such, I resort, together with the draughts, together with the preliminary draughts, together with offspring, together with cattle, together with the priests, together with those worthy of soma, together with the sadas-sitters, together with those worthy of gifts, together with the sacrifice, together with the lord of sacrifice.

14.26.1.b.s: indrāgnī paridhī mama vāto devapurā mama /
14.26.1.b.d: इन्द्राग्नी परिधी मम वातो देवपुरा मम ।
14.26.1.b.m: Indra and Agni are my enclosing sticks, the wind is my divine stronghold;

14.26.1.c.s: brahma varma mamāntaraṃ taṃ tvendragraha prapadye saguḥ saśvaḥ //
14.26.1.c.d: ब्रह्म वर्म ममान्तरं तं त्वेन्द्रग्रह प्रपद्ये सगुः सश्वः ॥
14.26.1.c.m: the sacred word is my inner armor; to you, as such, O Indra-draught, I resort, with cows, with horses.

14.26.1.d.m: Armor to me are Heaven and Earth, armor is Agni, armor the Sun;

14.26.1.e.s: varma me brahmaṇaspatirmā mā prāpadato bhayam //
14.26.1.e.d: वर्म मे ब्रह्मणस्पतिर्मा मा प्रापदतो भयम् ॥
14.26.1.e.m: armor to me is Brahmaṇaspati; may fear not reach me from this.

14.26.1.f.s: indrāgnī paridhī mama vāto devapurā mama /
14.26.1.f.d: इन्द्राग्नी परिधी मम वातो देवपुरा मम ।
14.26.1.f.m: Indra and Agni are my enclosing sticks, the wind is my divine stronghold;

14.26.1.g.s: brahma varma mamāntaraṃ taṃ tvendragraha praviśāni saguḥ sāśvaḥ sapūruṣaḥ /
14.26.1.g.d: ब्रह्म वर्म ममान्तरं तं त्वेन्द्रग्रह प्रविशानि सगुः साश्वः सपूरुषः ।
14.26.1.g.m: the sacred word is my inner armor; into you, as such, O Indra-draught, may I enter, with cows, with horses, with men,

14.26.1.h.s: saha yanme asti teneti dīrṇaṃ yajamāno 'numantrayate
14.26.1.h.d: सह यन्मे अस्ति तेनेति दीर्णं यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
14.26.1.h.m: together with whatever is mine"—with these words the sacrificer addresses the broken [vat].

14.26.2.a.s: ariṣṭyā avyathyai saṃveśāyopaveśāya gāyatryā abhibhūtyai svāhā /
14.26.2.a.d: अरिष्ट्या अव्यथ्यै संवेशायोपवेशाय गायत्र्या अभिभूत्यै स्वाहा ।
14.26.2.a.m: "For non-injury, for unshakableness, for lying down, for sitting down, for the overcoming power of the Gāyatrī, svāhā!

14.26.2.b.d: अरिष्ट्या अव्यथ्यै संवेशायोपवेशाय त्रिष्टुभो ऽभिभूत्यै स्वाहा ।
14.26.2.b.m: For non-injury, for unshakableness, for lying down, for sitting down, for the overcoming power of the Triṣṭubh, svāhā!

14.26.2.c.s: ariṣṭyā avyathyai saṃveśāyopaveśāya jagatyā abhibhūtyai svāhā /
14.26.2.c.d: अरिष्ट्या अव्यथ्यै संवेशायोपवेशाय जगत्या अभिभूत्यै स्वाहा ।
14.26.2.c.m: For non-injury, for unshakableness, for lying down, for sitting down, for the overcoming power of the Jagatī, svāhā!

14.26.2.d.m: For non-injury, for unshakableness, for lying down, for sitting down, for the overcoming power of the Anuṣṭubh, svāhā!

14.26.2.e.s: ariṣṭyā avyathyai saṃveśāyopaveśāya paṅktyā abhibhūtyai svāhetyetaiḥ pratimantramanusavanaṃ dīrṇe pañcāhutīrjuhotītyeke
14.26.2.e.d: अरिष्ट्या अव्यथ्यै संवेशायोपवेशाय पङ्क्त्या अभिभूत्यै स्वाहेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रमनुसवनं दीर्णे पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोतीत्येके
14.26.2.e.m: For non-injury, for unshakableness, for lying down, for sitting down, for the overcoming power of the Paṅkti, svāhā!"—some say that with these, verse by verse, at each pressing when [a vat] is broken, he offers five oblations.

14.26.3.a.s: yadi bahiṣpavamānaṃ sarpatāṃ prastotāpacchidyeta yajñasya śiraśchidyeta /
14.26.3.a.d: यदि बहिष्पवमानं सर्पतां प्रस्तोतापच्छिद्येत यज्ञस्य शिरश्छिद्येत ।
14.26.3.a.m: If while they are gliding to the Bahiṣpavamāna the prastotṛ should break away, the head of the sacrifice would be cut off.

14.26.3.b.s: brahmaṇe varaṃ dattvā sa eva punarvartavyaḥ
14.26.3.b.d: ब्रह्मणे वरं दत्त्वा स एव पुनर्वर्तव्यः
14.26.3.b.m: Having given a boon to the brahman, he alone must be chosen again.

14.26.4.a.m: If the pratihartṛ [breaks away], the sacrificer would be deprived of cattle.

14.26.5.a.m: If the udgātṛ [breaks away], the sacrificer would be deprived of the sacrifice.

14.26.5.b.m: That sacrifice should be completed without sacrificial gifts.

14.26.6.a.m: There he should give whatever he was going to give at the former [sacrifice].

14.26.7.a.m: In the case of a simultaneous breaking away, however, the udgātṛ's expiation [applies], and the general expiation for the pratihartṛ.

14.26.8.a.d: पूर्वापरापच्छेदे यो जघन्यो ऽपच्छिद्येत तस्य प्रायश्चित्तम्
14.26.8.a.m: In the case of breaking away one after another, the expiation belongs to whoever breaks away last.

14.26.9.a.m: If at the midday [pavamāna], the very same [applies].

14.26.9.b.m: If at the Ārbhava [pavamāna], he should offer the general expiation.

14.27.1.a.s: yatkalaśa upadasyetsuvarṇaṃ hiraṇyaṃ dvedhā vicchidyādhamantardhāyāpo 'vanīya payo 'bhyavanayet /
14.27.1.a.d: यत्कलश उपदस्येत्सुवर्णं हिरण्यं द्वेधा विच्छिद्याधमन्तर्धायापो ऽवनीय पयो ऽभ्यवनयेत् ।
14.27.1.a.m: If [the soma] in the vat should fail, having cut a piece of gold in two and having put half inside, having poured water, he should pour milk into it.

14.27.1.b.m: Drawing up half, they should proceed with the draughts.

14.27.2.a.m: He should give four choice gifts to the great priests.

14.27.3.b.m: If the jar should run short, he should draw [soma] from the āgrayaṇa [vessel].

14.27.4.a.m: If a draught or the jar should run short, he should draw from the āgrayaṇa, except for the śukra and the dhruva.

14.27.5.a.s: droṇakalśādgṛhyanta iti sarvagrahāṇāṃ skannānāmupadastānāṃ ca vijñāyate
14.27.5.a.d: द्रोणकल्शाद्गृह्यन्त इति सर्वग्रहाणां स्कन्नानामुपदस्तानां च विज्ञायते
14.27.5.a.m: It is known [from a Brāhmaṇa]: 'They are drawn from the droṇakalaśa,' regarding all draughts that have spilled or run short.

14.27.6.a.s: yaddhruva upadasyetskandeddīryeta vā tamabhimantrayetāyurdhā asi dhruvāyurme dhehi /
14.27.6.a.d: यद्ध्रुव उपदस्येत्स्कन्देद्दीर्येत वा तमभिमन्त्रयेतायुर्धा असि ध्रुवायुर्मे धेहि ।
14.27.6.a.m: If the dhruva should run short, spill, or crack, he should address it: 'You are the giver of life, O dhruva; bestow life upon me.

14.27.6.b.s: varcodhā asi dhruva varco me dhehi /
14.27.6.b.d: वर्चोधा असि ध्रुव वर्चो मे धेहि ।
14.27.6.b.m: You are the giver of splendor, O dhruva; bestow splendor upon me.

14.27.6.c.s: tanūpā asi dhruva tanvaṃ me pāhīti //
14.27.6.c.d: तनूपा असि ध्रुव तन्वं मे पाहीति ॥
14.27.6.c.m: You are the protector of the body, O dhruva; protect my body.'

14.27.6.d.s: tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyamavadhāya svāhā diva āpyāyasva svāhāntarikṣādāpyāyasva svāhā pṛthivyā āpyāyasvetyāpyāyayati
14.27.6.d.d: तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यमवधाय स्वाहा दिव आप्यायस्व स्वाहान्तरिक्षादाप्यायस्व स्वाहा पृथिव्या आप्यायस्वेत्याप्याययति
14.27.6.d.m: Having placed a piece of gold of one hundred mānas weight into it, he swells it with: 'Svāhā! Swell from heaven; svāhā! swell from the intermediate space; svāhā! swell from the earth.'

14.27.7.a.s: adhvaro 'yaṃ yajño astu devā oṣadhībhyaḥ paśubhyo me dhanāya /
14.27.7.a.d: अध्वरो ऽयं यज्ञो अस्तु देवा ओषधीभ्यः पशुभ्यो मे धनाय ।
14.27.7.a.m: 'May this sacrifice be free from injury, O gods, for the plants, for the cattle, and for my wealth.

14.27.7.b.m: May it be free from injury for every creature, O gods;

14.27.7.c.m: O divine sacrifice, swell rich in ghee.

14.27.7.d.m: Be right here, do not waver, unshakeable like a mountain.

14.27.7.e.m: Stand firm here like Indra, sustain the sacrifice here.

14.27.7.f.m: Indra has sustained this firm one with the firm oblation;

14.27.7.g.m: to him the gods have spoken in favor, and this Brahmaṇaspati.

14.27.7.h.s: dhruvā dyaurdhruvā pṛthivī dhrvaṃ viśvamidaṃ jagat /
14.27.7.h.d: ध्रुवा द्यौर्ध्रुवा पृथिवी ध्र्वं विश्वमिदं जगत् ।
14.27.7.h.m: Firm is heaven, firm is the earth, firm is this entire world;

14.27.7.i.s: dhruvā ha parvatā ime dhruvo rājā viśāmayamityetābhiścatasṛbhiḥ sannamabhimantrya varaṃ dadāti
14.27.7.i.d: ध्रुवा ह पर्वता इमे ध्रुवो राजा विशामयमित्येताभिश्चतसृभिः सन्नमभिमन्त्र्य वरं ददाति
14.27.7.i.m: firm indeed are these mountains; firm is this king of the subjects'—having addressed it when set down with these four [verses], he gives a choice gift.

14.28.1.a.s: yadi nārāśaṃsa upadasyedyamadhvaryuḥ pūrvaṃ grahaṃ gṛhṇīyāttaṃ vaṣaṭkṛtānuvaṣaṭkṛte hutvā camasādhvaryave prayacchet /
14.28.1.a.d: यदि नाराशंस उपदस्येद्यमध्वर्युः पूर्वं ग्रहं गृह्णीयात्तं वषट्कृतानुवषट्कृते हुत्वा चमसाध्वर्यवे प्रयच्छेत् ।
14.28.1.a.m: If the nārāśaṃsa [goblet] should run short, whichever draught the adhvaryu drew previously, having offered it at the vaṣaṭ-call and after-vaṣaṭ-call, he should hand it over to the camasādhvaryu.

14.28.1.b.s: tenainaṃ sa āpyāyayatyāpyāyasva sametu ta iti
14.28.1.b.d: तेनैनं स आप्याययत्याप्यायस्व समेतु त इति
14.28.1.b.m: With that, he swells it: 'Swell, let [the soma] unite with you…'

14.28.2.a.s: yadi prātaḥsavane somo havirvā skandenmādhyaṃdine tṛtīyasavane naktaṃ tiroahnyeṣu vā devāṃ janamaganyajña ityetairyathāpūrvamabhimantrya mano jyotirjuṣatāmityāhutiṃ juhuyāt
14.28.2.a.d: यदि प्रातःसवने सोमो हविर्वा स्कन्देन्माध्यंदिने तृतीयसवने नक्तं तिरोअह्न्येषु वा देवां जनमगन्यज्ञ इत्येतैर्यथापूर्वमभिमन्त्र्य मनो ज्योतिर्जुषतामित्याहुतिं जुहुयात्
14.28.2.a.m: If soma or an oblation should spill at the morning pressing, the midday [pressing], the third pressing, at night, or during the overnight [rounds], having addressed it respectively with: 'The sacrifice has gone to the divine folk…,' he should offer an oblation with: 'May the Mind enjoy the light…'

14.28.3.e.s: yaste drapsa ityetaiḥ pratimantramanusavanaṃ skanne pañcāhutīrjuhotītyeke
14.28.3.e.d: यस्ते द्रप्स इत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रमनुसवनं स्कन्ने पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोतीत्येके
14.28.3.e.m: 'Whatever drop of yours…'—with these [verses], one per formula, whenever [soma] has spilled at each pressing, he offers five oblations, say some [teachers].

14.28.4.a.s: yadṛtugrahaiḥ pracarantau muhyeyātāṃ visṛṣṭadhenāḥ sarito ghṛtaścuto vasanto grīṣmo madhumanti varṣāḥ /
14.28.4.a.d: यदृतुग्रहैः प्रचरन्तौ मुह्येयातां विसृष्टधेनाः सरितो घृतश्चुतो वसन्तो ग्रीष्मो मधुमन्ति वर्षाः ।
14.28.4.a.m: If the two performing with the season-draughts should become confused: 'The streams flowing with milk, dripping with ghee; spring, summer, the rainy season bearing sweetness;

14.28.4.b.s: śaraddhemanta ṛtavo mayobhuva udapruto nabhasī saṃvasantām //
14.28.4.b.d: शरद्धेमन्त ऋतवो मयोभुव उदप्रुतो नभसी संवसन्ताम् ॥
14.28.4.b.m: autumn, winter, the seasons bringing joy, water-bearing, let them dwell together in the two worlds.

14.28.4.c.s: ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatirdhātā dadātu sumanasyamānaḥ /
14.28.4.c.d: आ नः प्रजां जनयतु प्रजापतिर्धाता ददातु सुमनस्यमानः ।
14.28.4.c.m: May Prajāpati produce offspring for us; may Dhātṛ, well-disposed, grant [it];

14.28.4.d.m: may the Year, harmonizing with the seasons, the lord of nourishment, bestow nourishment upon me.'

14.28.4.h.m: 'Madhu and…'—with these, formula by formula, he offers.

14.28.5.a.s: ta imaṃ yajñamavantu te māmavantvanu va ārabhe 'nu mārabhadhvaṃ svāhetyṛtunāmasvanuṣajati
14.28.5.a.d: त इमं यज्ञमवन्तु ते मामवन्त्वनु व आरभे ऽनु मारभध्वं स्वाहेत्यृतुनामस्वनुषजति
14.28.5.a.m: He attaches to the names of the seasons: 'May they favor this sacrifice, may they favor me; I take hold of you, do you take hold of me, svāhā!'

14.28.6.a.s: yadi somaḥ skandedbrahmansomo 'skānityuktvābhūddevaḥ savitā vandyo nu na ityabhimantrya bhūpataye svāheti pañca prādeśānmimīte yathā purastāt
14.28.6.a.d: यदि सोमः स्कन्देद्ब्रह्मन्सोमो ऽस्कानित्युक्त्वाभूद्देवः सविता वन्द्यो नु न इत्यभिमन्त्र्य भूपतये स्वाहेति पञ्च प्रादेशान्मिमीते यथा पुरस्तात्
14.28.6.a.m: If soma should spill, having said: 'O Brahman, the soma has spilled,' and having addressed it with: 'The divine Savitṛ has become worthy of our praise…,' he measures five span-lengths with: 'To the lord of the earth, svāhā,' as before.

14.29.1.a.s: yadi camasamabhakṣitaṃ stotreṇābhyupākuryādāramatetyuktvota tyā no divā matiraditirūtyāgamat /
14.29.1.a.d: यदि चमसमभक्षितं स्तोत्रेणाभ्युपाकुर्यादारमतेत्युक्त्वोत त्या नो दिवा मतिरदितिरूत्यागमत् ।
14.29.1.a.m: If he should initiate the chant while a goblet has not been partaken of, having said: 'Stop,' and with: 'And may that divine thought, Aditi, come to us with aid;

14.29.1.b.m: may she, favorable, bring joy, [warding] off hostilities.

14.29.1.c.s: uta tyā daivyā bhiṣajā śaṃ naskarato aśvinā /
14.29.1.c.d: उत त्या दैव्या भिषजा शं नस्करतो अश्विना ।
14.29.1.c.m: And may those two divine physicians, the Aśvins, bring us blessing;

14.29.1.d.m: may you drive away affliction from us, [warding] off hostilities.

14.29.1.e.m: May Agni with his fires bring us blessing; may the Sun shine warmly upon us;

14.29.1.f.s: śaṃ vato vātvarapā apa sridha iti tisra āgnīdhrīye hutvā taṃ sadasi bhakṣayitvottaravāsasā pracchādya dakṣiṇāṃ dvārbāhumanu nirgṛtya mārjālīye prakṣālya pūrvayātihṛtya taditpadaṃ na viciketa vidvānyanmṛtaḥ punarapyeti jīvan /
14.29.1.f.d: शं वतो वात्वरपा अप स्रिध इति तिस्र आग्नीध्रीये हुत्वा तं सदसि भक्षयित्वोत्तरवाससा प्रच्छाद्य दक्षिणां द्वार्बाहुमनु निर्गृत्य मार्जालीये प्रक्षाल्य पूर्वयातिहृत्य तदित्पदं न विचिकेत विद्वान्यन्मृतः पुनरप्येति जीवन् ।
14.29.1.f.m: may the wind blow blessing to us, free from disease, [warding] off hostilities'—having offered three [oblations] in the Āgnīdhra fire, having partaken of it in the sadas, having covered it with an upper cloth, having taken it out along the south doorpost, having washed it at the mārjālīya fire, having brought it forward through the eastern door, with: 'That footprint the wise man did not discern, when dying he comes back again living;

14.29.1.g.s: trivṛdyadbhuvanasya rathavṛjjīvo garbho na mṛtaḥ sa jīvāditi taṃ camaseṣvapisṛjya hiraṇyagarbhaḥ samavartatāgra ityāhutiṃ hutvāpyāyasva madintama soma viśvābhirūtibhiḥ /
14.29.1.g.d: त्रिवृद्यद्भुवनस्य रथवृज्जीवो गर्भो न मृतः स जीवादिति तं चमसेष्वपिसृज्य हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्र इत्याहुतिं हुत्वाप्यायस्व मदिन्तम सोम विश्वाभिरूतिभिः ।
14.29.1.g.m: the threefold rolling wheel of the world; living, an embryo, not dead, he lives'—having mixed it into the goblets, having offered an oblation with: 'In the beginning the Golden Embryo arose…,' he swells it with: 'Swell, O most exhilarating Soma, with all your aids;

14.29.2.a.m: 'Bring [it] back for this one who desires to drink, who knows everything,

14.29.2.b.d: अरंगमाय जग्मवे ऽपश्चादृघ्वने नर इत्यववृष्टं भक्षमभिमन्त्र्येन्दुरिन्दुमवागादिन्दोरिन्द्रो ऽपात् ।
14.29.2.b.m: who goes swiftly, who runs fast, who goes forward, O men'—having addressed the portion rained upon, he partakes of it with: 'Indu has approached Indu; Indra has drunk of Indu.

14.29.2.c.s: tasya ta indavindrapītasya madhumata upahūtasyopahūto bhakṣayāmīti bhakṣayati
14.29.2.c.d: तस्य त इन्दविन्द्रपीतस्य मधुमत उपहूतस्योपहूतो भक्षयामीति भक्षयति
14.29.2.c.m: Of that sweet [drop] of yours, O Indu, drunk by Indra, invited, invited I partake.'

14.29.3.a.m: If the consecrated one should emit semen: 'O Agni, in the waters…'—this is [the verse].

14.29.3.b.s: tapo ṣvagne antarām̐ amitrāṃstapā śaṃsamararuṣaḥ parasya /
14.29.3.b.d: तपो ष्वग्ने अन्तराम्̐ अमित्रांस्तपा शंसमररुषः परस्य ।
14.29.3.b.m: 'Burn thoroughly, O Agni, the enemies near at hand; burn the praise of the hostile stranger;

14.29.3.c.s: tapā vaso cikitāno acittānvi te tiṣṭhantāmajarā ayāsaḥ //
14.29.3.c.d: तपा वसो चिकितानो अचित्तान्वि ते तिष्ठन्तामजरा अयासः ॥
14.29.3.c.m: burn, O Vasu, discerning the undiscerning; let your unaging, unwearying flames stand spread out.

14.29.3.d.s: yo naḥ sanutyo abhidāsadagne yo antaro mitramaho vanuṣyāt /
14.29.3.d.d: यो नः सनुत्यो अभिदासदग्ने यो अन्तरो मित्रमहो वनुष्यात् ।
14.29.3.d.m: Whoever, secret, would assault us, O Agni, or whoever near, O friend-cherished one, would seek to harm us—

14.29.3.e.m: burn him with your unaging, self-powering bulls; burn, fiery one, with heat, O most burning one.

14.29.3.f.s: sa saṃ kṛṇotu ketumā naktaṃ ciddūra ā sate /
14.29.3.f.d: स सं कृणोतु केतुमा नक्तं चिद्दूर आ सते ।
14.29.3.f.m: May he make a banner even at night for one who sits far off,

14.29.3.g.m: when the unaging purifier consumes the forest trees.

14.29.3.h.s: nahi te agne tanuvai krūramānāśa martyaḥ /
14.29.3.h.d: नहि ते अग्ने तनुवै क्रूरमानाश मर्त्यः ।
14.29.3.h.m: Indeed, O Agni, no mortal has reached harsh injury upon your body;

14.29.3.i.m: the brown monkey [swallowed] its own dart, like a cow [her own] afterbirth.

14.29.3.j.s: meṣa iva yadupa ca vi ca carvari yadapsararūparasya khādati /
14.29.3.j.d: मेष इव यदुप च वि च चर्वरि यदप्सररूपरस्य खादति ।
14.29.3.j.m: When like a ram he moves around and through, when in the water he eats the tail-end of the water-folk,

14.29.3.k.s: śīrṣṇā girau vakṣasā vakṣa ejayannaṃśuṃ gabhasti haritebhirāsabhiriti ṣaṭ pūrṇāhutīrhutvā pratyāhuti varāndadyāt
14.29.3.k.d: शीर्ष्णा गिरौ वक्षसा वक्ष एजयन्नंशुं गभस्ति हरितेभिरासभिरिति षट् पूर्णाहुतीर्हुत्वा प्रत्याहुति वरान्दद्यात्
14.29.3.k.m: with his head on the mountain, shaking his chest with his chest, [he holds] the soma stalk in his hand with tawny mouths'—having offered six full oblations [with these verses], he should give choice gifts at each oblation.

14.30.1.a.s: yaddevā devaheḍanamiti vā daśāhutīrhutvā pavamānaḥ suvarjana ityetenānuvākenābhiṣiñcet
14.30.1.a.d: यद्देवा देवहेडनमिति वा दशाहुतीर्हुत्वा पवमानः सुवर्जन इत्येतेनानुवाकेनाभिषिञ्चेत्
14.30.1.a.m: Or having offered ten oblations with: 'Whatever offense against the gods, O gods…,' he should sprinkle him with the anuvāka beginning with: 'The purifying, light-bringing [one]…'

14.30.2.a.s: yadi hutāhutau somau saṃsṛjyeyātāmantaḥparidhyaṅgāraṃ nirvartya yajñasya hi stha ṛtviyāvindrāgnī cetanasya ca /
14.30.2.a.d: यदि हुताहुतौ सोमौ संसृज्येयातामन्तःपरिध्यङ्गारं निर्वर्त्य यज्ञस्य हि स्थ ऋत्वियाविन्द्राग्नी चेतनस्य च ।
14.30.2.a.m: If offered and unoffered soma should become mixed together, after pulling out a burning ember inside the enclosing sticks, with: “For you two are the seasonal [priests] of the sacrifice and of consciousness, O Indra and Agni;

14.30.2.b.m: Be satisfied with the offered and unoffered, with the unoffered and offered!

14.30.2.c.m: With the offered and unoffered, with the unoffered and offered,

14.30.2.d.s: indrāgnī asya somasya vītaṃ pibataṃ juṣethāmityaṅgāre hutvā tamasmai bhakṣaṃ prayacchet
14.30.2.d.d: इन्द्राग्नी अस्य सोमस्य वीतं पिबतं जुषेथामित्यङ्गारे हुत्वा तमस्मै भक्षं प्रयच्छेत्
14.30.2.d.m: O Indra and Agni, partake of this soma, drink, enjoy!”—having offered upon the ember, he should hand that portion for partaking to him.

14.30.3.a.s: mā yajamānaṃ tamo vidanmartvijo mo imāḥ prajāḥ /
14.30.3.a.d: मा यजमानं तमो विदन्मर्त्विजो मो इमाः प्रजाः ।
14.30.3.a.m: “Let not darkness reach the sacrificer, nor the priests, nor these offspring;

14.30.3.b.s: mā yaḥ somamimaṃ pibātsaṃsṛṣṭamubhayaṃ kṛtamiti bhakṣayati
14.30.3.b.d: मा यः सोममिमं पिबात्संसृष्टमुभयं कृतमिति भक्षयति
14.30.3.b.m: Let not him who drinks this soma, mixed and made into both [suffer]!”—with this [formula] he partakes.

14.30.4.a.s: mā no dhvāriṣuḥ pitaro mota vīrā mā naḥ sabandhuruta vānyabandhuḥ /
14.30.4.a.d: मा नो ध्वारिषुः पितरो मोत वीरा मा नः सबन्धुरुत वान्यबन्धुः ।
14.30.4.a.m: “Let not the fathers injure us, nor the heroes, nor our kinsman, nor one who is no kin;

14.30.4.b.s: mā no duścakṣā aghaśaṃsa īśatāhuto 'yaṃ yajñamapyetu devāniti bhakṣayantamabhimantrayate
14.30.4.b.d: मा नो दुश्चक्षा अघशंस ईशताहुतो ऽयं यज्ञमप्येतु देवानिति भक्षयन्तमभिमन्त्रयते
