14.30.4.b.m: Let not an evil-eyed speaker of wickedness have power! May this unoffered [soma] attain the sacrifice, the gods!”—with this [formula] he consecrates the one partaking.

14.30.5.a.s: saptartvijaḥ sapta sadāṃsyeṣāṃ daśa kṣipo aśvinā pañca vājāḥ /
14.30.5.a.d: सप्तर्त्विजः सप्त सदांस्येषां दश क्षिपो अश्विना पञ्च वाजाः ।
14.30.5.a.m: “Seven are the priests, seven are their halls, ten the fingers, the two Aśvins, five the strengths;

14.30.5.b.s: prāṇo vyāno 'pāno mana ākūtamagniḥ svāhākṛtaṃ haviradantu devā iti bhakṣaṃ vyāpannamabhimantryedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama iti dakṣiṇapūrva uparave 'vanayet
14.30.5.b.d: प्राणो व्यानो ऽपानो मन आकूतमग्निः स्वाहाकृतं हविरदन्तु देवा इति भक्षं व्यापन्नमभिमन्त्र्येदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इति दक्षिणपूर्व उपरवे ऽवनयेत्
14.30.5.b.m: Prāṇa, vyāna, apāna, mind, intention, Agni: let the gods eat the oblation made with Svāhā!”—having addressed a spoiled portion for partaking with this [formula], he should pour it into the southeastern uparava with: “This Viṣṇu strode…”

14.30.7.a.s: yaḥ somavāmī syāttasmā etaṃ somendraṃ śyāmākaṃ caruṃ nirvapet
14.30.7.a.d: यः सोमवामी स्यात्तस्मा एतं सोमेन्द्रं श्यामाकं चरुं निर्वपेत्
14.30.7.a.m: For one who vomits soma, he should offer this śyāmāka caru to Somā-Indra.

14.31.1.a.s: yadi sadohavirdhānāni kṛṣṇaśakuniruparyuparyatipatetpakṣābhyāmādhūnvāna ivābhiniṣīdedvedaṃ viṣṇurvicakrama ityāhutiṃ juhuyāt /
14.31.1.a.d: यदि सदोहविर्धानानि कृष्णशकुनिरुपर्युपर्यतिपतेत्पक्षाभ्यामाधून्वान इवाभिनिषीदेद्वेदं विष्णुर्विचक्रम इत्याहुतिं जुहुयात् ।
14.31.1.a.m: If a black bird should fly right over the sadas or the havirdhāna [sheds], or settle down as if flapping its wings, he should offer an oblation with: “This Viṣṇu strode…”

14.31.1.b.m: If it should fly high above, he should pay no regard to it.

14.31.2.a.s: yadyano ratho vāntarāgnī sadohavirdhāne vā vīyātpāthikṛtīṃ pūrvavannirvapet
14.31.2.a.d: यद्यनो रथो वान्तराग्नी सदोहविर्धाने वा वीयात्पाथिकृतीं पूर्ववन्निर्वपेत्
14.31.2.a.m: If a cart or a chariot should pass between the two fires, or between the sadas and the havirdhāna [sheds], he should offer the oblation to Pathikṛt as before.

14.31.3.a.s: yadi havirdhānaṃ padyetodastāmpsītsavitā mitro aryamā sarvānamitrānavadhīdyugena /
14.31.3.a.d: यदि हविर्धानं पद्येतोदस्ताम्प्सीत्सविता मित्रो अर्यमा सर्वानमित्रानवधीद्युगेन ।
14.31.3.a.m: If the havirdhāna [shed] should collapse, with: “Savitṛ, Mitra, Aryaman have raised it up; he has slain all enemies with the yoke;

14.31.3.b.s: bṛhantaṃ māmakaradvīravantaṃ rathaṃtare śrayasva svāhetyāhavanīye juhuyāt
14.31.3.b.d: बृहन्तं मामकरद्वीरवन्तं रथंतरे श्रयस्व स्वाहेत्याहवनीये जुहुयात्
14.31.3.b.m: He has made me great, possessing heroes; rest in the Rathantara, svāhā!”—he should make an offering in the āhavanīya.

14.31.4.a.s: etenaiva pṛthivyāṃ vāmadevye śrayasva svāheti hotrīye yadi sadaḥ
14.31.4.a.d: एतेनैव पृथिव्यां वामदेव्ये श्रयस्व स्वाहेति होत्रीये यदि सदः
14.31.4.a.m: If [it is] the sadas, [he offers] in the hotṛ’s hearth with the very same [formula, substituting]: “Upon the earth, rest in the Vāmadevya, svāhā!”

14.31.5.a.m: If [it is] the āgnīdhra [shed], [he offers] in the āgnīdhra fire with: “In the atmosphere, rest in the Bṛhat, svāhā!”

14.31.6.a.m: If [it is] the prāgvaṃśa [hall], he should offer in the śālāmukhīya fire with all [the formulas].

14.31.7.a.m: The propping up of all [the sheds] is common [to each], with: “I prop you up in heaven with the Bṛhat!”

14.31.8.a.s: yadyenamārtvijyādvṛtaṃ santaṃ narharerannāgnīdhre juhuyādanu mā sarvo yajño 'yametu viśve devā marutaḥ sāmārkaḥ /
14.31.8.a.d: यद्येनमार्त्विज्याद्वृतं सन्तं नर्हरेरन्नाग्नीध्रे जुहुयादनु मा सर्वो यज्ञो ऽयमेतु विश्वे देवा मरुतः सामार्कः ।
14.31.8.a.m: If they should not bring [food] to him when he has been chosen for the office of priest, he should offer in the āgnīdhra fire with: “May this entire sacrifice follow me, the All-gods, the Maruts, the Sāman, the Arka;

14.31.8.b.m: The Āprī verses, the metres, the nivids, the yajuses, whatever belongs to sacrifice on this earth!”

14.31.9.a.m: Having partaken of soma at another’s sacrifice, he should offer an oblation of ghee in the āhavanīya for the fires, around the partaking:

14.32.1.a.s: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāmāgneḥ priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāhā /
14.32.1.a.d: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धामाग्नेः प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहा ।
14.32.1.a.m: “You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of Agni, svāhā!

14.32.1.b.s: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāmendrasya priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāhā /
14.32.1.b.d: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धामेन्द्रस्य प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहा ।
14.32.1.b.m: You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of Indra, svāhā!

14.32.1.c.s: apāṃ puṣpamasyoṣadhīnāṃ rasaḥ somasya priyaṃ dhāma viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ priyatamaṃ haviḥ svāheti
14.32.1.c.d: अपां पुष्पमस्योषधीनां रसः सोमस्य प्रियं धाम विश्वेषां देवानां प्रियतमं हविः स्वाहेति
14.32.1.c.m: You are the flower of the waters, the sap of the plants, the dear abode of Soma, the dearest oblation of the All-gods, svāhā!”

14.32.2.a.s: vayaṃ soma vrate tava manastanūṣu piprataḥ /
14.32.2.a.d: वयं सोम व्रते तव मनस्तनूषु पिप्रतः ।
14.32.2.a.m: “We, O Soma, in your observance, filling our minds in our bodies,

14.32.2.b.s: prajāvanto aśīmahīti śeṣaṃ bhakṣayitvā devebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāhā somyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāhā kavyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ svāheti dakṣiṇāgnau pratimantraṃ juhoti
14.32.2.b.d: प्रजावन्तो अशीमहीति शेषं भक्षयित्वा देवेभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहा सोम्येभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहा कव्येभ्यः पितृभ्यः स्वाहेति दक्षिणाग्नौ प्रतिमन्त्रं जुहोति
14.32.2.b.m: May we attain [life] rich in offspring!”—having partaken of the remainder, he offers into the dakṣiṇāgni, verse by verse, with: “To the divine fathers, svāhā! To the soma-loving fathers, svāhā! To the kavya-eating fathers, svāhā!”

14.32.3.a.s: taṃ jaghanena dakṣiṇāprāgagrāndarbhānsaṃstīrya dadhi dadāti devāsa iha mādayadhvaṃ somyāsa iha mādayadhvaṃ kavyāsa iha mādayadhvamiti
14.32.3.a.d: तं जघनेन दक्षिणाप्रागग्रान्दर्भान्संस्तीर्य दधि ददाति देवास इह मादयध्वं सोम्यास इह मादयध्वं कव्यास इह मादयध्वमिति
14.32.3.a.m: Having strewn darbha grass behind it with its points to the south and east, he gives curds with: “O divine ones, exhilarate yourselves here! O soma-loving ones, exhilarate yourselves here! O kavya-eating ones, exhilarate yourselves here!”

14.32.4.a.m: He reverences [it] with: “The soma-loving fathers have not been excluded from drinking the soma!”

14.32.5.a.s: bhaye jāte 'śakye yaṣṭuṃ sarvebhyo havirbhyaḥ somebhyaśca droṇakalaśe samavadhāya ye devā yeṣāmidaṃ bhāgadheyaṃ babhūva yeṣāṃ prayājā utānūyājāḥ /
14.32.5.a.d: भये जाते ऽशक्ये यष्टुं सर्वेभ्यो हविर्भ्यः सोमेभ्यश्च द्रोणकलशे समवधाय ये देवा येषामिदं भागधेयं बभूव येषां प्रयाजा उतानूयाजाः ।
14.32.5.a.m: If fear arises so that it is impossible to sacrifice, having placed [portions] from all the oblations and the somas together into the droṇakalaśa, with: “Which gods, whose share this has become, whose are the fore-offerings and the after-offerings,

14.32.5.b.s: indrajyeṣṭhebhyo varuṇarājabhyo 'gnihotṛbhyo devebhyaḥ svāheti droṇakalaśena hutvābhaye punaryajeta
14.32.5.b.d: इन्द्रज्येष्ठेभ्यो वरुणराजभ्यो ऽग्निहोतृभ्यो देवेभ्यः स्वाहेति द्रोणकलशेन हुत्वाभये पुनर्यजेत
14.32.5.b.m: To the gods whose chief is Indra, whose king is Varuṇa, who have Agni as hotṛ, svāhā!”—having offered with the droṇakalaśa, he should sacrifice again when fear has passed.

14.32.6.a.m: If a half-verse should be omitted, or if he should give a response over [another’s recitation], [he offers with]: “You, O Agni, [deliver us]…”;

14.32.6.d.m: “O Prajāpati…”—he should offer these four oblations,

14.32.7.a.s: yadyṛkto yajñaṃ bhreṣa āgacchedbhūriti gārhapatye juhuyāt /
14.32.7.a.d: यद्यृक्तो यज्ञं भ्रेष आगच्छेद्भूरिति गार्हपत्ये जुहुयात् ।
14.32.7.a.m: If a fault should come to the sacrifice through an ṛc, he should offer in the gārhapatya with: “Bhūḥ!”

14.32.7.b.m: If through a yajus, in the dakṣiṇāgni with: “Bhuvaḥ!”

14.32.7.c.m: If through a sāman, in the āhavanīya with: “Suvaḥ!”

14.32.7.d.m: If through all of them, he should offer them all.

14.33.1.a.m: Or the brahman should sit, meditating in his mind.

14.33.2.a.s: yadyaudumbarī naśyedanyāṃ pracchidyorgasyarjaṃ mayi dhehi śriyāṃ tiṣṭha pratiṣṭhitā /
14.33.2.a.d: यद्यौदुम्बरी नश्येदन्यां प्रच्छिद्योर्गस्यर्जं मयि धेहि श्रियां तिष्ठ प्रतिष्ठिता ।
14.33.2.a.m: If the post of udumbara wood should be ruined, having cut another, with: “You are vigor, place vigor in me; stand established in glory!

14.33.2.b.s: divaṃ stabdhvāntarikṣaṃ ca pṛthivyāṃ ca dṛḍhā bhava /
14.33.2.b.d: दिवं स्तब्ध्वान्तरिक्षं च पृथिव्यां च दृढा भव ।
14.33.2.b.m: Having propped up the sky and the atmosphere, be firm on the earth!

14.33.2.c.m: Upholder, supporter, mother, restrainer!”—the adhvaryu, the udgātṛ, and the sacrificer erect it.

14.33.3.a.m: When it is measured, he touches it with the regular yajus formula.

14.33.4.a.m: If the two havirdhāna carts should fall down, the adhvaryu should lift up the southern one, and the pratiprasthātṛ should prop it up;

14.33.4.b.m: the pratiprasthātṛ should lift up the northern one, and the adhvaryu should prop it up.

14.33.5.a.m: They two prop them up with a verse to Viṣṇu.

14.33.6.a.m: With the three [verses beginning]: “O Agni, of strength rich in cows…”:

14.33.6.b.s: bhadro no agnirāhuto bhadrā rātiḥ subhaga bhadro adhvaraḥ /
14.33.6.b.d: भद्रो नो अग्निराहुतो भद्रा रातिः सुभग भद्रो अध्वरः ।
14.33.6.b.m: “Auspicious for us is Agni when invoked, auspicious the gift, O fortunate one, auspicious the sacrifice,

14.33.6.d.s: bhadrā uta praśastayo bhadraṃ manaḥ kṛṇuṣva vṛtratūrye /
14.33.6.d.d: भद्रा उत प्रशस्तयो भद्रं मनः कृणुष्व वृत्रतूर्ये ।
14.33.6.d.m: And auspicious the praises, make our mind auspicious in the slaying of Vṛtra,

14.33.6.e.m: With which you may conquer in battles, cast down the firm [defenses] of the many who are insolent;

14.33.6.f.s: yenā samatsu sāsaho 'va sthirā tanuhi bhūri śardhatām /
14.33.6.f.d: येना समत्सु सासहो ऽव स्थिरा तनुहि भूरि शर्धताम् ।

14.33.6.g.m: May we win through your assistances!”—with these six uṣṇih-kakubh verses they two offer into the āgnīdhra fire.

14.33.7.a.m: The adhvaryu [offers] with the first uṣṇih verses.

14.33.7.b.m: The pratiprasthātṛ [offers] with the subsequent kakubh verses.

14.33.8.a.m: “May the head of the sacrifice be put back, immortal, consisting of the deities.

14.33.8.b.s: vaiṣṇavyā kriyatāṃ śira āśvinyā pratidhīyatāmiti pañcagṛhītena samānau homau juhutaḥ
14.33.8.b.d: वैष्णव्या क्रियतां शिर आश्विन्या प्रतिधीयतामिति पञ्चगृहीतेन समानौ होमौ जुहुतः
14.33.8.b.m: May the head be made with the [mantra] to Viṣṇu, may it be put back with the [mantra] to the Aśvins”—with [ghee] taken five times, both make identical offerings.

14.33.9.a.m: If the clay pan for the fire should break while raw, he should grind it together and make it anew.

14.33.10.a.s: yadi pakvā saṃpiṣyānayayā mṛdā saṃsṛjyokhāṃ kārayet
14.33.10.a.d: यदि पक्वा संपिष्यानयया मृदा संसृज्योखां कारयेत्
14.33.10.a.m: If baked, he should crush it, mix it with other clay, and have the pan made.

14.34.1.a.m: If the fire in the pan should go out for someone, he should carry another forth from the gārhapatya.

14.34.1.c.m: “He generates him from his own womb,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

14.34.2.a.s: kṛṣṇaṃ vāsaḥ kṛṣṇā dhenuḥ kṛṣṇo vā gauḥ śatamānaṃ ca hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā
14.34.2.a.d: कृष्णं वासः कृष्णा धेनुः कृष्णो वा गौः शतमानं च हिरण्यं दक्षिणा
14.34.2.a.m: A black garment, a black milch-cow or a black bull, and a piece of gold of one hundred mānas are the sacrificial gift.

14.34.3.a.m: By that which is done on the previous day for the subsequent day, he connects the day.

14.34.4.a.s: yatpūrvasminnahanyuttarasmā ahne vasatīvarīryajñāyajñiyaṃ prati gṛhṇāti tenāharabhyāsajati /
14.34.4.a.d: यत्पूर्वस्मिन्नहन्युत्तरस्मा अह्ने वसतीवरीर्यज्ञायज्ञियं प्रति गृह्णाति तेनाहरभ्यासजति ।
14.34.4.a.m: When on the previous day he receives the vasatīvarī waters for the subsequent day at the time of the Yajñāyajñīya [sāman], he connects the day thereby;

14.34.4.c.m: When on the previous day he orders the milks for the subsequent day, he connects the day thereby;

14.34.4.e.m: When he makes an anticipatory ritual call, he connects the day thereby;

14.34.5.a.s: eteṣāmekasminnapyakriyamāṇe namo brahmaṇe namo astvagnaye namaḥ pṛthivyai nama oṣadhībhyaḥ /
14.34.5.a.d: एतेषामेकस्मिन्नप्यक्रियमाणे नमो ब्रह्मणे नमो अस्त्वग्नये नमः पृथिव्यै नम ओषधीभ्यः ।
14.34.5.a.m: If even one of these is not performed, having offered the oblation with: “Homage to the Brahman! Homage be to Agni! Homage to the earth! Homage to the plants!

14.34.5.b.s: namo vāce namo vācaspataye namo viṣṇave bṛhate karomi svāhetyāhutiṃ hutvā sarvaprāyaścittaṃ juhuyājjuhuyāt
14.34.5.b.d: नमो वाचे नमो वाचस्पतये नमो विष्णवे बृहते करोमि स्वाहेत्याहुतिं हुत्वा सर्वप्रायश्चित्तं जुहुयाज्जुहुयात्
14.34.5.b.m: Homage to Speech! Homage to the Lord of Speech! Homage to the great Viṣṇu I make, svāhā!”, he should offer the general expiation, he should offer [it].

15.1.1.a.s: pravargyaṃ saṃbhariṣyannamāvāsyāyāṃ paurṇamāsyāmāpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā puṇye nakṣatre tūṣṇīṃ kāṇṭakīṃ samidhamādhāya yuñjate mana iti caturgṛhītaṃ juhoti
15.1.1.a.d: प्रवर्ग्यं संभरिष्यन्नमावास्यायां पौर्णमास्यामापूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा पुण्ये नक्षत्रे तूष्णीं काण्टकीं समिधमाधाय युञ्जते मन इति चतुर्गृहीतं जुहोति
15.1.1.a.m: Intending to gather the materials for the Pravargya, on the new moon day, the full moon day, or under an auspicious constellation of the waxing fortnight, having placed a thorny kindling stick silently, he offers four ladlings [of ghee] with: “They yoke their mind...”

15.1.2.a.m: Now, if he is consecrated, he should place just a thorny kindling stick with this [mantra].

15.1.3.a.s: devasya tvā savituḥ prasava ityabhrimādāyābhrirasi nārirasītyabhimantrayate
15.1.3.a.d: देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसव इत्यभ्रिमादायाभ्रिरसि नारिरसीत्यभिमन्त्रयते
15.1.3.a.m: Having taken up the spade with: “At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ...”, he consecrates it with: “You are a spade, you are a woman.”

15.1.5.a.m: He addresses the brahman with: “Arise, O Brahmaṇaspati!”

15.1.6.d.m: They lead along a she-goat that has borne male young, and an uncastrated horse.

15.1.7.a.s: praitu brahmaṇaspatiriti prāñco 'śvaprathamā abhipravrajanti yatra mṛdaṃ khaniṣyantaḥ syuḥ
15.1.7.a.d: प्रैतु ब्रह्मणस्पतिरिति प्राञ्चो ऽश्वप्रथमा अभिप्रव्रजन्ति यत्र मृदं खनिष्यन्तः स्युः
15.1.7.a.m: With: “May Brahmaṇaspati go forth,” they proceed eastward, with the horse foremost, to where they will dig the clay.

15.1.8.a.d: अपि वास्यैते संभाराः परिश्रिते ऽभ्युदाहृता भवन्ति
15.1.8.a.m: Or else, these materials of his have already been brought near within the enclosure.

15.1.9.a.m: In front of the āhavanīya is the clay pit;

15.1.10.a.s: uttareṇa mṛtkhanaṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīrya devī dyāvāpṛthivī iti mṛtkhanamabhimantrayate /
15.1.10.a.d: उत्तरेण मृत्खनं कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्य देवी द्यावापृथिवी इति मृत्खनमभिमन्त्रयते ।
15.1.10.a.m: North of the clay pit, having spread out the black antelope skin with its neck to the east and its hairy side turned upward, he addresses the clay pit with: “O divine Heaven and Earth!”

15.1.10.b.s: ṛdhyāsamadyeti mṛtkhane 'bhriyā prahṛtya makhasya śira ityapādāya makhāya tveti harati /
15.1.10.b.d: ऋध्यासमद्येति मृत्खने ऽभ्रिया प्रहृत्य मखस्य शिर इत्यपादाय मखाय त्वेति हरति ।
15.1.10.b.m: Having struck into the clay pit with the spade with: “May I prosper today,” [and] taking [clay] with: “The head of Makha,” he carries it with: “For Makha thee!”

15.1.10.c.s: makhasya tvā śīrṣṇa iti kṛṣṇājine nivapati
15.1.10.c.d: मखस्य त्वा शीर्ष्ण इति कृष्णाजिने निवपति
15.1.10.c.m: He pours it out onto the black antelope skin with: “For the head of Makha thee!”

15.1.11.a.m: In this manner he carries [clay] a second and a third time.

15.1.12.a.s: tūṣṇīṃ caturthaṃ yāvatīṃ vṛdaṃ pravargyapātrebhya āptāṃ manyate
15.1.12.a.d: तूष्णीं चतुर्थं यावतीं वृदं प्रवर्ग्यपात्रेभ्य आप्तां मन्यते
15.1.12.a.m: Silently a fourth time, as much clay as he deems sufficient for the Pravargya vessels.

15.2.1.a.m: [earth] torn up by a boar with: “So large wert thou formerly...”;

15.2.1.b.m: an ant-hill mound with: “O divine ants...”;

15.2.1.c.s: indrasyaujo 'sīti pūtīkānajalomāni kṛṣṇājinalomāni ca saṃsṛjyāgnijā asi prajāpate reta iti
15.2.1.c.d: इन्द्रस्यौजो ऽसीति पूतीकानजलोमानि कृष्णाजिनलोमानि च संसृज्याग्निजा असि प्रजापते रेत इति
15.2.1.c.m: with: “Thou art Indra's might,” pūtīka plants; and having mixed goat's hair and black antelope hairs, with: “Born of fire art thou, the seed of Prajāpati.”

15.2.2.a.s: āyurdhehi prāṇaṃ dhehītyaśvenāvaghrāpya madhu tvā madhulā karotvityajayābhidohayati
15.2.2.a.d: आयुर्धेहि प्राणं धेहीत्यश्वेनावघ्राप्य मधु त्वा मधुला करोत्वित्यजयाभिदोहयति
15.2.2.a.m: Having made the horse sniff it with: “Bestow life, bestow breath,” he causes it to be milked over by a she-goat with: “May the honey-sweet one make thee sweet.”

15.2.3.a.m: Some teach that the milking over precedes the sniffing.

15.2.4.a.m: Several Āryas take hold of it and carry it.

15.2.5.a.d: उत्तरेण विहारमुद्धते ऽवोक्षिते सिकतोपाप्ते परिश्रिते निदधति
15.2.5.a.m: North of the sacrificial enclosure, on a raised, sprinkled, sand-covered, enclosed [ground], they set it down.

15.2.6.a.m: He pours on hot water with: “May the honey-sweet one make thee sweet.”

15.2.7.a.s: ye cokhāsaṃsarjanāḥ saṃbhārā yaccānyaddṛḍhārtha upārdhaṃ manyate
15.2.7.a.d: ये चोखासंसर्जनाः संभारा यच्चान्यद्दृढार्थ उपार्धं मन्यते
15.2.7.a.m: And whatever materials belong to the mixing of the pan, and whatever else he considers suitable for the purpose of strengthening.

15.2.9.a.m: Whatever action involving water is done in the Pravargya, that is done only with hot water.

15.2.9.b.m: Neither a woman nor a Śūdra looks upon it.

15.2.10.a.m: While making it, he does not breathe over it.

15.2.11.a.m: Turning his face away, not breathing over it, he fashions it with a bamboo [knife].

15.2.12.a.m: One should not pass between the Pravargya and the sun.

15.2.13.a.s: yatra kvaca viprakrānte pravargya ādityo 'stamiyāt kṛtāntādeva viramet /
15.2.13.a.d: यत्र क्वच विप्रक्रान्ते प्रवर्ग्य आदित्यो ऽस्तमियात् कृतान्तादेव विरमेत् ।
15.2.13.a.m: Wherever the sun should set when the Pravargya has been commenced, he should stop right at a finished stage;

15.2.13.b.m: on the next day he should complete the remainder.

15.2.14.a.s: saṃprakliśya mṛdaṃ makhasya śiro 'sīti piṇḍaṃ kṛtvā yajñasya pade stha ityaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ nigṛhya mahāvīraṃ karoti tryuddhitaṃ pañcoddhimaparimitoddhiṃ vā prādeśamātramūrdhvasānumupariṣṭādāsecanavantaṃ madhye saṃnataṃ vāyavyaprakāram
15.2.14.a.d: संप्रक्लिश्य मृदं मखस्य शिरो ऽसीति पिण्डं कृत्वा यज्ञस्य पदे स्थ इत्यङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां निगृह्य महावीरं करोति त्र्युद्धितं पञ्चोद्धिमपरिमितोद्धिं वा प्रादेशमात्रमूर्ध्वसानुमुपरिष्टादासेचनवन्तं मध्ये संनतं वायव्यप्रकारम्
15.2.14.a.m: Having thoroughly kneaded the clay, made a lump with: “Thou art the head of Makha,” and held it with both thumbs with: “Ye are in the step of the sacrifice,” he makes the Mahāvīra pot with three elevations, or with five elevations, or with an indefinite number of elevations, one span high, with a raised collar, having a pouring lip at the top, narrowed in the middle, in the shape of a Vāyu vessel.

15.3.1.a.m: [He fashions] the first [third] with: “I make thee with the gāyatrī metre”;

15.3.3.a.m: With: "Thou art the collar of Makha," he makes the collar around the rim.

15.3.4.a.s: aditiste bilaṃ gṛhṇātviti veṇuparvaṇā bilaṃ karoti
15.3.4.a.d: अदितिस्ते बिलं गृह्णात्विति वेणुपर्वणा बिलं करोति
15.3.4.a.m: With: "May Aditi seize thy cavity," he makes the cavity by means of a bamboo joint.

15.3.5.a.m: He carries it beyond the third mark.

15.3.6.a.m: "As much as he thinks sufficient for the divinity, for the sviṣṭakṛt, for the agnihotra, and for the consuming"—this is another [view].

15.3.7.a.s: sūryasya harasā śrāyetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya makho 'sītyanuvīkṣate
15.3.7.a.d: सूर्यस्य हरसा श्रायेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य मखो ऽसीत्यनुवीक्षते
15.3.7.a.m: Having placed it upon the sands to the north with: "Be cooked by the heat of the sun," he gazes after it with: "Thou art Makha."

15.3.8.a.m: Thus he makes the second and the third.

15.3.10.a.s: etasyā eva mṛdo dogdhre karoti hastyoṣṭhye prasecanavatī yathā srugadaṇḍaivam
15.3.10.a.d: एतस्या एव मृदो दोग्ध्रे करोति हस्त्योष्ठ्ये प्रसेचनवती यथा स्रुगदण्डैवम्
15.3.10.a.m: Out of this very clay he makes two milking vessels, with handles and lips, having spouts, like ladles without handles.

15.3.11.a.m: The one belonging to the adhvaryu is larger than the one belonging to the pratiprasthātṛ.

15.3.12.a.m: [He makes] the clarified butter-pot, and two circular potsherds for the rauhiṇa [cake] in the shape of a horse's hoof.

15.3.13.a.m: The gharma-brick and the kulāyinī [brick], if [the sacrifice] is accompanied by the piling of the fire-altar.

15.3.14.a.m: "They should not exist where there is no pravargya"—this is another [view].

15.3.16.a.m: with unwashed caṇḍātaka garments, with gavīdhukā grains, with klītaka roots, with bamboo joints, [and] with clarified butter.

15.3.17.a.s: vṛṣṇo 'śvasya śakṛdgārhapatye pradīpya prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhya dhūpayati vṛṣṇo aśvasya niṣpadasīti
15.3.17.a.d: वृष्णो ऽश्वस्य शकृद्गार्हपत्ये प्रदीप्य प्रथमकृतं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्य धूपयति वृष्णो अश्वस्य निष्पदसीति
15.3.17.a.m: Having kindled the dung of a stallion in the gārhapatya fire, having seized the first-made mahāvīra with two tongs, he fumigates it with: "Thou art the stepping out of the stallion."

15.3.18.a.m: Thus he fumigates the second and the third.

15.3.19.a.m: From then on, he handles the mahāvīras only with the two tongs.

15.3.20.a.s: agreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhārairavastīrya teṣu mahāvīrānupāvaharati
15.3.20.a.d: अग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैरवस्तीर्य तेषु महावीरानुपावहरति
15.3.20.a.m: Having dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya, having strewn it with materials for baking red, he deposits the mahāvīras in them.

15.4.1.c.m: With: "Thou art the light; thou art the heat," the third.

15.4.2.a.s: tūṣṇīmitarāṇyanvavadhāya lohitapacanīyaiḥ saṃbhāraiḥ pracchādya gārhapatye muñjānādīpyopoṣatyarciṣe tvetyetaiḥ pratimantraṃ pratidiśam
15.4.2.a.d: तूष्णीमितराण्यन्ववधाय लोहितपचनीयैः संभारैः प्रच्छाद्य गार्हपत्ये मुञ्जानादीप्योपोषत्यर्चिषे त्वेत्येतैः प्रतिमन्त्रं प्रतिदिशम्
15.4.2.a.m: Having deposited the other [vessels] silently, having covered [them] with the materials for baking red, having kindled muñja grass in the gārhapatya, he sets [them] on fire in each direction, formula by formula, with these [words]: "To the flame thee..."

15.4.3.a.m: Or on all sides with all [formulas].

15.4.4.a.m: While they are being baked, he attends upon them with the verse addressed to Mitra: "This one with greatness heaven..."

15.4.6.a.s: pakveṣu siddhyai tveti dhṛṣṭī ādāya bhasmāpohya prathamakṛtaṃ mahāvīraṃ śaphābhyāṃ parigṛhyodvāsayati
15.4.6.a.d: पक्वेषु सिद्ध्यै त्वेति धृष्टी आदाय भस्मापोह्य प्रथमकृतं महावीरं शफाभ्यां परिगृह्योद्वासयति
15.4.6.a.m: When they are baked, having taken two fire-shovels with: "To accomplishment thee," having brushed away the ashes, and having seized the first-made mahāvīra with the two tongs, he removes it.

15.4.7.a.s: devastvā savitodvapatvityudvāsyāpadyamānaḥ pṛthivyāmāśā diśa āpṛṇetyuttarataḥ sikatāsu pratiṣṭhāpya sūryasya tvā cakṣuṣānvīkṣa ityanuvīkṣate
15.4.7.a.d: देवस्त्वा सवितोद्वपत्वित्युद्वास्यापद्यमानः पृथिव्यामाशा दिश आपृणेत्युत्तरतः सिकतासु प्रतिष्ठाप्य सूर्यस्य त्वा चक्षुषान्वीक्ष इत्यनुवीक्षते
15.4.7.a.m: Having removed it with: "May god Savitṛ remove thee," having set it down upon the sands to the north with: "Falling down on the earth, fill the quarters and directions," he gazes after it with: "With the eye of the sun I gaze after thee."

15.4.8.a.m: Thus he removes the second and the third.

15.4.9.a.s: athainānpradakṣiṇaṃ sikatābhiḥ paryūhatīdamahamamumāmuṣyāyaṇaṃ viśā paśubhirbrahmavarcasena paryūhāmīti /
15.4.9.a.d: अथैनान्प्रदक्षिणं सिकताभिः पर्यूहतीदमहममुमामुष्यायणं विशा पशुभिर्ब्रह्मवर्चसेन पर्यूहामीति ।
15.4.9.a.m: Then he heaps sands clockwise around them with: "Here I enclose NN, descendant of NN, with the people, with cattle, with spiritual lustre."

15.4.9.c.m: "With cattle," in the case of a vaiśya.

15.4.10.a.m: Then he drenches them with abundant goat's milk.

15.4.10.b.m: With: "With the gāyatrī meter I drench thee," [and so forth], each one with these three [formulas], three by three.

15.4.12.a.m: Then, having tied them up in a black antelope skin, he suspends them with: "O god, going in front, may I endure thee."

15.4.13.a.m: "This formula belongs to a later time"—this is another [view].

15.5.1.a.m: When about to perform the pravargya, they close the doors.

15.5.3.c.m: To the south the brahman, the sacrificer, and the prastotṛ.

15.5.3.d.m: To the north the pratiprasthātṛ and the agnīdhra.

15.5.4.a.s: madantīrupaspṛśya prathamenānuvākena śāntiṃ kṛtvāgreṇa gārhapatyaṃ darbhānsaṃstīrya teṣu mahāvīrānupāvaharati deva puraścara saghyāsaṃ tveti
15.5.4.a.d: मदन्तीरुपस्पृश्य प्रथमेनानुवाकेन शान्तिं कृत्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यं दर्भान्संस्तीर्य तेषु महावीरानुपावहरति देव पुरश्चर सघ्यासं त्वेति
15.5.4.a.m: Having touched the madantī waters, having performed the appeasement rite with the first section, having strewn darbha grass in front of the gārhapatya, he deposits the mahāvīras on them with: "O god, going in front, may I endure thee."

15.5.5.a.m: "This formula belongs to a later time"—this is another [view].

15.5.6.a.m: Here itself are all the utensils belonging to the gharma.

15.5.7.c.m: Some teach [it to be] taller than the king's chair.

15.5.7.d.m: Woven with single-strand cords of muñja grass.

15.5.10.a.m: Between the two with handles, the larger [is] the under-holding ladle for the sprinkling-water vessel.

15.5.11.a.s: sruvau śaphau mahāvīrasaṃmitāvraskyau dhṛṣṭī methīṃ mayūkhānṣaṭ śakalānkāṇṭakīṃ ca samidhaṃ trayodaśa vaikaṅkatānparidhīnvaikaṅkatāni gharmendhanāni /
15.5.11.a.d: स्रुवौ शफौ महावीरसंमिताव्रस्क्यौ धृष्टी मेथीं मयूखान्षट् शकलान्काण्टकीं च समिधं त्रयोदश वैकङ्कतान्परिधीन्वैकङ्कतानि घर्मेन्धनानि ।
15.5.11.a.m: Two dipping spoons; two pairs of tongs; two cutting knives matching the mahāvīra pots; two fire-pokers; a peg; six pegs; splinters; a thorny fuel-stick; thirteen enclosing sticks of vikankata wood; [and] fuel-sticks of vikankata wood for the gharma.

15.5.11.b.s: khādirāṇi pālāśānyaudumbarāṇyarkamayāṇi kārṣmaryamayāṇi vaiṇavāni śamīmayāni vā
15.5.11.b.d: खादिराणि पालाशान्यौदुम्बराण्यर्कमयाणि कार्ष्मर्यमयाणि वैणवानि शमीमयानि वा
15.5.11.b.m: Or [they are] of khadira wood, of palāśa wood, of udumbara wood, of arka wood, of kākṣmarya wood, of bamboo, or of śamī wood.

15.5.12.a.m: Three fans made of black-antelope skin, with white and black hair.

15.5.13.a.s: teṣāṃ vaiṇavā daṇḍā bāhumātrā bhavantīti vijñāyate
15.5.13.a.d: तेषां वैणवा दण्डा बाहुमात्रा भवन्तीति विज्ञायते
15.5.13.a.m: Their handles are of bamboo, one cubit in length—so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

15.5.14.a.m: Having handles of udumbara wood, says another [view].

15.5.15.a.m: Two gold plates, [one of] silver and [one of] gold.

15.5.19.a.m: One of the two is trimmed around.

15.5.20.a.m: A halter; two hobble cords; three branching tethers; [and] abundant tufts of muñja grass.

15.5.20.b.m: Flour of unhusked [grains] for the two rauhiṇa cakes.

15.5.21.a.m: Having prepared the sprinkling waters according to the rite of sprinkling waters, he addresses the brahman:

15.6.1.a.m: "O brahman, we shall proceed with the Pravargya.

15.6.1.c.m: O agnīdh, set the two rauhiṇa cakes on [the fire].

15.6.2.a.m: Having murmured, "Yoked by the yajus, anointed with sāmans, the space [is made]," [the brahman] loudly authorizes with: "Om! Possessed of Indra, proceed!"

15.6.4.a.s: yamāya tvā makhāya tveti sarvaṃ parigharmyamabhipūrvaṃ triḥ prokṣati
15.6.4.a.d: यमाय त्वा मखाय त्वेति सर्वं परिघर्म्यमभिपूर्वं त्रिः प्रोक्षति
15.6.4.a.m: With: "For Yama, you! For Makha, you!" he sprinkles everything belonging to the gharma three times in succession.

15.6.5.a.m: He sets apart the sprinkled items.

15.6.6.a.m: The āgnīdhra puts the two rauhiṇa cakes on [the fire], served silently.

15.6.7.a.m: At this time the pratiprasthātṛ prepares the ghee according to the preparation of a ladle-offering.
